docs.title: Vergil Actions
docs.text: Shared GitHub Actions library providing reusable composite actions for CI/CD across all managed repositories.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Stable (v2.x) — Actions and reusable workflows are consumed by pinning to a rolling minor tag (e.g., @v2.1), which automatically receives patch releases.

docs.title: Action categories
docs.text: Phase Actions Purpose CI / Security codeql, semgrep SAST scanning CI / Version Bump version-divergence Pre-merge version validation CI / Matrix matrix Per-version job matrix and container images CI / Toolchain pin-python, install-python, assert Pin uv to a leg's Python interpreter; install a Python leg's dev dependencies, skipped on a repo not bootstrapped yet; fail a leg whose running toolchain is not the resolved version CI / Evidence emit, reports Per-gate CI evidence artifact; per-language test and audit report contract, and staging of each leg's reports CD / Release tag-and-release Release tagging and GitHub Releases CD / Release validate-inputs, ci-evidence-gate, registry-publish, ci-evidence-attach cd-release input checks, pre-publish evidence gate, build and registry publish, post-publish evidence attach CD / Docs deploy MkDocs Material + mike versioned deployment Ops / GitHub Config branch-sweep Delete branches whose PR is merged or closed Shared / Security trivy Vulnerability scanning and SBOM generation Shared / Docs stage Stage changelog and release-notes pages for the docs build Shared / Setup vergil, system-packages, build-command vergil-tooling install and CI version set; test-job system packages and build command Package setup Package toolchain image check and vergil-tooling install for package build and install-test containers Local freeze-internal-refs Pin this repository's internal action refs to the release tag (used only by its own cd.yml)

docs.title: Reusable workflows
docs.text: Reusable workflows provide canonical job and check names across all managed repositories. See Reusable Workflows for details.

docs.title: CI (pre-merge)
docs.text: Workflow Purpose ci-docs Strict MkDocs build of the documentation site ci-security Security scanning (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) ci-quality Common linting, custom validation, language-specific lint and typecheck ci-audit Dependency audit ci-test Unit tests ci-version-bump Version divergence gate ci-package Build and install-test .deb/.rpm packages (repos with [package] only)

docs.title: CD (post-merge)
docs.text: Workflow Purpose cd-release Full release pipeline (tag, build, publish, version bump), plus signed .deb/.rpm packages for repos with [package] cd-docs MkDocs documentation deployment cd-docs-refresh Regenerate a docs site's generated pages (roadmap, activity) and redeploy it; the caller runs it on a schedule and on demand publish-index Signed apt/dnf package-repository site for an <org>/packages repo, deployed to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• Composite actions only — No custom JavaScript or Docker actions. Every action is a composite action.yml with shell steps.
  • Reusable workflows — CI and CD workflows are provided as reusable workflow_call templates that produce canonical check names across all consuming repositories.
  • Self-referencing CI — This repository's own CI uses ./actions/... and ./.github/workflows/... local paths, so changes are tested by the same PR that modifies them.
  • Centralized standards — Workflow patterns and validation rules are defined once here and consumed by all repositories.

docs.title: Canonical standards
docs.text: This repository follows the vergil-tooling repository for commit messages, branching, versioning, and code management practices.

docs.title: Repository Configuration
docs.text: This page documents the GitHub configuration prerequisites that each managed repository needs before CI workflows and automation work correctly. For action-specific configuration (inputs, outputs, behavior), see the Action Reference.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Each repository requires specific secrets depending on its workflow set. APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY live in each repository's automation environment (Settings > Environments > automation), and are set per repository. There is no org-level or repository-level copy of either: a copy at either level would reach a job on any branch, which the environment exists to prevent (see The automation environment).

Secret Where it is set Required by Purpose APP_CLIENT_ID The repository's automation environment Every repository with an ops.yml or epic-rollup.yml, and every repository that releases through cd-release.yml Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (<org>-automation) APP_PRIVATE_KEY The repository's automation environment Every repository with an ops.yml or epic-rollup.yml, and every repository that releases through cd-release.yml Private key of the org's automation GitHub App

Do not pipe secret values via stdin

Always use the --body flag when setting secrets with gh secret set. Piping the value via stdin (printf '%s' 'VALUE' | gh secret set ...) can corrupt the secret value during encryption, causing "Bad credentials" errors at runtime that are difficult to diagnose.

docs.title: APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY
docs.text:
These secrets hold the Client ID and private key of the org's automation GitHub App. Workflows pass them to actions/create-github-app-token to mint a short-lived installation token for work that GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do.

Each org has its own automation App, named <org>-automation. The App is owned by the org (registered under the org's Developer settings, not a personal account), and its installation covers all repositories in that org:

Org App vergil-project vergil-project-automation logical-minds-foundry logical-minds-foundry-automation mnemosys-project mnemosys-project-automation mq-rest-admin-project mq-rest-admin-project-automation

The App is an automation identity, not a per-contributor one. It is separate from the per-developer agent Apps described in vergil-tooling's Identity Architecture.

Why a GitHub App? A reusable workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN can carry only the permissions its caller grants, and the standard ops.yml grants just contents: read and issues: write. It is also limited to the repository the run belongs to. The App token supplies the extra scopes (for example Dependabot alerts or branch deletion) and the cross-repository reach (the org's .github epics, the org's packages index) these workflows need.

Who uses it. Every repository with an ops.yml needs these secrets, not only library repositories. So does every caller of cd-docs.yml or cd-docs-refresh.yml: the docs deploy pushes gh-pages with the App token on every run, on main as well as develop, and fails without the secrets, and the reporting job mints the App token on develop. A caller of publish-index.yml needs them for its reporting job on develop. These workflows declare the secrets optional, but a run that does not pass them turns the deploy or the reporting job red. Pass them as on the other App-key workflows: secrets: inherit from a caller in vergil-project, by name from a caller in another org (see The automation environment below):

Workflow Job or step Token scope ops-github-config.yml branch-sweep, github-config, dependabot-audit Calling repository only ops-github-config.yml trusted-authors-check (in <org>/.github only, skipped elsewhere) Every repository the App is installed on in the org, read-only ops-agent-audit.yml agent-audit Calling repository only ops-epic-rollup.yml epic-rollup (from the caller's epic-rollup.yml) Calling repository and the epic repository ops-epic-sweep.yml epic-sweep Every repository the App is installed on in the org ops-upstream-refresh.yml publish (vrg-upstream-refresh publish mints the token itself) Calling repository only cd-docs.yml docs (pushes gh-pages, also when nested in cd-docs-refresh.yml) Calling repository only, Contents write cd-release.yml release (pushes the release tags) Calling repository only, Contents write cd-release.yml Package-index dispatch <org>/packages only vergil-actions' own cd.yml release vergil-actions only The ops/report action The reporting job of ops-github-config.yml (report-branch-sweep), ops-epic-sweep.yml, ops-epic-rollup.yml, ops-upstream-refresh.yml, cd-docs.yml, cd-docs-refresh.yml and publish-index.yml (each report) Calling repository and <org>/.github, Issues write only

App permissions. Every org's automation App is configured identically, and this table is that configuration. Each org's App must hold exactly these permissions:

Permission Access Needed by Metadata Read-only Required by GitHub (always enabled) Administration Read & write github-config, which runs vrg-github-repo-config update: it reads and converges repository settings, branch protection, rulesets (whose bypass actors GitHub returns only to a caller that can edit them), Actions permissions and whether vulnerability alerts are enabled Contents Read & write branch-sweep (deletes branch refs); upstream-refresh (pushes the automation/upstream-refresh/<run-id> branch, and deletes an earlier run's branch when it closes that run's PR); cd-release.yml pushes the release tags and dispatches the package index to <org>/packages; cd.yml pushes the release tags; github-config pushes the sync branch, and GitHub returns a repository's merge settings only to a token with Contents read and write; epic-sweep reads each repository's vergil.toml; agent-audit moves the vergil/agent-audit/* marker refs Pull requests Read & write upstream-refresh (opens the refresh PR with auto-merge, updates its branch from develop, merges it, and closes an earlier run's open one); github-config (opens the sync PR, closes an earlier one and turns on auto-merge); branch-sweep, epic-sweep and agent-audit read them Issues Read & write ops-epic-rollup.yml and ops-epic-sweep.yml (close, reopen, relabel and link issues); the ops/report action (opens and comments on ops issues, creates the ops-report label, links issues under the operations epic); agent-audit reads PR timelines and task-issue comments Workflows Read & write cd.yml (the release tag points at the freeze-internal-refs commit, which changes workflow files: see local/freeze-internal-refs); github-config, the automatic fleet sync, whose PRs can change files under .github/workflows/; upstream-refresh, only for the wait's branch update, which merges develop into the PR branch and is refused without it whenever develop has changed a workflow file (the path fence keeps every refresh patch out of .github/**) Actions Read-only github-config, which runs vrg-github-repo-config update: it reads the automation environment and its deployment branch policies, which GitHub serves only with Actions read (creating or changing them needs Administration write) Dependabot alerts Read-only dependabot-audit (vrg-dependabot-audit lists open alerts) Variables Read-only trusted-authors-check, in the org's .github repository only (vrg-trusted-authors check lists every repository's Actions variables, for a repository-level copy of VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS or VRG_AUTOMATION_APP) Variables (organization permission) Read-only trusted-authors-check, in the org's .github repository only (vrg-trusted-authors check reads the org variables VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP)

Why the App holds no Repository security advisories permission. The App must not hold Repository security advisories at any access level. No automation job uses it: the security-records pass that syncs advisory states in the org's .github runs as the human or the user agent, through vrg-security-record sync, and vrg-epic-audit --close in the epic-sweep job makes no security-advisory call (vergil-project/vergil-tooling#4313).

Why Administration and Workflows are write. The automatic fleet sync (epic vergil-project/.github#1064) has the nightly github-config job converge each repository itself and open one auto-merging pull request for any managed file that has drifted from its master copy. The automation identity does only this mechanized work, never anything an AI agent does (that epic's spec, §3). Converging settings and rulesets needs Administration write, and a sync PR that touches a workflow file needs Workflows write. These rights are safe to hold only because every token is scoped, as Token scoping describes.

Creation steps:

  1. Go to the org's Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps, so the App is owned by the org.
  2. Click New GitHub App.
  3. Name it <org>-automation and set the homepage URL.
  4. Under Permissions > Repository permissions, grant the permissions listed above, and under Permissions > Organization permissions, grant Variables: Read-only.
  5. Disable webhooks (not needed).
  6. Create the app and note the Client ID from the app's settings page.
  7. Under Private keys, click Generate a private key. Save the downloaded .pem file.
  8. Under Install App, install it on the org and choose All repositories.

  9. In each repository that calls the workflows above, set APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY in its automation environment. The environment must already exist with its deployment branch policy: run vrg-github-repo-config update --repo <org>/<repo> first if it does not (see The automation environment). Then:

    gh secret set APP_CLIENT_ID --repo <org>/<repo> --env automation --body "<client-id>"
gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY --repo <org>/<repo> --env automation --body "$(cat <path-to-private-key>.pem)"

    Never set them at org level (--org) or as repository secrets (--repo without --env).

  10. Set the org-level Actions variable VRG_AUTOMATION_APP to the App's slug (<org>-automation), visible to all repositories. It names the automation App. The github-config job fails when it is empty, and otherwise passes it to vergil-tooling, which checks that the job's token was minted by that App before it does any automation work. It is written with VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS, from the automation_app of the org's [orgs.<org>] stanza in the host configuration, never set by hand (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS for the order):

    vrg-trusted-authors publish --org <org>

Changing a permission later:

  1. On the App's settings page, open Permissions & events, change the permission and save.
  2. Accept the change on the installation: Org settings > GitHub Apps > \ > Configure, then review and accept the pending permission request. GitHub does not apply a new App permission to an installation until it is accepted, and until then minted tokens do not carry it. For Dependabot alerts, the dependabot-audit job exits 2 ("could not check") on every repository and the ops run fails.

    Key rotation: Generate a new private key from the app's settings page, update APP_PRIVATE_KEY in the automation environment of every repository in that org (step 9's command, once per repository), then revoke the old key. A repository still holding the old key fails to mint its token once the old key is revoked. Each org has its own App and key, so rotate per org.

docs.title: The automation environment
docs.text:
Each repository has a GitHub deployment environment named automation. Its deployment branch policy admits only the custom branches develop and main (releases run on main), with no required reviewers and no wait timer, since the jobs that use it run unattended. A job running on any other branch, an agent's feature branch included, cannot use the environment, so it never sees the App's credentials.

How it is created. Do not create it by hand. vrg-github-repo-config update creates the automation environment and its branch policy in every managed repository, audit reports drift from it, and the nightly github-config job keeps it converged. The environment must exist with its policy before its secrets are set: a workflow job that names an environment the repository does not have creates it with no branch policy.

Who declares it. Every job in vergil-actions that reads APP_CLIENT_ID or APP_PRIVATE_KEY declares environment: automation, as must any repository-local job that mints an automation App token. A calling job cannot declare an environment, so the caller passes the keys on, and they reach the called workflow's jobs that declare environment: automation by either of two routes:

  • Within vergil-project, the caller passes secrets: inherit. vrg-validate's secrets-inherit check allows it only to the vergil-actions workflows that read these keys.
  • Across organizations, where secrets: inherit passes nothing, the caller passes APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY by name. A call job also passes them by name to its own repository's local reusable workflow.

Checking it. List a repository's environment secrets with gh secret list --repo <org>/<repo> --env automation: it must list both APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY. gh secret list --repo <org>/<repo> and gh secret list --org <org> must list neither.

docs.title: Token scoping
docs.text:
GitHub gives a token minted from an App every permission the App's installation holds, unless the token asks for less. Once the App holds Administration write, an unscoped token would carry it into every job. So every actions/create-github-app-token step in vergil-actions passes explicit permission-* inputs, and each job requests only what it needs:

Workflow Job or step Requested permissions ops-github-config.yml branch-sweep contents: write, pull-requests: read ops-github-config.yml github-config (from develop only) administration: write, contents: write, pull-requests: write, workflows: write, actions: read, metadata: read (update; Get a repository also returns the merge settings only with Contents read and write, and reading an environment and its deployment branch policies needs Actions read) ops-github-config.yml trusted-authors-check (in <org>/.github only, skipped elsewhere; the org's whole installation, not the calling repository) organization-actions-variables: read, actions-variables: read, metadata: read ops-github-config.yml dependabot-audit vulnerability-alerts: read ops-agent-audit.yml agent-audit (from develop only) contents: write, pull-requests: read, issues: read, metadata: read ops-epic-rollup.yml epic-rollup issues: write ops-epic-sweep.yml epic-sweep issues: write, pull-requests: read, contents: read ops-upstream-refresh.yml publish (minted in-process by vrg-upstream-refresh, from develop only) contents: write, pull-requests: write, workflows: write, metadata: read cd-release.yml release, its "Mint release tag token" step (pushes the release tags) contents: write cd-release.yml Package-index dispatch contents: write cd.yml (vergil-actions only) release contents: write, workflows: write

Metadata: Read is always included. Only one job requests Administration write: github-config, which runs update. It fails before minting its token unless the run's ref is refs/heads/develop, and checks out develop, so no other branch's code runs with that token. A repository-local workflow that mints an automation App token follows the same rule.

Upstream refresh mints its own token. ops-upstream-refresh.yml has no create-github-app-token step. Its publish job passes the App's client ID and private key to vrg-upstream-refresh publish on that one step, and the tool mints installation tokens itself, limited to the calling repository and the four permissions above. It renews the token every 30 minutes, revokes each token it replaces, and revokes the last one when it exits, on success, on failure, and on the SIGINT or SIGTERM that a cancel sends. The key is held only in publish, never in prepare, which runs the repository's hook with a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN on a runner of its own (the key boundary: see ops-upstream-refresh). Like github-config, both jobs fail unless the run's ref is refs/heads/develop. Only a hard kill skips the last revocation: the runner lost, the kill at the end of the cancel grace period, or a cancel signal that does not reach the publish step inside its container. The token is then left to expire within its hour, in the memory of a runner that never ran the hook.

A token can only narrow what the installation already holds: a step that requests a permission the installation lacks, or has not accepted yet, fails to mint and the job goes red.

Each job in ops-github-config.yml also runs in its own per-repository concurrency group, <owner>/<repo>/<job>, which queues and never cancels: a scheduled run and a dispatch of the same job never overlap. The github-config job runs gh auth setup-git with the App token before the tool runs, so the git clone and git push the tooling makes authenticate as the App with that job's scoped token.

docs.title: VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS
docs.text:
The org-level Actions variable VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS, visible to all repositories, holds the trusted-authors configuration that vergil-tooling judges GitHub content against: the human and agents logins and the automation App of every Vergil org, as compact JSON. It is derived from the human's host configuration and published by the human at org setup and whenever that configuration changes, never edited by hand.

Publishing it. On the host, the human runs:

vrg-trusted-authors publish --org <org>

It writes two org Actions variables from the host configuration, both visible to all repositories: VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, the org's own automation App slug (see step 10 of the App setup). Without --org it publishes for every org the configuration lists. It refuses an org where a repository-level variable of either name would shadow the org copy. vrg-trusted-authors render --org <org> prints the values the host configuration implies, with no GitHub call, to preview them first. The daily trusted-authors-check reads the published values back. For the host configuration itself, see vergil-tooling's account setup guide.

The order. Every job that runs a vergil-tooling release carrying the trust layer reads the variable, the release's own CI evidence gate included. publish ships in that same release, so:

  1. Add the org's [orgs.<org>] stanza, beside [trusted_authors], to the host configuration.
  2. Install that vergil-tooling release on the host.
  3. Run vrg-trusted-authors publish --org <org> right away.

A job that runs the release before the variable is published stops loudly on the missing variable; re-run it once the variable is published.

Under GitHub Actions, with no configuration file on the runner, vergil-tooling reads it from the environment and stops when it is missing or invalid. The reusable workflows pass it, as VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS: ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }}, into the env of each step that runs a vrg-* command that calls GitHub, and into the step that uses a composite action running one (a composite action cannot read vars). Only those steps get it: no workflow-level or job-level env sets it. actions/shared/setup/vergil/tests/trusted-authors-env.test.sh checks this. A repository-level variable of the same name would override the org copy in that repository's jobs, so none is set.

docs.title: Binary package environments
docs.text:
Repositories whose vergil.toml has a [package] section, and the organization's <org>/packages index repository, keep their signing key in GitHub environments (Settings > Environments), not in repository secrets. Each environment's deployment-branch policy restricts it to a single branch.

Environment Repository Admits Secrets Used by package-signing Each [package] repository main only PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE The package-sign job in cd-release.yml index-signing <org>/packages develop only PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE The build-index job in publish-index.yml

PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY holds the ASCII-armored export of the org signing subkey. index-signing admits develop because repository_dispatch and schedule runs always use the default branch.

Neither workflow declares the signing secrets. Within vergil-project the caller passes secrets: inherit, which carries them. A [package] repository outside vergil-project cannot sign its packages yet (vergil-project/.github#1592). See Release publishing secrets.

The GitHub App behind APP_CLIENT_ID / APP_PRIVATE_KEY must also be installed on <org>/packages with Contents: Read & write, so that cd-release.yml can dispatch package-released to it after a packaged release.

docs.title: Container system packages
docs.text: A repository can declare extra Ubuntu packages under [container].system-packages in its vergil.toml. On CI, the ci-test workflow installs those packages on its test jobs (via the shared/setup/system-packages action), so tests run against the same system dependencies as the local dev container. The key's schema and semantics are documented on the vergil-tooling side: container-config reference. Every image a test job runs in is built on Ubuntu 24.04, and the GitHub-hosted runners are ubuntu-24.04; vergil-containers' OS usage page lists the OS of every image and runner, and why it was chosen.

docs.title: Container build command
docs.text: A repository can declare a build step under [container].build-command in its vergil.toml. On CI, the ci-test workflow runs that command on its test jobs (via the shared/setup/build-command action, after the system-packages install and before the tests), so tests run against the same build output as the local dev container. The step fails closed with no retry — a failing build command fails the test job immediately rather than being retried. After it runs, the action exports NODE_PATH so a node library the build baked out-of-workspace resolves; note that NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require only and ignored by ESM import. The key's schema and semantics are documented on the vergil-tooling side: container-config reference.

docs.title: Repository rulesets
docs.text:
Every managed repository uses six rulesets to enforce merge requirements (a docs-single-branch repository, which has no main, has no CI gates (main)):

  • Branch protection — PR requirements for main and develop
  • CI gates (develop) — Required status checks for develop; the branch need not be up to date
  • CI gates (main) — The same required status checks for main; the branch must be up to date
  • Tag protection — Protect release tags (v*.*.*) and rolling minor tags (v*.*); only the repository Admin role and the org automation App may create, move or delete them
  • Rolling tag branch names — Block branches named like a rolling tag (v[0-9]*)
  • Automation branches — Only the org automation App and the repository Admin role may write automation/** branches

For detailed configuration including settings, check names per repository type, and API commands, see Repository Rulesets.

docs.title: Workflow permissions
docs.text: GitHub Actions workflows use the GITHUB_TOKEN for most operations. This token is automatically created per workflow run and scoped to the repository.

docs.title: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions
docs.text:
Each workflow declares its minimum required permissions at the top level:

permissions:
  contents: read
Permission Typical workflows contents: read CI (test, lint, validate) contents: write Documentation deployment, publish (tagging) security-events: write CodeQL, Semgrep, Trivy (SARIF upload) attestations: write Build provenance attestation (Python) id-token: write OIDC-based publishing (PyPI trusted publisher) pull-requests: write Publish workflow (version bump PR creation)

docs.title: When external tokens are needed
docs.text: The GITHUB_TOKEN is insufficient when a job needs scopes or repositories beyond the caller's grant: a reusable workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN carries only what the caller grants and reaches only its own repository. The org's automation App token (APP_CLIENT_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY, from the automation environment) is required for the nightly ops jobs (config update (vrg-github-repo-config update), branch sweep, Dependabot alert audit), the epic roll-up and sweep, the release tag pushes and the package-index dispatch. See APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

docs.title: Auto-merge
docs.text:
All managed repositories have auto-merge enabled in repository settings. This allows PRs to merge automatically once all required status checks pass.

To enable: Settings > General > Pull Requests > Allow auto-merge.

docs.title: New repository onboarding checklist
docs.text: Use this checklist when adding a new repository to the managed environment.

docs.title: 1. Repository settings
docs.text:
• [ ] Set default branch to develop
  • [ ] Enable auto-merge (Settings > General > Pull Requests)
  • [ ] Enable Automatically delete head branches

docs.title: 2. Rulesets
docs.text:
Do not create the rulesets by hand. vrg-github-repo-config update creates every ruleset of the standard configuration: Branch protection, CI gates (develop), CI gates (main), Tag protection, Rolling tag branch names and Automation branches. It also creates the automation environment and its deployment branch policy. The nightly github-config job runs the same command and keeps them converged from then on.

  • [ ] Run vrg-github-repo-config update --repo <org>/<repo>

docs.title: 3. Secrets
docs.text:
• [ ] After step 2 has created the automation environment, set APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY in it, as step 9 of the App setup shows
  • [ ] Confirm that neither secret is set at org or repository level
gh secret list --repo <org>/<repo> --env automation
gh secret list --repo <org>/<repo>
gh secret list --org <org>

The first command must list both APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY; the other two must list neither.

docs.title: 4. GitHub App installation
docs.text:
• [ ] Confirm the org's <org>-automation App installation has All repositories access, so it already covers the new repository (Org settings > GitHub Apps > \ > Configure). There is no per-repository install step.
  • [ ] Verify by checking Settings > GitHub Apps on the repository
  • [ ] After the first nightly ops run, confirm the dependabot-audit job did not exit 2 ("could not check")

docs.title: 4a. Binary packages ([package] repositories only)
docs.text:
See Binary package environments.

  • [ ] Create a package-signing environment whose deployment-branch policy admits only main
  • [ ] Add PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE to it
  • [ ] Call cd-release.yml with secrets: inherit. A repository outside vergil-project cannot sign its packages yet: see vergil-project/.github#1592
  • [ ] Call ci-package.yml under a job keyed package. Do not add package / evidence to the CI gates rulesets by hand: vrg-github-repo-config requires it for a repository with a [package] section

For the <org>/packages index repository itself:

  • [ ] Create an index-signing environment that admits only develop, holding PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE
  • [ ] Set Settings > Pages > Source to GitHub Actions
  • [ ] Call publish-index.yml with secrets: inherit

docs.title: 5. Workflow files
docs.text:
• [ ] Add ci.yml with standard checks for the repository type
  • [ ] Add cd.yml with docs and/or release jobs as needed

docs.title: 6. CI gates activation
docs.text:
• [ ] Push the CI workflow and verify all checks run
  • [ ] Confirm the CI gates (develop) and CI gates (main) rulesets require them. Do not add a check by hand: vrg-github-repo-config derives the required-check set and the nightly update converges the rulesets (procedure)

docs.title: 7. Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] Open a test PR and confirm all required checks run
  • [ ] Confirm auto-merge works after checks pass

docs.title: Consuming actions
docs.text:
Reference actions from this repository using the full path with a rolling minor tag pin:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/<action-path>@v2.1

Tag pinning

Pin to a rolling minor tag (e.g., @v2.1) to automatically receive patch releases. Pin to an exact tag (e.g., @v2.1.1) for full reproducibility.

docs.title: Minimal workflow example
docs.text:
name: CI - Test and Validate

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  codeql:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Consuming reusable workflows
docs.text:
Reusable workflows produce canonical check names across all repositories. Reference workflows using the full path to the workflow file:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1

docs.title: CI workflow example
docs.text:
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    with:
      language: python

docs.title: CD workflow example
docs.text:
name: CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [develop, main]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # The docs job deploys gh-pages, and the report job reports develop's
    # deploys to the org's operations queue, as the automation App. `inherit`
    # within the org: it carries the App keys from the `automation`
    # environment. A caller in another org passes APP_CLIENT_ID and
    # APP_PRIVATE_KEY by name, since `inherit` reaches only a reusable
    # workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise.
    secrets: inherit

  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
    # Every release pushes its tags as the automation App. `inherit` within
    # the org: it carries the App keys from the `automation` environment.
    # Python publishes via OIDC trusted publishing, so no publishing secret is
    # needed. A caller in another org passes APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY
    # by name (see Release publishing secrets below).
    secrets: inherit

docs.title: Org Actions variables
docs.text:
Besides the App secrets, the reusable workflows read two org-level Actions variables, visible to all repositories, which the human publishes once per org from the host configuration:

Variable Holds VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS The trusted-authors configuration, as compact JSON. Every step that runs a vergil-tooling command reading GitHub content gets it, and stops when it is missing or invalid VRG_AUTOMATION_APP The slug of the org's automation App

Set them up in this order: add the org's [orgs.<org>] stanza to the host configuration, install a vergil-tooling release that carries the trust layer on the host, and run vrg-trusted-authors publish --org <org> right away. vrg-trusted-authors render --org <org> previews the values with no GitHub call. A job that runs that release before the variables are published stops loudly; re-run it once they are. See VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS for details.

docs.title: Release publishing secrets
docs.text:
Every release needs the org automation App's APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY: the release tags are pushed with the App's installation token, and a release without them fails before anything is published or tagged (CD Release: secrets). The keys live in the repo's automation environment, and the release job passes them on by one of two routes, as vrg-github-repo-init generates it.

Within vergil-project, the release job passes secrets: inherit. It carries the App keys and every other secret the release reads: the publishing credential the ecosystem needs and, for a repo with a [package] section (one that publishes .deb/.rpm binary packages), the PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE that its package-sign job reads from the repo's main-only package-signing environment. vrg-validate's secrets-inherit check allows inherit only to the vergil-actions workflows that read such secrets, cd-release.yml among them:

  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !github.event.created
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: rust
    secrets: inherit

Across organizations, secrets: inherit passes nothing, so the release job passes the App keys by name, with the publishing credential the ecosystem needs:

Ecosystem Publishing secrets to pass python None — OIDC trusted publishing (requires id-token: write) go None rust CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN 
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !github.event.created
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: rust
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}

A [package] repo outside vergil-project cannot sign its packages yet: the generated release job does not pass the signing secrets (vergil-project/.github#1592).

See CD Release: binary packages for the package-signing environment and the GitHub App setup.

See Reusable Workflows for the full list and detailed documentation.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Each action documents its required workflow permissions. Common patterns:

Permission Actions that require it contents: read All actions (repository checkout) contents: write cd/docs/deploy, cd/release/tag-and-release security-events: write security/codeql, security/semgrep, security/trivy

docs.title: Self-referencing CI
docs.text:
This repository uses local paths (./actions/...) rather than remote references in its own CI workflow. This means changes to an action are validated by the same PR that modifies them — no separate integration testing step is needed.

Consuming repositories use the full remote reference (vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/...@v2.1).

docs.title: Action Reference
docs.text: All actions are composite GitHub Actions located under the actions/ directory, organized by pipeline phase. Each action is self-contained with an action.yml definition and optional supporting scripts.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
• ci/security/codeql — Runs GitHub CodeQL static analysis for a single language.
  • ci/security/semgrep — Runs Semgrep SAST scanning with language-specific and cross-cutting security rulesets.
  • ci/version-bump/version-divergence — Verifies that the PR branch version differs from the main branch version.
  • ci/matrix — Builds the per-version job matrix (version label and container image for each entry) from the resolver outputs of shared/setup/vergil; auto-wired into ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/toolchain/pin-python — Pins uv to a Python leg's resolved version and to the image's interpreter (UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system); auto-wired into the Python matrix legs of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/toolchain/install-python — Installs a Python leg's dev dependencies (uv sync --group dev --frozen), or skips the install with a notice on a repository with neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock; auto-wired into the Python legs of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/toolchain/assert — Fails a CI leg whose running Python, Go, Rust or Node (TypeScript) is not the version CI resolved for it; auto-wired into the matrix legs of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test.
  • ci/evidence/emit — Writes a gate's evidence.json and uploads it with the gate's report files as a ci-evidence-<gate> artifact for the release-time evidence bundle.
  • ci/evidence/reports — Holds each language's test and audit report files and stages a matrix leg's reports for the evidence artifact, failing when a passing gate wrote none; auto-wired into ci-test and ci-audit.
  • ci/evidence/assert — Checks ci-quality's build job against vergil-tooling's BUILD flag: skipped with BUILD off, successful with BUILD on; auto-wired into the ci-quality evidence job.

docs.title: CD
docs.text:
• cd/release/tag-and-release — Creates annotated git tags and GitHub Releases.
  • cd/release/validate-inputs — Checks the cd-release inputs and fails early on an invalid combination.
  • cd/release/ci-evidence-gate — Pre-publish gate: harvests the release PR's CI evidence artifacts and checks they are complete before anything is published.
  • cd/release/registry-publish — Builds the release for the repository's language ecosystem, attests it, generates an SBOM and, when enabled, publishes to the package registry.
  • cd/release/ci-evidence-attach — Post-publish: assembles the evidence bundle including the SBOM, attests it and attaches it to the GitHub Release.
  • cd/docs/deploy — Deploys MkDocs documentation using mike for versioned documentation.

docs.title: Ops
docs.text:
• ops/github-config/branch-sweep — Deletes branches whose PR is merged or closed and lists them in the job summary, flagging merged-PR leftovers (auto-wired into ops-github-config).
  • ops/report — Reports a named unattended job's result to the org's operations queue as the automation App, from develop only: opens or comments on the job's ops issue on a failure, records the first green run after one, and never closes an issue.

docs.title: Shared
docs.text:
• shared/security/trivy — Runs Trivy vulnerability scanning, SBOM generation, or container image scanning.
  • shared/docs/stage — Stages the changelog and release-notes pages and patches the MkDocs nav, so ci-docs and cd-docs build from the same source tree.
  • shared/setup/vergil — Installs the vergil-tooling version pinned in vergil.toml and resolves the CI version set with vrg-ci-resolve (versions, primary-version, primary-container-tag, container-tags, container-suffixes; auto-wired into the reusable workflows).
  • shared/setup/primary-suffix — Picks a single-container job's image suffix from the resolver's primary version, with the caller's container-suffix as a must-match cross-check (auto-wired into ci-quality, ci-version-bump and cd-release).
  • shared/setup/system-packages — Installs a repository's declared [container].system-packages on CI test jobs (test-runtime only; auto-wired into ci-test).
  • shared/setup/build-command — Runs a repository's declared [container].build-command on CI test jobs (test-runtime only; auto-wired into ci-test; fail-closed with no retry; exports NODE_PATH so a baked out-of-workspace node library resolves).

docs.title: Package
docs.text:
• package/setup — Checks a package toolchain image (prod-pkg-ubuntu or prod-pkg-rhel) against its /etc/vergil/package-toolchain marker and installs vergil-tooling in it, inside a package build or install-test container. It installs no OS packages, uv or nFPM (auto-wired into ci-package and cd-release).
  • package/image-prefix — Applies a workflow's container-prefix to the vrg-package matrix outputs, so the package jobs run on the <prefix>-pkg-* images (auto-wired into ci-package and cd-release).

docs.title: Publish
docs.text: • publish/index/live-check — Records the digests of the signed package index a publish-index run built, then checks that GitHub Pages serves exactly those files after the deploy. It fails within minutes if Pages is still serving an older deployment (auto-wired into publish-index).

docs.title: Local
docs.text:
Actions used only by this repository's own workflows, not by consumers.

  • local/freeze-internal-refs — Rewrites this repository's relative ./actions/... and @develop refs to absolute refs at the release tag, checks none remain and commits the result (used by cd.yml).

docs.title: docs-deploy
docs.text: Deploys MkDocs documentation using mike for versioned documentation. Handles git configuration, version detection, and mike deploy/set-default.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2
    mkdocs-config: docs/site/mkdocs.yml
    mike-command: mike
    git-user-name: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.name }}
    git-user-email: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.email }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Name Required Default Description version-command Yes — Shell command to extract the version string on main (e.g. cat VERSION, grep -oP ... version.go). mkdocs-config No docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to mkdocs.yml configuration file. mike-command No mike Command to run mike. Set to uv run mike for Python repos that manage their own dependencies via their project's virtual environment. git-user-name Yes — The user.name of the deploy commit. cd-docs.yml passes the org automation App's <app-slug>[bot]. git-user-email Yes — The user.email of the deploy commit. cd-docs.yml passes the App bot user's noreply address, <user-id>+<app-slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com.

A composite action does not enforce required, so the action checks both identity inputs itself: an empty one fails the deploy. There is no default identity.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • The checkout's persisted credentials must be able to push the gh-pages branch (Contents write). cd-docs.yml checks out with a Contents-write token of the org automation App, so its GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-only.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Configure git identity — Sets the git user of the deploy commit from the git-user-name and git-user-email inputs, and fails when either is empty. Marks the workspace as a safe directory to avoid dubious-ownership errors in container jobs.
  2. Determine version — On main, runs the version-command to extract the version and sets alias=latest. On all other branches, sets version=dev with no alias.
  3. Stage changelog and release notes — Copies CHANGELOG.md and releases/*.md into the docs directory, and generates a release notes index page sorted by semver. Uses system Python (/usr/local/bin/python3) to avoid venv PATH shadowing.
  4. Patch mkdocs nav — Injects release version entries into the mkdocs.yml nav under the Releases section.
  5. Deploy docs — On main, runs mike deploy --push --update-aliases <version> latest followed by mike set-default --push latest. On other branches, runs mike deploy --push dev, then makes dev the default version only while the site has no release. See Default version.

docs.title: Default version
docs.text:
The default version is the one the site root redirects to. A release makes latest the default. A develop deploy makes dev the default only while no version carries the latest alias, which it reads from mike list --json. Once a release exists, a develop deploy leaves the default alone.

mike records the default only as the root index.html that mike set-default writes, not in versions.json, so mike list does not show it. An earlier guard looked for a [default] marker that mike list never prints, so every develop deploy reset a released site's default to dev (issue #1214). If mike list fails, the deploy fails and the default is not changed. The logic is in the action's deploy.sh, and tests/default.test.sh checks it with the real mike. The smoke-cd-docs.yml workflow runs that test.

docs.title: Reusable workflow
docs.text:
Docs deployment is typically consumed via the cd-docs.yml reusable workflow rather than calling the composite action directly:

jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # `inherit` within the org: it carries the App keys from the `automation`
    # environment. A caller in another org passes APP_CLIENT_ID and
    # APP_PRIVATE_KEY by name, since `inherit` reaches only a reusable
    # workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise.
    secrets: inherit

docs.title: The App identity
docs.text:
cd-docs.yml's docs job deploys as the org automation App (epic vergil-project/.github#1494, spec §5.4). It runs in the automation environment, which holds the App's APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY, and:

  1. mints an App token scoped to the calling repository, with only Contents write;
  2. checks out with that token, so the gh-pages push uses it;
  3. looks up the App's bot user and passes <app-slug>[bot] and its noreply address to this action as the commit identity.

The workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only. The secrets are declared optional, but a caller that passes none fails the docs job at its token step: there is no fallback to GITHUB_TOKEN. actions/ops/report/tests/app-identity.test.sh guards this.

docs.title: Operations-queue reporting
docs.text: cd-docs.yml also takes a boolean report input (default true). Its report job reports a develop deploy to the org's operations queue as docs-deploy-develop, through ops/report. report: false keeps that job off; cd-docs-refresh.yml passes it, because the refresh reports its own run.

docs.title: Interpreter source
docs.text: The action's "Deploy docs" step sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, and the cd-docs.yml docs job sets it in its job env too, so it also reaches the pre-deploy command. For Python repositories, uv run mike and uv run mkdocs then use the image's Python, never a managed Python that uv downloads because the repository sets python-preference = "only-managed". If the image cannot satisfy the repository's requires-python, the deploy fails loudly. Only the source is pinned: UV_PYTHON is not set (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5; issue #1002). The pin is on the step, so a direct caller of this action gets it without setting anything.

docs.title: MkDocs 2.0 banner
docs.text: The cd-docs.yml workflow sets NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=1 on its "Deploy docs" step, which reaches the mkdocs and mike processes this action starts. Without it, mkdocs-material 9.7.x prints a MkDocs 2.0 warning banner on every build. Callers of cd-docs.yml cannot set it, because a caller's env does not reach a reusable workflow. The workflow sets the variable, not the action, so to hide the banner when you call the action directly, set it in that step's env. The variable only hides the banner. Consumers still pin mkdocs<2 in their own docs dependencies. Added in v2.1.43 (#947, PR #948).

docs.title: Direct usage (standalone)
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2
    git-user-name: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.name }}
    git-user-email: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.email }}

docs.title: Python repo with uv-managed dependencies
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/docs/deploy@v2.1
  with:
    version-command: cat VERSION | cut -d. -f1,2
    mike-command: uv run mike
    git-user-name: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.name }}
    git-user-email: ${{ steps.git-identity.outputs.email }}

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Pages — Enable GitHub Pages in repository settings with source set to Deploy from a branch and branch set to gh-pages.
  • The gh-pages branch is created automatically by mike deploy --push on first run.

docs.title: cd/release/ci-evidence-attach
docs.text:
The post-publish CI-evidence step. It assembles the evidence bundle from what cd/release/ci-evidence-gate downloaded, adds the SBOM built earlier in the job, attests the bundle, and attaches it to the GitHub Release. It runs after tag-and-release, because both the Release (the upload target) and the SBOM (bundle content) exist only then.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves; they choose the mode with the cd-release input evidence-enforce.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Attach CI evidence bundle (post-release)
  id: evidence_attach
  continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }}
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/ci-evidence-attach@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    enforce: ${{ inputs.evidence-enforce }}
    sbom-file: ${{ steps.evidence_sbom.outputs.path }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH and the .ci-evidence-staging directory that ci-evidence-gate left in the workspace earlier in the same job.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 2.1.129). tag Yes — Release tag the bundle is attached to (e.g. v2.1.129). enforce No "true" "true" (enforcing): a bundling or upload failure fails the step. "false" (warning): it emits a ::warning:: and the step succeeds. Warning mode is a temporary opt-out, not a permanent soft gate. timeout-minutes No "15" Upper bound on the assemble step, enforced with the coreutils timeout command. A timeout counts as a bundling failure. sbom-file No "" Path to the SBOM that registry-publish built. Included when the file exists; when it is set but missing, the step logs a notice and bundles without it.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description attached "true" only when the bundle was assembled, attested and uploaded to the Release. Empty on any failure, in either mode.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Assemble. Runs vrg-ci-evidence assemble with --staging .ci-evidence-staging, the version, a UTC --generated-at timestamp and --sbom-file when the SBOM exists. The command makes no network calls: it builds the tarball and a standalone manifest in evidence-out/ from the evidence already downloaded. On failure it reports failed (exit <rc>) or timed out after <n>m and exits with that code in enforcing mode, or 0 with a warning in warning mode.
  2. Attest. Runs actions/attest-build-provenance on evidence-out/*.tar.gz. Skipped when assembly failed.
  3. Attach. Runs gh release upload <tag> evidence-out/*.tar.gz evidence-out/*-manifest.json --clobber and writes attached=true on success. A failed upload is fatal in enforcing mode and a warning in warning mode. Skipped when assembly failed.

The attest step is a uses: step, so the shell's warning-mode handling cannot catch its failure. cd-release covers that with continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }} on the calling step.

docs.title: Enforcement in cd-release
docs.text: A plain Enforce CI evidence attach step follows this one and, in enforcing mode, fails the job when the attach step's outcome is failure or it succeeded without attached=true (#925). By then the tag and Release are already published, so its error says the release is missing its evidence bundle and needs operator attention.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• contents: write (to upload Release assets)
  • id-token: write and attestations: write (for the provenance attestation)

docs.title: cd/release/ci-evidence-gate
docs.text:
The pre-publish CI-evidence gate. It finds the release PR, downloads the ci-evidence-<gate> artifacts its CI produced (see ci/evidence/emit), and checks that every required gate's evidence is present and complete. It runs before anything is published, so in enforcing mode no package, tag or Release is created without complete evidence.

It does not build, attest or attach anything: at this point the GitHub Release does not exist and the SBOM is not built. cd/release/ci-evidence-attach does that after tag-and-release, from the evidence this action downloaded.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves; they choose the mode with the cd-release input evidence-enforce.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: CI evidence gate (pre-publish)
  id: evidence_gate
  continue-on-error: ${{ !inputs.evidence-enforce }}
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/ci-evidence-gate@v2.1
  env:
    VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS: ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }}
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    enforce: ${{ inputs.evidence-enforce }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH. It also needs VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS set from ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }} in the calling step's env: a composite action cannot read vars, and vergil-tooling stops when the variable is missing or invalid (see Variables).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 2.1.129). enforce No "true" "true" (enforcing): a failure or timeout fails the step, before publish. "false" (warning): it emits a ::warning:: and the step succeeds. Warning mode is a temporary opt-out, not a permanent soft gate. timeout-minutes No "15" Upper bound on the harvest, enforced with the coreutils timeout command (composite steps cannot use timeout-minutes). A timeout counts as a gate failure.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description passed "true" only when the harvest exited 0. Empty on any failure or timeout, in either mode.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs one step:

timeout "${TIMEOUT_MINUTES}m" vrg-ci-evidence harvest \
  --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --merge-sha "$GITHUB_SHA" \
  --out-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.ci-evidence-staging"

vrg-ci-evidence harvest resolves the release PR from the merge commit, downloads the required gate artifacts, validates them, and exits non-zero when a required gate is missing or incomplete. It leaves the downloaded evidence and a harvest-state.json in .ci-evidence-staging, which ci-evidence-attach reads later, so the artifacts are downloaded once.

On success the step writes passed=true. On failure it reports failed (exit <rc>) or timed out after <n>m, then exits with the tool's code in enforcing mode, or exits 0 with a warning in warning mode.

docs.title: Enforcement in cd-release
docs.text: cd-release does not rely on the step's exit code alone. A plain Enforce CI evidence gate step follows it and fails the job when, in enforcing mode, the gate step's outcome is failure or it succeeded without passed=true. So a gate failure cannot be masked into a green step (#925). See All Hard Gates.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• actions: read, to list and download the release PR's ci-evidence-* artifacts from its CI run. A reusable workflow's permissions are capped by the caller, so the consuming repository's cd.yml must grant it too.
  • contents: read (the cd-release release job grants contents: write for its other steps).

The step authenticates with the workflow's github.token.

docs.title: cd/release/registry-publish
docs.text:
Builds the release for the repository's language ecosystem, optionally attests the build and generates an SBOM, and, when enabled, publishes to the package registry. Build and publish commands come from vergil-tooling's ecosystem metadata (vrg-ecosystem-resolve) unless the caller overrides them.

This action is wired automatically into the cd-release release job, where its Build and publish step runs for python, rust, go and typescript repositories. Consuming repositories set its behavior through the cd-release inputs and secrets, not by calling it directly.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Build and publish
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/registry-publish@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    registry-publish: "true"
    attestation-subject-path: dist/*
    sbom-output-file: sbom-$VERSION.cdx.json

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language. Selects the ecosystem build and publish commands. version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 1.2.3). Exported as VERSION to the build and publish commands. registry-publish No "false" "true" runs the publish step. build-command No "" Replaces the ecosystem build command. publish-command No "" Replaces the ecosystem publish command. attestation-subject-path No "" Glob of build outputs to attest with actions/attest-build-provenance. Empty skips attestation. sbom-output-file No "" SBOM output path; $VERSION is replaced with the version. Empty skips the SBOM. cargo-registry-token No "" Rust: crates.io token. Exported as CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, which cargo publish reads.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description build-command The build command used (derived or overridden). publish-command The publish command used (derived or overridden). sbom-output-file The SBOM path with $VERSION replaced; empty when no SBOM was requested.

docs.title: Ecosystem commands
docs.text:
The derived commands come from vergil-tooling's language registry:

Language Build Publish Credential variable python uv build uv publish none (PyPI trusted publishing) rust cargo build --release --locked --workspace cargo publish --locked CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN go go build ./... none none typescript npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run build none none

Rust's commands carry --locked, so a release builds and publishes exactly what Cargo.lock records and a stale lockfile fails the step, and the build takes --workspace, so it builds every member of a workspace. It is the same command vrg-validate builds before release, so validation and release build the same thing. Both flags come from vergil-tooling (vergil-tooling#4470 and #4476); a vergil-tooling release without them derives cargo build --release and cargo publish.

TypeScript has no publish command, so a TypeScript release builds and is never published to npm. Its build installs from the lockfile first, with --ignore-scripts so no dependency's install script runs, because the release job builds on a fresh checkout with no node_modules. The command comes from vergil-tooling (vergil-tooling#4509); a vergil-tooling release without it derives no TypeScript build command, so the build step is skipped.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Derive commands. Runs vrg-ecosystem-resolve <language>, which sets build, publish and credential-secret step outputs, then replaces build or publish with build-command / publish-command when given. An unsupported language fails the step.
  2. Resolve version placeholders. Replaces $VERSION in sbom-output-file.
  3. Build. Creates dist/, then runs the build command with VERSION set. Skipped when there is no build command.
  4. Attest build provenance. Runs actions/attest-build-provenance on attestation-subject-path. Skipped when it is empty.
  5. Generate SBOM. Runs shared/security/trivy with scan-type: sbom. Skipped when sbom-output-file is empty.
  6. Publish. Runs only when registry-publish is "true" and there is a publish command. The step sets CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN from the cargo-registry-token input, then runs publish.sh. When the ecosystem names a credential variable and that variable is empty, the step fails with an ::error:: naming the cd-release secret to set (or telling you to turn registry-publish off): CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN comes from the CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret. A requested publish that cannot happen never lets the release report success. A credential variable this action does not set also fails the step, since it means vergil-tooling and vergil-actions disagree on the name. Python names no credential: uv publish uses PyPI trusted publishing, which needs id-token: write and a trusted publisher configured for the project on PyPI.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• contents: read to build
  • id-token: write and attestations: write when attestation-subject-path is set
  • id-token: write to publish a python release (PyPI trusted publishing)

docs.title: cd/release/tag-and-release
docs.text:
Creates an annotated git tag and a GitHub Release. All mutating steps are skipped when the tag already exists, making the action safe to re-run. Every tag push uses the automation App's installation token passed as tag-token, never the checkout's GITHUB_TOKEN.

Rolling minor tags

Rolling minor tags (e.g. v1.2) are no longer created by this action. They are now managed by vrg-promote in the release orchestrator's promote phase.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Mint release tag token
  id: tag_token
  uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
  with:
    app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
    private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
    repositories: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
    permission-contents: write

- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: "1.2.3"
    tag-token: ${{ steps.tag_token.outputs.token }}
    release-title: mqrestadmin
    release-notes: "Release notes markdown here"
    release-artifacts: ""
    tag-prefix: v

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description version Yes — Semver version string (e.g. 1.2.3). tag-token Yes — The automation App's installation token, with Contents write on this repository, that every tag push uses. The action fails before tagging when it is empty. release-title No <repo-name> v<version> Release title override. release-notes No A link to the GitHub Pages site Release notes override. release-artifacts No "" Space-separated glob of files to attach to the GitHub Release. Leave empty for no artifacts. tag-prefix No v Prefix prepended to the version to form the git tag.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Name Description tag The full tag name that was (or would be) created (e.g. v1.2.3). tag-created true if a new tag was created, false if it already existed.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• contents: write on the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which creates the GitHub Release.
  • Contents write on the App token passed as tag-token, which pushes the tags. A tag whose commit changes .github/workflows/ files that are not yet on the remote also needs Workflows write (vergil-actions' own cd.yml, whose release commit freezes its internal refs).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Compute tag name — Concatenates tag-prefix and version (e.g. v + 1.2.3 = v1.2.3).
  2. Check existing tag — If the tag already exists, all subsequent steps are skipped (idempotent re-run).
  3. Require the tag token — Fails, with nothing tagged, when tag-token is empty.
  4. Configure git identity — Sets the git user to github-actions[bot].
  5. Create annotated tag — Creates v<version> with message Release <version> and pushes it with the App token.
  6. Create GitHub Release — Uses gh release create with the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, the provided title and notes, and optional artifacts.
  7. Verify tag is resolvable from remote — Clones the tag back from GitHub. If that fails, the tag reached the remote with missing objects: it is re-pushed whole with the App token and cloned again.

Every push goes through the action's push-tag.sh. actions/checkout leaves its token in the repository's git config as an http.<server>/.extraheader Authorization header, and git sends every value of that key. The script resets that list and sets the App token's header, as command-line git config, so the push authenticates as the App alone.

docs.title: Standard library release
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    tag-token: ${{ steps.tag_token.outputs.token }}
    release-title: mqrestadmin
    release-notes: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.notes }}

docs.title: Release with build artifacts
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/tag-and-release@v2.1
  with:
    version: "2.0.0"
    tag-token: ${{ steps.tag_token.outputs.token }}
    release-title: myapp
    release-notes: "## What's New\n\nInitial v2 release."
    release-artifacts: "dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.whl"

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text: • Tag protection — The Tag protection ruleset restricts the creation, update and deletion of release tags to the repository Admin role and the automation App (creation since epic vergil-project/.github#1350). So the tags are pushed as the App, which needs Contents write on the repository; see APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

docs.title: cd/release/validate-inputs
docs.text:
Checks the cd-release inputs before anything else runs and fails early on an invalid combination. It runs vrg-release-validate-inputs from vergil-tooling.

This action is wired automatically as the first check in the cd-release release job. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Validate inputs
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/cd/release/validate-inputs@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    container-tag: ""
    registry-publish: "true"

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description language No "" The repository's language. Empty for repositories with no language ecosystem. container-tag No "" Container image tag. cd-release passes the release job's tag, the resolver's primary-container-tag from its setup job, never a caller input. registry-publish No "false" Whether publishing to a package registry is enabled ("true" to enable).

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The step fails when either of these holds for a language vergil-tooling supports:

  • registry-publish is "true" but the language has no publish command (e.g. go, cpp, typescript).
  • container-tag is set but the language is not one of python, rust or go.

It passes without checking when language is empty. A language that vergil-tooling does not support also passes: the action hands the language to vrg-release-validate-inputs as a positional argument, and the tool rejects an unsupported language only when it is given with --language.

docs.title: ci/evidence/assert
docs.text:
Checks the result of ci-quality's build job against vergil-tooling's BUILD flag, so the quality evidence gate passes only when the build ran exactly when it should have (epic vergil-project/.github#1174).

The build job runs vrg-validate --check build only when vergil-tooling turns the BUILD check on for the repository's language. vrg-ci-resolve reports that as build-enabled, which the setup action passes on. A skipped build job is therefore a valid result, so the job cannot be gated by the evidence job's "every job succeeded" check. This action checks it against the flag instead.

This action is wired automatically into the evidence job of ci-quality. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/assert@v2.1
  with:
    build-enabled: ${{ needs.matrix.outputs.build-enabled }}
    build-result: ${{ needs.build.result }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description build-enabled Yes — The matrix job's build-enabled output, true or false. build-result Yes — needs.build.result: success, failure, cancelled or skipped.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
build-gate.sh passes for exactly two pairs and fails with an ::error:: for every other:

build-enabled build-result Outcome false skipped Pass true success Pass true skipped, failure or cancelled Fail: BUILD is on, but the build did not succeed false success, failure or cancelled Fail: BUILD is off, but the build job was not skipped anything else any Fail: the flag must be true or false any anything else Fail: the result must be one GitHub reports

An empty flag is an error, never read as off. The setup action already gives false when an older vergil-tooling reports no build-enabled, so an empty flag means the matrix job did not run.

docs.title: ci/evidence/emit
docs.text:
Writes a gate's evidence.json and uploads it, with the gate's report files, as a ci-evidence-<gate> workflow-run artifact. At release time cd-release harvests these artifacts (vrg-ci-evidence) into the attested evidence bundle it attaches to the GitHub Release (see cd/release/ci-evidence-gate and cd/release/ci-evidence-attach).

This action is wired automatically into the evidence-producing jobs of the reusable CI workflows:

Workflow gate ci-security security ci-quality quality ci-audit audit ci-test test ci-package package

Consuming repositories do not add it themselves. In ci-test and ci-audit the report files and tools come from each language's contract in ci/evidence/reports. In ci-quality the files are evidence-reports/quality-*: the common and custom transcripts and every lint and typecheck leg's reports. The tools are vrg-validate-common and vrg-validate-custom, then the language's lint and typecheck tools from the same contract. Because an entry that matches no file is skipped, ci-quality first checks, with that action's expect mode, that every lint and typecheck report of the language is there.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/emit@v2.1
  with:
    gate: test
    files: |
      evidence-reports/coverage-*.xml
      evidence-reports/junit-*.xml
    tools: '[{"name": "pytest"}, {"name": "coverage.py"}]'

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description gate Yes — Evidence gate name: security, test, audit, quality or package. Sets the artifact name (ci-evidence-<gate>) and the gate field of evidence.json. files No "" Newline- or space-separated report file paths or globs to include (e.g. SARIF, coverage XML, JUnit XML). An entry that matches no file is skipped, not an error. tools No [] JSON array for the tools field, e.g. [{"name":"codeql","version":"2.17.0"}]. metrics No {} JSON object for the metrics field, e.g. coverage percent or finding counts.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Stage. Creates $RUNNER_TEMP/ci-evidence-<gate>, copies every regular file that matches an entry in files into it (flattened to its basename), and writes evidence.json:

    {"gate": "<gate>", "tools": [...], "metrics": {...}, "files": ["<basename>", ...]}

    tools and metrics must be valid JSON; jq fails the step otherwise. 2. Upload. Uploads the staging directory as the ci-evidence-<gate> artifact with actions/upload-artifact.

Because evidence.json is always written, the artifact is always produced, even for a gate that has no report files yet. Whether an artifact is complete enough is decided at release time: the harvest rejects an evidence.json-only payload as incomplete (see All Hard Gates).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: None beyond the default; uploading a workflow artifact needs no extra scope.

docs.title: ci/evidence/reports
docs.text:
Holds the per-language report-file contract of the test and audit evidence gates and of the quality gate's lint and typecheck legs, stages one matrix leg's reports for the gate's evidence artifact, and checks that the quality evidence job received every lint and typecheck report.

vrg-validate writes each gate's machine-readable reports at the workspace root. At release time the evidence gate (cd/release/ci-evidence-gate) refuses a required gate whose artifact carries no report file, so the names staged here must be the ones the language's gate commands write:

Language Gate Report files Tools python test coverage.xml, junit.xml pytest, coverage.py python audit pip-audit.json, licenses.json pip-audit, pip-licenses rust test coverage.xml, junit.xml cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-nextest rust audit cargo-deny.json cargo-deny python lint quality-ruff.json ruff python typecheck quality-mypy.xml mypy rust lint quality-clippy.json rustfmt, clippy rust typecheck quality-cargo-check.json cargo typescript test coverage.xml, junit.xml vitest, @vitest/coverage-v8 typescript audit npm-audit.json, licenses.json npm audit, vrg-npm-license-gate typescript lint quality-eslint.json prettier, eslint typescript typecheck quality-tsc.txt tsc

lint and typecheck are the legs of the quality gate in ci-quality. Each leg is its own job and writes only its own report, so the contract is per leg. The gate's common and custom transcripts (quality-common.log and quality-custom.log) belong to no leg's contract; ci-quality stages them itself.

The Rust test gate writes junit.xml through cargo-nextest, and the Rust lint and typecheck gates write quality-clippy.json and quality-cargo-check.json (clippy's and cargo check's --message-format=json output) from vergil-tooling#4473 on. A repository pinned to a vergil-tooling release whose Rust gate does not write its report fails its passing legs here, on the missing file. cargo-deny.json, quality-clippy.json and quality-cargo-check.json hold JSON Lines, one object per line; they are staged as written.

The TypeScript gates write their reports from vergil-tooling#4508 on: Vitest's JUnit report and its Cobertura coverage (copied to coverage.xml), npm audit --json as npm-audit.json, ESLint's JSON formatter output as quality-eslint.json, and the tsc --diagnostics output as quality-tsc.txt. Prettier runs first in the lint gate and writes no report. As for Rust, a repository pinned to a vergil-tooling release without them fails its passing legs here.

Like Python's, the TypeScript audit gate also writes a license report, licenses.json: vrg-npm-license-gate checks each package in the committed package-lock.json against the license policy and writes its findings there, from vergil-tooling#4722 on (released in vergil-tooling v2.1.327). A repository pinned to an earlier vergil-tooling release fails its passing TypeScript audit legs here, on the missing licenses.json.

This table, in actions/ci/evidence/reports/reports.sh, is the one place vergil-actions records the contract. The files are written by vergil-tooling's gate commands (lib/languages.py), so a change to a gate's report names changes both.

A fleet language with no entry in the table (today go and cpp) writes no report file the release-time evidence gate accepts yet. Its legs do not fail: the step emits a ::warning:: naming the language and gate and saying its reports are not produced yet, and stages nothing, and mode: tools gives an empty tools list with the same warning. The release-time evidence gate still decides; in enforcing mode it rejects an empty payload.

The quality gate also serves repositories with no fleet primary language: a shell or Claude plugin repository, or one that passes no language. Their lint and typecheck legs write no report, so for those two gates such a language, or an empty one, is not an error: the step emits a ::notice:: saying it has no report contract, stages nothing and lists no tools, and the quality evidence carries the common and custom transcripts alone. The test and audit gates still refuse it.

Any other unknown language, an unknown gate, an empty or unsafe version, or an unknown mode fails the step.

This action is wired automatically into ci-test, ci-audit and ci-quality. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Run unit tests
  id: gate
  run: vrg-validate --check test

- name: Stage test reports for evidence
  if: always()
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/reports@v2.1
  with:
    mode: stage
    language: rust
    gate: test
    version: ${{ matrix.version }}
    gate-outcome: ${{ steps.gate.outcome }}

In the evidence job, mode: tools gives the tools JSON for ci/evidence/emit:

- name: Resolve test evidence tools
  id: reports
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/reports@v2.1
  with:
    mode: tools
    language: rust
    gate: test
    reports-dir: evidence-reports

- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/emit@v2.1
  with:
    gate: test
    files: evidence-reports/*
    tools: ${{ steps.reports.outputs.tools }}

The quality evidence job checks the downloaded legs with mode: expect before it emits, since the emit action skips a pattern that matches nothing:

- name: Require the lint and typecheck reports
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/evidence/reports@v2.1
  with:
    mode: expect
    language: rust
