    reports-dir: evidence-reports

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description mode Yes — stage copies this leg's reports into out-dir; tools outputs the gate's tools JSON; expect checks reports-dir holds every lint and typecheck report of the language. language Yes — Primary language of the calling repository, e.g. python or rust. May be empty only for the lint and typecheck gates and in expect mode. gate Stage and tools modes "" test, audit, lint or typecheck. Not used in expect mode. version Stage mode "" The matrix leg's version label, appended to each staged file's stem. gate-outcome Stage mode "" The outcome of the step that ran the gate (steps.<id>.outcome). out-dir No ci-reports Stage mode, the directory to stage the reports into. reports-dir Expect mode; optional in tools mode "" The directory holding every leg's staged reports, the evidence job's download directory. In tools mode, a gate whose legs left skip records there lists no tools.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description tools Tools mode, the gate's tools JSON array, e.g. [{"name":"cargo-deny"}].

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Stage. Each of the language's report files is copied into out-dir as <stem>-<version>.<ext>, for example cargo-deny.json as cargo-deny-1.85.json, so every version's report stays distinct once the evidence job flattens the legs' files by basename. No other file is staged, so the evidence job takes every file the legs uploaded.

  • When gate-outcome is success, every report must exist and be non-empty. A missing or empty one fails the step with an ::error:: naming it, so a gate that passed without writing its evidence fails the leg, and through it the required evidence check, instead of failing later at release.
  • When the gate step did not succeed, the leg has already failed. The reports that exist are staged for diagnosis and the missing ones are noted.
  • An empty or placeholder file is never staged.
  • A gate skipped because the repository is not bootstrapped yet is accepted, as Not-bootstrapped repositories says.
  • For a language with no entry in the table, the step warns (or, for a lint or typecheck leg of a repository with no fleet primary language, notes) and stages nothing, whatever gate-outcome says.

Tools. Writes the gate's tools JSON array to the tools output: [], with a warning or notice, for a language with no entry. Given reports-dir, a gate whose legs were skipped as not bootstrapped lists no tools (see below).

Expect. For each of the language's lint and typecheck reports, reports-dir must hold at least one non-empty, version-suffixed copy (<stem>-<version>.<ext>, for example quality-clippy-1.95.json). A missing one fails the step with an ::error:: naming it. For a language with no lint or typecheck entry, the step warns or notes as above and passes. A gate whose legs were all skipped as not bootstrapped needs no report (see below). An empty reports-dir, or one that is not a directory, fails.

docs.title: Not-bootstrapped repositories
docs.text:
A freshly initialised repository has none of its language's manifests yet (no pyproject.toml or uv.lock, no Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, no package.json or package-lock.json, or a package.json that declares no dependency and no package-lock.json) and no source of the language. vrg-validate skips its language stages for such a repository, loudly, recording each one warn in .vergil/vrg-validate-last.json (vergil-tooling#4384) with a skip that gives the reason (not-bootstrapped), the language and the missing manifests (vergil-tooling#5034, released in vergil-tooling v2.1.342), and the gate passes having written no report.

In stage mode a leg whose gate passed and wrote none of its reports is accepted as skipped only when all of these hold:

  • the vrg-validate record is of the checked-out commit and the run exited 0;
  • every stage the run recorded is warn, the gate's own among them, so no stage really ran;
  • every stage carries a skip with the reason not-bootstrapped, the leg's language and at least one missing manifest.

The record alone decides: vrg-validate applies the manifest and source tests, and this action does not repeat them. A warn stage with no skip, as a vergil-tooling release before v2.1.342 records one, is not a skip.

The step then prints a ::notice:: naming the leg and the reason, stages no report, and writes the leg's skip record into out-dir: <gate>-not-bootstrapped-<version>.json, or quality-<gate>-not-bootstrapped-<version>.json for a lint or typecheck leg. It is a JSON object with "skipped": true, "reason": "not-bootstrapped", the gate, language, version, the commit (head) and the missing manifests the record gives the gate's stage. When any condition fails, each failing one is an ::error:: and the leg fails on its missing reports, as any passing gate that wrote no report does.

In expect mode a lint or typecheck gate with no report passes, with a ::notice::, when reports-dir holds its legs' skip records. A skip record of another language or gate, or one found beside a report of the same gate, fails the step.

In tools mode, given reports-dir, the step reads the same skip records the same way. A gate whose legs left them gives [], with a ::notice:: naming them, so the gate's evidence.json names no tool that never ran; a skip record expect mode would refuse fails the step here too. ci-test, ci-audit and ci-quality pass their download directory.

The skip record is uploaded with the leg's reports and reaches the gate's evidence artifact, so the release-time evidence gate finds the skip recorded in the gate's payload rather than an empty one. A bootstrapped repository never gets a skip record, so a missing report there still fails the leg.

docs.title: ci/matrix
docs.text:
Builds the per-version job matrix for a reusable CI workflow. Each matrix entry carries the version label, used in the job and check name, and the fully qualified container image the leg runs in.

The versions, and the image suffix and tag of each, come from the single resolver, vrg-ci-resolve, by way of the outputs of shared/setup/vergil. This action does no version or family routing of its own.

This action is wired automatically into the matrix job of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Install vergil-tooling
  id: setup
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1

- name: Resolve matrix
  id: resolve
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/matrix@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    versions: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.versions }}
    primary-version: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.primary-version }}
    container-tags: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.container-tags }}
    container-suffixes: ${{ steps.setup.outputs.container-suffixes }}
    container-suffix: python

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language of the calling repository (e.g. python, cpp, shell). Selects the run-once collapse only. versions Yes — The setup action's versions output, e.g. ["3.14","3.13"] or ["clang-20","gcc-14"]. primary-version Yes — The setup action's primary-version output. container-tags Yes — The setup action's container-tags output: version to image tag. container-suffixes Yes — The setup action's container-suffixes output: version to image suffix. container-prefix No prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev). container-suffix No "" The calling workflow's container-suffix, used only as a cross-check. When set, it must be one of the resolved suffixes.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description all JSON array of {version, image} objects, one per resolved version. Used by per-version kinds (TEST always; TYPECHECK for C++ and the single-suffix languages). once The primary version's entry alone for C++ and TypeScript; identical to all for every other language. Used by run-once kinds (LINT and AUDIT; TYPECHECK too for TypeScript).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Every image is ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<container-suffixes[v]>:<container-tags[v]>, for every language:

Version Resolver's suffix and tag Image clang-20 cpp-clang, 20 prod-cpp-clang:20 gcc-14 cpp-gcc, 14 prod-cpp-gcc:14 node-24 ts-node, 24 prod-ts-node:24 3.14 python, 3.14 prod-python:3.14 latest (no language) base, latest prod-base:latest

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
The action fails with an ::error:: annotation, and writes no matrix, when:

  • an input is empty, or versions is not a non-empty JSON array;
  • a version has no tag in container-tags or no suffix in container-suffixes;
  • primary-version is not one of versions;
  • container-suffix is set but is not one of the resolved suffixes. The workflow's inputs and the repository's vergil.toml then disagree on the language (for example container-suffix: python with no [project].primary-language, which resolves to prod-base:latest), and the legs would run on the wrong image.

docs.title: Run-once kinds
docs.text: For C++ and TypeScript some check kinds run once, on the primary version, rather than once per version: LINT and AUDIT for C++; LINT, AUDIT and TYPECHECK for TypeScript. The once output gives those jobs a one-entry matrix.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The logic is in resolve.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/resolve.test.sh). The step prints both resolved arrays to the job log. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: security/codeql
docs.text: Runs GitHub CodeQL static analysis (init + autobuild + analyze) for a single language, then evaluates the resulting SARIF and fails on gating findings.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    queries: "+security-extended"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description language Yes — Language to analyze: python, go, rust, cpp or typescript. queries No +security-extended Query suite to run.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• security-events: write (required for uploading SARIF results)
  • contents: read

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Resolve the CodeQL language — Maps the language input to its CodeQL analysis-language identifier with resolve-language.sh: typescript becomes javascript-typescript and cpp becomes c-cpp. Every other language passes through unchanged.
  2. Initialize CodeQL — Uses github/codeql-action/init@v4 to set up the CodeQL database for the mapped language and the query suite.
  3. Autobuild — Uses github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4 to automatically detect and build the project.
  4. Run analysis — Uses github/codeql-action/analyze@v4 to perform the analysis and upload results, writing the SARIF to ${{ runner.temp }}/codeql-sarif. Results are categorized by /language:<mapped language>, for example /language:c-cpp for cpp.
  5. Fail on CodeQL findings — Runs vrg-sarif-evaluate on that SARIF directory. It filters the findings by severity, annotates them and writes a job summary, and fails the step on a gating finding. vrg-sarif-evaluate comes from vergil-tooling, so install it first with shared/setup/vergil, as ci-security does.

docs.title: Python CodeQL analysis
docs.text:
jobs:
  codeql:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Go CodeQL analysis
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/codeql@v2.1
  with:
    language: go

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) — Must be enabled on the repository for SARIF upload to work. For public repositories, GHAS is available by default.
  • Code scanning alerts — Results appear in the repository's Security > Code scanning alerts tab.

docs.title: security/semgrep
docs.text: Runs Semgrep static analysis with language-specific and cross-cutting security rulesets.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    extra-config: "p/owasp-top-ten"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description language Yes — Language ruleset to enable (maps to p/<language>, e.g. python, golang). extra-config No "" Additional Semgrep config strings, space-separated (e.g. p/owasp-top-ten).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• security-events: write (required for uploading SARIF results)
  • contents: read

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Check language ruleset — Queries the Semgrep registry to verify that p/<language> exists. If the registry does not have a ruleset for the specified language, the language-specific config is silently skipped.
  2. Auto-detect rulesets — Scans the repository for content that benefits from specialized rulesets:
    • p/dockerfile — enabled when Dockerfile* files are present
    • p/github-actions — enabled when .github/workflows/ contains workflow files
  3. Run scan — Executes semgrep scan with the following config rulesets:
    • p/ci — CI pipeline security rules (injection, secrets in workflows, unsafe patterns)
    • p/command-injection — Unsafe shell construction and command injection patterns
    • p/security-audit — Cross-cutting security audit rules
    • p/secrets — Secret detection rules
    • p/<language> — Language-specific rules (if available in the registry)
    • p/dockerfile — Dockerfile best practices (if Dockerfiles detected)
    • p/github-actions — GitHub Actions injection patterns (if workflow files detected)
    • Any additional rulesets from extra-config
  4. Filter and upload SARIF — Runs vrg-sarif-filter to write semgrep-results.upload.sarif, a copy with accepted-suppressed results (e.g. justified nosemgrep) removed, and uploads that copy to GitHub code scanning using github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4, categorized as semgrep. The unfiltered semgrep-results.sarif is left in place for the evidence bundle. These steps run even if the scan finds issues (if: always()) and need vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Rule exclusions
docs.text: The underlying vrg-semgrep-scan supports a repeatable --exclude-rule <full-rule-id> flag that drops individual findings by their full Semgrep rule ID. Caller-supplied --exclude-rule values are added on top of the fleet DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES — they never replace the defaults, so the fleet baseline always applies.

docs.title: Fleet default: github-actions-mutable-action-tag
docs.text:
github-actions-mutable-action-tag is currently exempted fleet-wide (it lives in DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES). This rule flags third-party actions pinned to a mutable tag (e.g. @v4) rather than a full commit SHA. The exemption is temporary, pending backlog vergil-project/.github#194 — once pin-advancement tooling exists to keep SHA pins current, third-party action SHAs will be pinned and the exemption lifted.

Our own vergil-project/vergil-actions/…@v2.1 references are a permanent exception: they track our controlled release line and are never SHA-pinned, so the rule does not apply to them regardless of the backlog above.

docs.title: Python Semgrep scan
docs.text:
jobs:
  semgrep:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
        with:
          language: python

docs.title: Go with additional OWASP rules
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/security/semgrep@v2.1
  with:
    language: golang
    extra-config: "p/owasp-top-ten"

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) — Must be enabled for SARIF upload. It is available by default on public repositories.
  • Code scanning alerts — Results appear in the repository's Security > Code scanning alerts tab alongside CodeQL results.

docs.title: Future rulesets
docs.text: Additional Semgrep rulesets (such as p/owasp-top-ten for web application security) can be enabled per-repo via the extra-config input. These are not included in the base config because they target specific application types that not all repos in the fleet share.

docs.title: ci/toolchain/assert
docs.text:
Fails a CI leg when the interpreter or toolchain actually running it is not the version CI resolved for it. A repository's own files can choose the interpreter behind Vergil's back (for Python, .python-version or uv's python-preference; for Rust, a rust-toolchain.toml or a rustup override), and a leg would then pass on a version it never ran. This action is the backstop for that. For Rust, the image already pins rustup to its own release (RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, with auto-install off) and vrg-validate rejects a rust-toolchain.toml, so the assertion is the last check behind those. For TypeScript, Vergil selects the Node runtime, and the assertion checks that the Node on the job's PATH is the leg's major.

This action is wired automatically into every matrix leg of ci-quality, ci-audit and ci-test, as the assert-toolchain step. It runs after the dependency install. For Python, an earlier step in the leg (ci/toolchain/pin-python) sets UV_PYTHON to the leg's version and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE to only-system, so uv uses the image's interpreter for the install and the checks. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: assert-toolchain
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/assert@v2.1
  with:
    language: python
    expected: ${{ matrix.version }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description language Yes — Primary language of the calling repository. expected Yes — The version CI resolved for this leg, as x.y (e.g. 3.14, 1.26, 1.100), or for typescript a Node major, bare or with a leading node- (e.g. node-26, 26). Ignored for languages without an assertion.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Language Check python Runs uv run --frozen python -c '...' and compares the interpreter's x.y with expected, logging the interpreter's path. --frozen keeps uv from rewriting uv.lock. go Runs go env GOVERSION in the module (so a toolchain switch in go.mod is what gets reported) and compares its x.y (go1.26.3 is 1.26). rust Runs rustc --version in the repository checkout (so a rustup override would be what gets reported) and compares its x.y (rustc 1.100.0 is 1.100). typescript Runs node -p 'process.versions.node + "\n" + process.execPath' once, in the repository checkout, and compares the version's major (26.1.0 is 26) with expected (a leading node- stripped), logging the Node executable's path. Any other No check yet; prints a ::notice:: saying so and passes.

On a mismatch the step fails with ::error::CI resolved <expected> but the job runs <actual>. It also fails, with an ::error:: annotation, when expected is not an x.y version (for typescript, not a Node major), or the toolchain cannot be asked for its version or gives an answer it cannot read.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The logic is in assert.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/assert.test.sh, which fakes uv, go, rustc and node). The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• shared/setup/vergil — resolves the versions the legs run.
  • ci/matrix — builds the legs from those versions.

docs.title: ci/toolchain/install-python
docs.text:
Installs a Python CI leg's dev dependencies with uv sync --group dev --frozen, or skips the install with a visible notice on a repository that is not bootstrapped yet (issue #1206).

A Python repository is bootstrapped by two manifests, pyproject.toml and uv.lock. vrg-validate skips its language stages, loudly, when every one of them is missing (vergil-tooling#4384). This action uses the same test, so a freshly initialised Python repository reaches the leg's vrg-validate step and its skip, instead of failing at the install:

The repository has The step Neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock Prints a ::notice:: naming both files and passes. Either of them, or both Runs uv sync --group dev --frozen and fails when it fails.

A partial bootstrap (a pyproject.toml with no uv.lock, say) is not skipped: uv sync --frozen fails on it, and so does the step, as vrg-validate fails it. A skipped install does not pass a repository that has Python sources but no manifest either: the leg's vrg-validate fails its install stage.

This action is wired automatically into every Python leg of ci-quality (lint, typecheck, custom, build), ci-audit (dependencies) and ci-test (unit), after ci/toolchain/pin-python. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Pin uv to the leg's Python interpreter
  if: inputs.language == 'python'
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/pin-python@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ matrix.version }}

- name: Install dependencies
  if: inputs.language == 'python'
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/install-python@v2.1

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: None. The manifests are looked up in the working directory, the checkout.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: On a skip, the notice reads skipped: no pyproject.toml, uv.lock (python repo not bootstrapped yet); add them to install the dev dependencies, and the step exits 0. Otherwise the step runs uv sync --group dev --frozen with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system and exits with uv's status. The interpreter version is the one ci/toolchain/pin-python exported before this step.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: The logic is in install.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/install.test.sh) against a fake uv. The same harness also checks the CI workflows: every job that pins through ci/toolchain/pin-python installs through this action after the pin, and no workflow runs uv sync itself. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ci/toolchain/pin-python — pins uv to the leg's version and the image's interpreter first.
  • ci/toolchain/assert — fails the leg if it runs a version other than the resolved one.

docs.title: ci/toolchain/pin-python
docs.text:
Pins uv to a CI leg's Python interpreter. It exports two variables to the rest of the job:

Variable Value What it fixes UV_PYTHON The leg's resolved x.y The version: the one CI resolved, not one a repository file such as .python-version selects. UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE only-system The source: the image's interpreter.

A repository may set uv's python-preference (for example only-managed, so a local VM never seeds a venv from the host interpreter). That setting picks managed versus system Python, not the version. Without the second variable, a leg in such a repository would have uv download its own managed Python and pass on an interpreter the image never provided. With it, uv always uses the image's interpreter, and a missing interpreter fails the leg instead of being downloaded (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5). uv's environment variables take precedence over a repository's uv settings.

This action is wired automatically into every Python matrix leg of ci-quality (lint, typecheck), ci-audit (dependencies) and ci-test (unit), and into ci-quality's single-container custom job (on the primary version), before the dependency install (ci/toolchain/install-python). Consuming repositories do not add it themselves. ci/toolchain/assert is the backstop that checks the result.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Pin uv to the leg's Python interpreter
  if: inputs.language == 'python'
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/toolchain/pin-python@v2.1
  with:
    version: ${{ matrix.version }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description version Yes — The Python version CI resolved for this leg, as x.y (e.g. 3.14).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Appends UV_PYTHON=<version> and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system to $GITHUB_ENV. The step fails with an ::error:: annotation, writing nothing, when version is not an x.y version or GITHUB_ENV is not set.

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
The logic is in pin.sh next to action.yml, so it can be unit tested (tests/pin.test.sh). The same harness also checks the CI workflows: every job with an assert-toolchain step must pin through this action, and no workflow may set UV_PYTHON by hand. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

The harness also guards the interpreter source everywhere uv runs against a repository's project (issue #1002). Every workflow job that runs a uv project command (uv run, uv sync, uv lock and so on) or uses ci/toolchain/assert must pin UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system before that point: through this action, or with a job-level env. Jobs that resolve no version, such as the ci-docs and cd-docs docs jobs, use the job env. Every composite action or script that runs one must pin it on the step's env or inline on the command line. There are four exceptions:

  • ci/toolchain/assert is pinned by its caller.
  • package/setup/detect.sh reads vergil.toml in package toolchain images that ship no Python, so it needs uv's managed interpreter, and exports a release commit's uv.lock (uv export) in a fetched copy of that commit. Instead of the pin, every uv command in it must pass --no-config, so the repository's uv settings cannot reach it at all (issue #1003). Without it, a repository that sets python-downloads = "manual" stops uv downloading that interpreter.
  • shared/setup/vergil/install-tooling.sh's self-repo sync on a host runner, uv sync --frozen --group dev --python 3.15, is exempt as that exact line. It runs only in vergil-tooling's own CI, whose runner Python is not a series vergil-tooling supports, so it names 3.15 and uv provides it (epic vergil-project/.github#1256). Any other uv command in the file must still pin the source; its container sync does.
  • shared/setup/vergil/install-tooling.sh's lock export, uv export --no-config --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes --format requirements-txt --directory "$1" -o "$2" >/dev/null, is exempt as that exact line. It exports the uv.lock of the released vergil-tooling commit being installed, fetched into a temporary directory, never the repository's own project. Like every vergil-tooling install, it runs with --no-config and with UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE and UV_NO_MANAGED_PYTHON unset (epic vergil-project/.github#1350), so pinning the source there would break that rule.

uv tool commands are not checked, because uv ignores a project's uv settings for them. Fixture workflows and actions test the guard both ways.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ci/toolchain/assert — fails the leg if it runs a version other than the resolved one.
  • ci/matrix — builds the legs and their versions.

docs.title: release-gates/version-divergence
docs.text: Verifies that the PR branch version differs from the main branch version. Fails the step if the two versions are identical.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
  with:
    head-version-command: cat VERSION
    main-version-command: git show origin/main:VERSION

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description head-version-command Yes — Shell command that prints the HEAD (PR branch) version to stdout. main-version-command Yes — Shell command that prints the main branch version to stdout.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Name Description head-version The version extracted from the PR branch. main-version The version extracted from the main branch. diverged true if versions differ, false otherwise.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • contents: read (default)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Fetch main branch — Runs git fetch origin main --depth=1.
  2. Compare versions — Executes both version commands and compares the results. If the versions are identical, the step fails with exit code 1 and a diagnostic message. If they differ, the step succeeds.

docs.title: Simple VERSION file check
docs.text:
jobs:
  version-gate:
    name: "release: version-divergence"
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
        with:
          head-version-command: cat VERSION
          main-version-command: git show origin/main:VERSION

docs.title: Python project version check
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ci/version-bump/version-divergence@v2.1
  with:
    head-version-command: >-
      grep -oP 'version\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' pyproject.toml
    main-version-command: >-
      git show origin/main:pyproject.toml | grep -oP 'version\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+'

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text: • Required status check — Add this as a required status check on the develop branch to prevent PRs from merging without a version bump.

docs.title: local/freeze-internal-refs
docs.text:
Rewrites this repository's internal action and workflow refs to absolute refs at the release tag, checks that none are left unfrozen, and commits the result. It runs vrg-freeze-refs from vergil-tooling.

This is a local action: only this repository's own cd.yml uses it, in the release job on main, just before cd/release/tag-and-release. It is not meant for consuming repositories.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: During development the workflows and actions here refer to each other with relative refs (./actions/..., ./.github/workflows/...) or @develop, so a PR is tested by the code it changes. A consumer that pins @v2.1.0 must get the actions from that same release, and a relative ref does not resolve when a reusable workflow is called from another repository. Freezing the refs at release time solves both. See Reference freezing.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Freeze internal refs to release tag
  uses: ./actions/local/freeze-internal-refs
  with:
    tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}

- name: Tag and release
  uses: ./actions/cd/release/tag-and-release
  with:
    version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description tag Yes — Release tag to freeze to (e.g. v1.5.20). owner-repo No ${{ github.repository }} OWNER/REPO used to build the absolute refs.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Configure the git identity as github-actions[bot].

  2. Freeze and validate. Runs vrg-freeze-refs --owner-repo <owner-repo> --tag <tag> over every .yml and .yaml file under .github/workflows and actions. On each line that contains uses: it rewrites:

    From To ./actions/<path> <owner-repo>/actions/<path>@<tag> ./.github/workflows/<path> <owner-repo>/.github/workflows/<path>@<tag> <owner-repo>/<path>@develop <owner-repo>/<path>@<tag>

    It then fails the step, listing each line in the job summary, if any relative or @develop ref remains. 3. Commit. If anything changed, stages .github/workflows and actions and commits chore(release): freeze internal refs to <tag>.

The commit is not pushed to a branch. The tag-and-release step that follows tags HEAD, so the frozen refs exist only at the release tag; develop and main keep their relative refs.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The step itself only edits and commits locally. Because it changes files under .github/workflows, cd.yml checks out with a GitHub App token that requests contents: write and workflows: write: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push a tag whose commit changes workflow files.

docs.title: ops/github-config/branch-sweep
docs.text:
Deletes the branches on a repo whose pull-request work is finished, and lists every deleted branch in the job summary. It runs vrg-branch-sweep --apply from vergil-tooling, which decides what counts as finished and what is never deleted.

This action is the scheduled safety net behind the delete-on-merge repo setting and the delete-on-close rule. It is wired automatically into the branch-sweep job of the ops-github-config.yml reusable workflow, so every repo whose ops.yml calls that workflow is swept on the same nightly schedule as its github-config job (vrg-github-repo-config update). Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ops/github-config/branch-sweep@v2.1
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
    VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS: ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }}

The action requires vergil-tooling on PATH (installed by a preceding shared/setup/vergil step) and a GH_TOKEN that can read the repo's pull requests and delete its branches. It also needs VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS set from ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }} in the calling step's env: a composite action cannot read vars, and vergil-tooling stops when the variable is missing or invalid (see Variables).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description repo No ${{ github.repository }} Repository to sweep, as OWNER/NAME

docs.title: Token
docs.text: ops-github-config.yml mints a GitHub App token for this job with only contents: write (to delete the branch ref) and pull-requests: read (to decide which branches are finished). The token is scoped to the calling repo alone. The workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: a called workflow can only request the permissions the caller grants, and the standard ops.yml grants contents: read.

docs.title: Job summary
docs.text:
The summary lists each deleted branch with a link to its PR, in two groups:

  • Merged PR, branch not auto-deleted. The delete-on-merge setting should already have removed these. A leftover means GitHub skipped its after-merge processing, and the merge may also have fired no push event (the vergil-actions #951 case). This group is shown in a warning block, and each branch also gets a ::warning:: annotation on the run, so it stands out rather than being quietly cleaned up.
  • PR closed without merging. GitHub never deletes these on its own; the sweep is the expected cleanup when the delete-on-close rule missed one.

Errors are listed in a third group. The full vrg-branch-sweep output is included in a collapsed block.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
The step fails, and so does the job, when:

  • vrg-branch-sweep exits non-zero. A branch that could not be processed, a branch list that could not be read, and an authentication failure all count. The summary is still written first.
  • the per-branch lines cannot be reconciled with the sweep's own summary line (the deleted and error counts disagree, or the summary line is missing). This guards against a change in vrg-branch-sweep's output format silently producing an empty report.

The job does not use continue-on-error.

The reporting logic lives in sweep.sh so it is unit-testable; see actions/ops/github-config/branch-sweep/tests/sweep.test.sh, run by the smoke-branch-sweep.yml workflow.

docs.title: ops/report
docs.text:
Reports a named unattended job's result to the org's operations queue (epic vergil-project/.github#1494). It runs vrg-ops-report from vergil-tooling as the org's automation App. The reporter keeps one open ops issue per job, titled ops: <repo> / <job> failing and labelled ops-report, filed in the calling repository and linked as a sub-issue under the org's operations epic in <org>/.github:

  • a failure or a cancel opens that issue, or comments on it when it is open;
  • the first green run after one records the recovery on it;
  • a green run with no open issue, or one already recovered, writes nothing;
  • a run whose jobs were all skipped reports nothing at all.

Nothing closes an ops issue: a person closes it once the cause is dealt with. The issue holds only the run link, the job name, the failing step, the conclusion and the date, never log text.

A reporting job is the last job of its workflow, with if: always(), so it runs whatever the jobs it reports did.

docs.title: The shared workflows' reporting jobs
docs.text:
Each shared unattended workflow ends with one reporting job per stable job name:

Workflow Reporting job Stable name Reports ops-github-config.yml report-branch-sweep branch-sweep branch-sweep ops-epic-sweep.yml report epic-sweep epic-sweep ops-epic-rollup.yml report epic-rollup epic-rollup ops-upstream-refresh.yml report upstream-refresh prepare, publish cd-docs.yml report docs-deploy-develop docs (job deploy) cd-docs-refresh.yml report docs-refresh refresh publish-index.yml report publish-index build-index, deploy

github-config, trusted-authors-check and dependabot-audit get none: their failures are security signals, never a public ops issue. cd-docs.yml's job also stays off when its caller passes report: false (cd-docs-refresh.yml does, and reports the run itself as docs-refresh) and for a release push: a push to main, or a develop push whose head commit merges a release/* branch, both of which the release records already track. tests/reporting-jobs.test.sh, tests/ops-report-skipped.test.sh, tests/release-push-skip.test.sh and tests/docs-refresh-reports-once.test.sh check these jobs.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  report:
    needs: [build-index, deploy]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: automation
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/ops/report@v2.1
        env:
          VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS: ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }}
          VRG_AUTOMATION_APP: ${{ vars.VRG_AUTOMATION_APP }}
        with:
          job: publish-index
          results: ${{ needs.build-index.result }},${{ needs.deploy.result }}
          app-client-id: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          app-private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

The job declares environment: automation, where the App keys are kept, and checks out the repository first: setting up vergil-tooling reads its vergil.toml. The uses: step sets VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP from the org Actions variables in its own env: a composite action cannot read vars, and the step's env reaches every step of the action (see Variables). Set them nowhere else: on the job or the workflow, VRG_AUTOMATION_APP would reach steps that hold no App token.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description job Yes — The job's stable name, the report key: for example docs-refresh. Never the workflow file, so renaming a file keeps the issue results Yes — Comma list of the needs.<job>.result values of every GitHub job that makes up the named job step No "" The failing step's name, when known app-client-id Yes — The automation App's client ID (secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID) app-private-key Yes — The automation App's private key (secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY)

The results combine into one: any failure makes a failure; else any cancelled makes a cancel; else at least one success makes a success; all skipped reports nothing.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Require develop. On any ref other than refs/heads/develop the action prints a notice and stops, with no token minted and nothing reported, so a feature-branch workflow_dispatch files nothing. On develop it fails when VRG_AUTOMATION_APP or VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS is empty or unset.
  2. Require the App keys. The action fails, naming each empty input, when app-client-id or app-private-key is empty, before any token is minted: an input's required: true does not reject an empty string. The keys are the automation environment's APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets, so the calling job must declare environment: automation to read them. There is no fallback to GITHUB_TOKEN.
  3. Mint the App token, with permission-issues: write only, for the calling repository and the org's .github repository (the operations epic lives there).
  4. Set up vergil-tooling with that token as GH_TOKEN. The setup's identity check sees VRG_AUTOMATION_APP and verifies the token as that App's, so the token is minted before the setup.
  5. Report with vrg-ops-report --repo <owner/repo> --job <job> --results <results> --run-url <run attempt URL>, adding --step when it is set. A reporter that cannot read or write fails the job.

Every step after the first runs only when the first one allowed it. tests/ops-report-ref-guard.test.sh and tests/ops-report-inputs.test.sh check this layout; .github/workflows/smoke-ops-report.yml runs them.

docs.title: Token
docs.text: The token holds Issues write (and Metadata read, which GitHub always grants) on two repositories: the calling one, for its ops issue and the ops-report label, and <org>/.github, for the operations epic and the sub-issue link. GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be used: the issues must be written by the automation App, whose authorship is what the reporter trusts when it reads them back.

docs.title: package/image-prefix
docs.text:
Applies a reusable workflow's container-prefix to the build and test outputs of vrg-package matrix. vrg-package matrix names every cell's image ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod-pkg-<distro>:<version>. With container-prefix: dev this action rewrites the prod-pkg- start of each image to dev-pkg-, so the package jobs run on the development package images. With the default prod both outputs are passed on byte for byte.

This action is wired automatically into the matrix job of ci-package and the package-matrix job of cd-release. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves. They set the workflow's container-prefix input.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Resolve package matrix
  id: resolve
  run: vrg-package matrix --github-output

- name: Apply container prefix
  id: images
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/package/image-prefix@v2.1
  with:
    container-prefix: ${{ inputs.container-prefix }}
    build: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.build }}
    test: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.test }}

The action needs jq on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description container-prefix No prod The calling workflow's container-prefix: prod or dev. An empty value means prod. build Yes The vrg-package matrix build output: a one-line JSON array of cells. test Yes The vrg-package matrix test output: a one-line JSON array of cells.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description build The build cells with the prefix applied to each image. test The test cells with the prefix applied to each image.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Only the ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod-pkg- start of a cell's image changes. Every other field, and the order of the cells, stays as it was.
  • A cell whose image is not under prod-pkg- keeps it, with a ::warning::.
  • A repo without [package] has [] outputs, which pass through as [].
  • The log lists the image each cell will use.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The step fails with an ::error:: annotation, and writes no output, when:

  • container-prefix is not prod, dev or empty;
  • build or test is empty;
  • build or test is not a one-line JSON array of objects that each have a string image.

docs.title: package/setup
docs.text:
Checks a package toolchain image and installs vergil-tooling in it, inside a package build or install-test container. Package jobs run only in a vergil package toolchain image, prod-pkg-ubuntu or prod-pkg-rhel, built by vergil-containers (epic vergil-project/.github#607). The image ships the OS prerequisites, uv and nFPM preinstalled, but no Python and no vergil-tooling. The container must run as root (the GitHub Actions container default).

This action is wired automatically into the build and install-test jobs of ci-package.yml and the package-build jobs of cd-release.yml. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/package/setup@v2.1
  with:
    nfpm: "true"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description nfpm "false" Require nFPM in the toolchain image. Build cells pass "true"; install-test cells leave it off. python "3.15" Python version for the driver vergil-tooling, uv-managed. It is the only place the version is written: the install step passes it to uv tool install --python (with --managed-python) and to detect.sh as VRG_DRIVER_PYTHON.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Check the toolchain image. check-toolchain.sh checks the image against its marker file, /etc/vergil/package-toolchain (with --nfpm when nfpm: "true"). The step then adds the workspace to git's safe.directory.
  2. Install vergil-tooling. detect.sh resolves the install spec. In vergil-tooling itself it is the checkout, so CI exercises the PR's own vrg-package. Elsewhere it reads [dependencies].vergil from vergil.toml with uv run --no-config under a uv-managed Python of the python input's version, then:
    • A line pin vX.Y resolves to the newest vX.Y.Z tag, never the moving vX.Y tag. An exact pin vX.Y.Z is that tag. Either way, one git ls-remote resolves the tag to its commit SHA, and everything after uses that SHA. The spec is vergil-tooling @ git+https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-tooling@<sha>. detect.sh fetches that commit alone over git and exports its uv.lock (uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes) as the install's constraints. The step logs the tag and the SHA.
    • Any other ref is a dev ref. It installs as written, with no constraints.

A failed ls-remote, a line with no release tag, a failed fetch or export, or a commit with no uv.lock fails the job with a named error. It never falls back to an older or unconstrained install. detect.sh also fails if VRG_DRIVER_PYTHON is unset or empty; there is no default.

The install is uv tool install --force --no-config --python <python> --managed-python, with --constraints for a released ref. It runs with UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE and UV_NO_MANAGED_PYTHON unset. --no-config ignores the repository's uv settings ([tool.uv], uv.toml), so settings such as python-downloads = "manual" cannot stop the download. The cleared variables mean the job's env cannot pick another interpreter either. The tools land in uv's tool bin directory under $HOME, never in /usr/local/bin. That way install-test smoke checks, which run with a system-only PATH, cannot resolve this copy. The step then checks that vrg-whoami resolves to that directory and runs, and that vrg-package runs.

The action installs no OS packages, uv or nFPM itself. A job in a raw ubuntu or UBI image fails at the first step:

::error::package jobs require a vergil package toolchain image; /etc/vergil/package-toolchain not found

docs.title: The marker contract
docs.text:
The image writes one <tool> <version> line per tool, separated by a single space. <tool> is a command name. <version> is the first [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+ token of the standard output of <tool> --version. The marker always lists uv, nfpm, curl, git, gpg, tar and gzip:

uv 0.13.9
nfpm 2.47.0
curl 8.5.0
git 2.43.0
gpg 2.4.4
tar 1.35
gzip 1.12

check-toolchain.sh passes only when the marker lists uv, curl, git, gpg, tar and gzip, every listed tool is on PATH at its listed version and, with --nfpm, the marker lists nfpm. nfpm is required only with --nfpm, since install-test cells need no nFPM. The script never falls back to installing anything. It fails the job with one ::error:: line per problem, after checking every line, if the marker is missing, leaves out a required tool, or lists a tool that is missing, at another version, or prints no version. It also fails if nfpm is needed but not listed, or if the marker is empty, malformed or lists a tool twice.

actions/package/setup/tests/check-toolchain.test.sh exercises the script against fixture markers (VRG_TOOLCHAIN_MARKER) and stub tools, with no root and no container. The Smoke - setup/vergil outputs workflow runs it on every PR that touches this action.

docs.title: apt behaviour
docs.text: The apt mirror list and the fail-fast apt config (/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-vergil-fast-fail), on both architectures, are part of the prod-pkg-ubuntu image, so every apt call vergil-tooling makes during build and install-test inherits them. vergil-containers writes them, and checks them when it builds the image.

docs.title: Job timeouts and the runner host
docs.text: package-sign in cd-release.yml installs rpm and gnupg on the runner host itself, not in a container. It passes fail-fast options on the command line (-o Acquire::Retries=3 -o Acquire::Retries::Delay=false -o Acquire::http::Timeout=20 -o Acquire::https::Timeout=20 -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60). Acquire::Retries::Delay "false" avoids an apt 2.4 to 2.8 deadlock after a mirror failover, in which the timeouts never fire (LP #2003851). Every package job also sets timeout-minutes as a backstop: matrix 5, build 30, install-test 15 and evidence 5 in ci-package.yml, and package-matrix 5, package-build 30 and package-sign 15 in cd-release.yml.

docs.title: publish/index/live-check
docs.text:
Proves that GitHub Pages serves the package index the current run built. Pages can report a deployment success, and mark it active, while its origin goes on serving the previous deployment (vergil-project/packages#46). Without this check the fault surfaced only an hour later, in vrg-release's package-index stage.

This action is wired automatically into both jobs of publish-index.yml. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# build-index, after `vrg-package index --out _site`
- id: manifest
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/publish/index/live-check@v2.1
  with:
    mode: manifest
    site: _site

# deploy, after actions/deploy-pages
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/publish/index/live-check@v2.1
  with:
    mode: verify
    base-url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    manifest: ${{ needs.build-index.outputs.index-manifest }}

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description mode (required) manifest or verify. Any other value fails. site _site manifest: the built site directory. base-url "" verify: the deployed site's base URL, the page_url output of actions/deploy-pages. An empty value fails. manifest "" verify: the manifest output of a mode: manifest run. attempts "30" verify: rounds of fetches before failing. interval "10" verify: seconds between rounds.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description manifest manifest: one <sha256> <path> line per signed InRelease and per repomd.xml in the site, with the path relative to the site root.

docs.title: What identifies the built index
docs.text: The manifest holds the sha256 of every deb/dists/<suite>/InRelease and every rpm/<el>/<arch>/repodata/repomd.xml. Each InRelease is signed at build time and carries the build's Date: line, so no two builds share one. The manifest step fails if the site holds no InRelease, since nothing would then identify the build.

docs.title: The verify loop
docs.text:
Each round fetches every file not yet confirmed live from <base-url>/<path>?vrg-live-check=<time>-<round>-<random>, sending Cache-Control: no-cache and Pragma: no-cache. A file is live once it is served with HTTP 200 and its manifest digest. The step passes as soon as all files are live. A fetch error, a non-200 status or a wrong digest is retried until the window runs out: 30 rounds 10 seconds apart, about five minutes. The step then prints one ::error:: per file still wrong. Each one names the deployment (repository, run ID and attempt), the URL, the expected digest and what was served, with its HTTP status, digest, Last-Modified and X-Cache. A final ::error:: says Pages is likely serving an older deployment and recommends a re-run, or a GitHub Support ticket if the fault repeats.

A malformed or empty manifest, a path containing .., or a bad attempts or interval value fails at once, before any fetch.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: tests/live-check.test.sh is a framework-free harness that runs the script against a fake curl and sleep. It covers the manifest, every verify outcome, cache busting and the wiring in publish-index.yml. The smoke-publish-index workflow runs it on pull requests.

docs.title: shared/docs/stage
docs.text:
Stages the changelog and release-notes pages into the MkDocs source tree and patches the MkDocs nav with the release versions. ci-docs (the PR-time strict build) and cd-docs (the post-merge deploy) both run this action, so they build the docs from the same source tree: a green docs / docs check predicts a green docs deploy.

This action is wired automatically into ci-docs and cd-docs. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0

- name: Install vergil-tooling
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1

- name: Stage documentation sources
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/docs/stage@v2.1
  env:
    VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS: ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }}
  with:
    mkdocs-config: docs/site/mkdocs.yml

The action needs vergil-tooling on PATH and a checkout with full history (fetch-depth: 0), because the staging reads git tags. It also needs VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS set from ${{ vars.VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS }} in the calling step's env: a composite action cannot read vars, and vergil-tooling stops when the variable is missing or invalid (see Variables).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Required Default Description mkdocs-config No docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to the MkDocs configuration file. The docs directory is taken to be docs/ next to it.

The action has no outputs.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
1. Mark the workspace safe for git. Runs git config --global --add safe.directory '*', because inside a container the workspace is owned by a different UID than the user git runs as.
  2. Stage the changelog and release notes. Runs vrg-docs-stage --docs-dir <docs-dir>. It links each release page to that release's CI-evidence bundle with gh release view, so the step sets GH_TOKEN to the workflow's github.token.
  3. Patch the nav. Runs vrg-docs-patch-nav against the MkDocs config and <docs-dir>/releases, adding the release versions to the nav.

Both steps edit the working tree only; nothing is committed or pushed.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: • contents: read (enough for gh release view on the repository's own releases)

docs.title: security/trivy
docs.text: Runs Trivy vulnerability scanning, SBOM generation, or container image scanning.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/security/trivy@v2.1
  with:
    scan-type: fs
    scan-ref: "."
    severity: "CRITICAL,HIGH"
    exit-code: "1"
    scanners: "vuln"
    output-file: "trivy-results.sarif"

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Name Required Default Description scan-type Yes — Scan mode: fs (filesystem vuln scan to SARIF), sbom (CycloneDX SBOM generation), or image (container image scan to SARIF). scan-ref No . Filesystem path or container image reference to scan. severity No CRITICAL,HIGH Comma-separated severity levels to report. exit-code No 1 Exit code when vulnerabilities are found (0 = advisory only). scanners No vuln Comma-separated Trivy scanners to enable. output-file No trivy-results.sarif Output file path for SARIF or SBOM results. sarif-category No "" Category for SARIF upload. Use unique values when multiple matrix entries upload SARIF to avoid overwrites. Defaults to trivy-fs or trivy-image based on scan-type. trivyignores No "" Comma-separated list of .trivyignore file paths. trivy-image No aquasec/trivy:0.70.0 Docker image to use for Trivy. Override to pin a specific version.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description result Outcome of an fs or image scan: passed, findings or error (see Scan outcomes and retry). Empty for sbom.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• security-events: write (required for SARIF upload when scan-type is fs or image)
  • contents: read

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs Trivy via Docker (docker run) rather than the aquasecurity/trivy-action GitHub Action. Each scan mode uses a single Docker session that scans once to JSON, then converts to both table output (stdout) and SARIF (file). The trivy convert step operates on cached JSON with no re-scan or extra DB download.

The fs and image vuln scans skip pip's vendored CycloneDX SBOM (**/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json, shipped by pip 26.x). Trivy would otherwise ingest that SBOM and report pip's vendored dependencies (e.g. setuptools, msgpack) as findings even though they are pip internals, not the scan target's attack surface. The sbom mode does not skip it — an SBOM should describe everything present.

docs.title: Scan outcomes and retry
docs.text:
The fs and image scans run through scan.sh, which tells three outcomes apart by whether the scan wrote its SARIF report:

result When Step passed The report was written and the scan exited 0. Passes. findings The report was written and the scan exited non-zero: Trivy found vulnerabilities at severity after the ignore files. Fails with Trivy found <severity> vulnerabilities in <scan-ref>, using the exit-code input. Not retried. error No attempt wrote a report: Trivy stopped before it could report, for example on a dropped image-layer download or a failed vulnerability-DB download. Fails with Trivy scan errored (no report produced) for <scan-ref>.

A scan that writes no report is retried up to two more times (three attempts, waiting 15s and then 30s), since those download errors are usually transient. Any stale report is deleted before each attempt, so it cannot stand in for a scan that errored. A scan that never wrote a report never passes, even with exit-code: "0". When there is no report, the SARIF upload is skipped rather than failing a second time on the missing file.

Callers that gate on the step outcome (with continue-on-error: true) can read the result output to word their own failure message.

actions/shared/security/trivy/tests/scan.test.sh tests these outcomes and the retry against a stub docker; the smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs it.

docs.title: Filesystem scan (fs)
docs.text:
1. Runs trivy fs inside the Trivy Docker container against the specified scan-ref.
  2. Outputs results as a table to stdout and in SARIF format to the output file.
  3. Filters accepted-suppressed results into a *.upload.sarif copy with vrg-sarif-filter and uploads that copy to GitHub code scanning (category: trivy-fs or custom sarif-category).

docs.title: Image scan (image)
docs.text:
1. Runs trivy image inside the Trivy Docker container against the specified image reference (with Docker socket mounted).
  2. Outputs results as a table to stdout and in SARIF format to the output file.
  3. Filters accepted-suppressed results into a *.upload.sarif copy with vrg-sarif-filter and uploads that copy to GitHub code scanning (category: trivy-image or custom sarif-category).

docs.title: SBOM generation (sbom)
docs.text:
1. Runs trivy fs with --format cyclonedx inside the Trivy Docker container.
  2. Outputs the SBOM to the specified output file. No SARIF upload.

docs.title: Filesystem vulnerability scan
docs.text:
jobs:
  trivy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/security/trivy@v2.1
        with:
          scan-type: fs

docs.title: Container image scan
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/security/trivy@v2.1
  with:
    scan-type: image
    scan-ref: "myapp:latest"

docs.title: SBOM generation (advisory only)
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/security/trivy@v2.1
  with:
    scan-type: sbom
    output-file: sbom.cdx.json

docs.title: Custom SARIF category for matrix builds
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/security/trivy@v2.1
  with:
    scan-type: fs
    sarif-category: "trivy-fs-${{ matrix.target }}"

docs.title: GitHub configuration
docs.text:
• GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) — Must be enabled for SARIF upload (fs and image scan types). It is available by default on public repositories.
  • Code scanning alerts — Results appear in Security > Code scanning alerts with categories trivy-fs or trivy-image.

docs.title: shared/setup/build-command
docs.text:
Runs the command a repository declares under [container].build-command in its vergil.toml, so that CI test jobs perform the same build step as the local dev container before the tests run.

This action is wired automatically into the ci-test reusable workflow — consuming repositories do not add it themselves. It is documented here for operators who need to understand what the step does and why a test job might fail inside it.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/build-command@v2.1

The action takes no inputs. It requires vergil-tooling to be on PATH (installed by the preceding shared/setup/vergil step in the ci-test workflow), because it reads the command through vrg-container-build-command.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs a single step, install.sh, which:

  1. Reads the command from vrg-container-build-command --script. This is the single speller shared with the local dev-container cache build, so CI and the dev container run the exact same build command — there is no second place the command is spelled out.
  2. If the repository declares no [container].build-command, the script prints No [container].build-command declared; skipping. and exits 0. The step is a no-op for repositories that need no build step.
  3. Otherwise it runs the command via bash -c.
  4. After the command runs, it exports NODE_PATH (the npm global root, from npm root -g) to $GITHUB_ENV so the subsequent CI test steps can resolve a node library the build-command baked out-of-workspace (e.g. npm install -g <lib>). This mirrors the NODE_PATH the local dev image injects (vergil-tooling#2781), so a baked library resolves identically locally and in CI — the local/CI drift this epic exists to prevent. The export is guarded on CI context ($GITHUB_ENV present) and npm being installed, so it is a clean no-op on a non-CI or non-node run.

require-only caveat. NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require resolution only; ESM import ignores it. A baked library consumed via import will not resolve through NODE_PATH — this is a documented Node limitation, not an action bug.

docs.title: Fail-closed, no retry
docs.text:
Unlike the sibling shared/setup/system-packages action — whose bounded retry absorbs a transient apt mirror flake — this action does not retry. An arbitrary build command that fails is a real failure, not a transient one, so retrying it would mask a genuine break. The step is fail-closed: if the command exits non-zero, the step exits non-zero and the test job fails. Nothing is silently skipped.

The logic lives in install.sh (not inline YAML) so it is unit-testable; see actions/shared/setup/build-command/tests/install.test.sh. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: Test-runtime scope only
docs.text: This action runs a test-runtime build step. It is wired only onto jobs that execute the repository's tests — never onto lint or typecheck jobs, which do not exercise the code and so do not need the build output. It runs after Install vergil-tooling and after the system-packages install, before the tests. See the ci-test workflow reference for where it sits in the job graph.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The command is declared by the consuming repository in its vergil.toml under [container].build-command. That key — its schema, semantics, and the dev-container side of its effect — is documented on the vergil-tooling side:

  • container-config reference (build-command)

This page covers only the vergil-actions CI side: which jobs run the build step and how the step behaves.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ci-test reusable workflow — runs the declared build-command on test jobs only.
  • shared/setup/system-packages — the sibling install step (bounded retry) that runs immediately before this one.
  • Repository Configuration — repository-level GitHub configuration overview.

docs.title: shared/setup/primary-suffix
docs.text:
Picks the image suffix of a single-container job from the resolver's answer: the primary version's entry in the setup action's container-suffixes output. With the resolver's primary-container-tag, the job's image is the one CI's primary leg runs on, for example prod-cpp-clang:20 for clang-20.

This action is wired automatically into the setup jobs of ci-quality (for the common and custom jobs), ci-version-bump (for the version-bump job) and cd-release (for the release job). Consuming repositories do not add it themselves.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- name: Resolve the primary version with vrg-ci-resolve
  id: derive
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1

- name: Resolve primary-container-suffix
  id: suffix
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/primary-suffix@v2.1
  with:
    primary-version: ${{ steps.derive.outputs.primary-version }}
    container-suffixes: ${{ steps.derive.outputs.container-suffixes }}
    container-suffix: ${{ inputs.container-suffix }}

The action needs jq on PATH.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description primary-version Yes The setup action's primary-version output. container-suffixes Yes The setup action's container-suffixes output: a JSON object mapping each resolved version to its image suffix. container-suffix No "" The calling workflow's container-suffix, as a cross-check only. It never changes the output.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description primary-container-suffix The primary version's image suffix (e.g. cpp-clang, ts-node, python, base).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The step fails with an ::error:: annotation when:

  • primary-version or container-suffixes is empty;
  • container-suffixes is not a JSON object, or has no suffix for the primary version;
  • container-suffix is set and does not equal the primary version's suffix. The calling workflow (ci.yml or cd.yml) and vergil.toml ([project].primary-language, [ci]) disagree on the language, and a job on the wrong image could check, build or publish the wrong thing.

Unlike ci/matrix, which accepts any resolved suffix because it runs every version, these jobs run only on the primary version, so the caller's suffix must be the primary version's.

docs.title: shared/setup/system-packages
docs.text:
Installs the Ubuntu packages a repository declares under [container].system-packages in its vergil.toml, so that CI test jobs run against the same system dependencies as the local dev container.

This action is wired automatically into the ci-test reusable workflow — consuming repositories do not add it themselves. It is documented here for operators who need to understand what the step does and why a test job might fail inside it.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/system-packages@v2.1

The action takes no inputs. It requires vergil-tooling to be on PATH (installed by the preceding shared/setup/vergil step in the ci-test workflow), because it reads the package list through vrg-container-system-packages.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs a single step, install.sh, which:

  1. Reads the apt install snippet from vrg-container-system-packages --install-script. This is the single speller shared with the local dev-container cache build, so CI and the dev container install the exact same packages the same way — there is no second place a package list is spelled out.
  2. If the repository declares no [container].system-packages, the script prints No [container].system-packages declared; skipping. and exits 0. The step is a no-op for repositories that need no extra system packages.
  3. Otherwise it runs the install snippet with a bounded retry (3 attempts by default, with a delay between attempts) so a transient apt mirror flake does not fail the job.
  4. Fail-closed on a missing candidate. If a declared package genuinely has no install candidate, the retries are exhausted and the step exits non-zero with the speller's own "not installable" message — naming the offending package and the platform — still visible in the log. Nothing is silently skipped: an unresolvable package fails the test job rather than letting the tests run against a missing dependency.

The retry and fail-closed logic lives in install.sh (not inline YAML) so it is unit-testable; see actions/shared/setup/system-packages/tests/install.test.sh. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs the tests.

docs.title: Test-runtime scope only
docs.text: This action installs test-runtime dependencies. It is wired only onto jobs that execute the repository's tests — never onto lint or typecheck jobs, which do not exercise the code and so do not need its system dependencies. See the ci-test workflow reference for where it sits in the job graph.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The package list is declared by the consuming repository in its vergil.toml under [container].system-packages. That key — its schema, semantics, and the dev-container side of its effect — is documented on the vergil-tooling side:

  • container-config reference (system-packages)

This page covers only the vergil-actions CI side: which jobs run the install step and how the step behaves.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ci-test reusable workflow — installs declared system packages on test jobs only.
  • shared/setup/build-command — the sibling build step (fail-closed, no retry) that runs immediately after this one.
  • Repository Configuration — repository-level GitHub configuration overview.

docs.title: shared/setup/vergil
docs.text:
Installs vergil-tooling at the version the repository pins in vergil.toml, then resolves the repository's CI version set by calling vrg-ci-resolve, the single resolver that ships with it. Reusable workflows read their version matrix and container tags from this action's outputs instead of from hard-coded inputs.

This action is wired automatically into the reusable workflows: every job that runs a vrg-* command, and the matrix and setup jobs that resolve the version set. Consuming repositories do not add it themselves. It is documented here for operators who need to understand what the step does and why a job might fail inside it.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6

- name: Install vergil-tooling
  id: setup
  uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/actions/shared/setup/vergil@v2.1

The repository must be checked out first: the action reads vergil.toml (and, to detect vergil-tooling itself, pyproject.toml) from the working directory.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description install-source No auto auto or git. Both install vergil-tooling the same way, with uv tool install from git (below); neither touches the vergil apt repository. git stays for the callers that set it, such as publish-index's build-index job, which rebuilds that repository's index. Any other value fails the job. version-window No "" Path to a local window.json for the resolver to read instead of the published window. When set, the Derive step exports it as VRG_VERSION_WINDOW, the resolver's one sanctioned override. For tests only: leave it empty in real workflows.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Description versions The resolved versions, newest first, as a compact JSON array string, e.g. ["3.14","3.13","3.12"]. The matrix job passes it to ci/matrix to fan out per-version legs. primary-version [ci].primary-version when it is set; otherwise the newest resolved version. primary-container-tag The resolver's image tag for the primary version (clang-20 has tag 20, node-24 has 24, 3.14 has 3.14). Used by the single-container common and custom jobs in ci-quality, the version-bump job in ci-version-bump and the release job in cd-release. container-tags Compact JSON object mapping each resolved version to its image tag, e.g. {"clang-20":"20","gcc-14":"14"}. Passed to ci/matrix. container-suffixes Compact JSON object mapping each resolved version to its image suffix, e.g. {"clang-20":"cpp-clang","gcc-14":"cpp-gcc"}. Passed to ci/matrix, and to shared/setup/primary-suffix for the single-container jobs' image suffix. build-enabled true when vergil-tooling turns the BUILD check on for the repository's language (vrg-ci-resolve's build-enabled), else false. A vergil-tooling release older than the field gives false, with a notice; any value other than true or false fails the step. ci-quality's matrix job passes it on, and its build job runs only when it is true.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The action runs these steps in order:

  1. Mark the workspace safe for git. Adds the workspace to git's safe.directory list, because inside a container the workspace is owned by a different UID than the user git runs as.

  2. Install vergil-tooling. install-tooling.sh installs it with uv tool install from git, logs what it installs (each log line starts vergil-tooling:), and fails the job when any step fails. Nothing reads the vergil package repository, and nothing falls back after a failure.

    • If pyproject.toml declares name = "vergil-tooling", the repository is vergil-tooling itself. The step runs uv sync --frozen --group dev and adds .venv/bin to PATH, so CI tests the PR's own code rather than a released version. On a host runner the sync names --python 3.15, the one Python series vergil-tooling supports, and uv provides that interpreter. In a container job it runs with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system, so it uses the image's interpreter and never downloads a managed one (issue #1002). uv tool install needs no such pin, because uv tool commands ignore a project's uv settings.
    • Otherwise it reads [dependencies].vergil from vergil.toml (e.g. v2.1) and installs vergil-tooling at that ref, the same way on a host runner and in a container job:
      • A released ref, a line (vX.Y) or an exact release (vX.Y.Z), is resolved to one commit with a single git ls-remote of the vergil-tooling repository. A line resolves to its newest vX.Y.Z tag, never the floating vX.Y tag, so a pin never installs an older release; an exact pin to that tag. The commit is the tag's peeled commit. The log names the tag and the SHA, for example vergil-tooling: v2.1 resolves to v2.1.327 at <sha>, with the full 40-character SHA. From then on only the SHA is used: the step fetches that commit alone over git, exports its uv.lock (uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes) as constraints, and runs uv tool install --force --no-config --python 3.15 --managed-python -c <constraints> 'vergil-tooling @ git+https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-tooling@<sha>'. A failed tag lookup, a line with no vX.Y.Z tag, a missing exact tag, a failed commit fetch or lock export, constraints that name vergil-tooling itself or an editable install, and a failed install each fail the job with an ::error:: naming the ref or commit and the step. Nothing installs unconstrained.
      • A dev ref (anything but vX.Y or vX.Y.Z, such as develop): uv tool install --force --no-config --python 3.15 --managed-python from git at that ref, with no constraints.

    Every install, and the lock export, runs with --no-config, so no uv.toml or [tool.uv] in the repository, and no user uv config, can change or block it, and with the job's UV_PYTHON, UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE and UV_NO_MANAGED_PYTHON unset, so it always runs on a uv-managed Python 3.15, never a family image's or the runner's interpreter. The variables are cleared for this step's uv commands only.

    Where the Python comes from: - VERGIL_CORE_PYTHON_DIR set (a Vergil image publishes its managed Python's directory there): the install uses that directory as UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR with UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never, so it never downloads an interpreter. A path that is not a directory, or one without a managed 3.15, fails the job instead of downloading. - Not set (a host runner, an image older than the managed core Python, or a non-Vergil image): uv may download its managed 3.15, and the step logs vergil-tooling: no VERGIL_CORE_PYTHON_DIR; uv may download 3.15.

    After the install, the vrg-* commands are in uv's tool bin directory (uv tool dir --bin, usually ~/.local/bin), which is added to PATH for later steps. vrg-whoami must resolve to that directory and run; otherwise the job fails, so a stale copy that would answer in its place (such as an old packaged /usr/bin/vrg-whoami) is caught. The tool environment's interpreter must also be a released Python 3.15 (python --version prints Python 3.15.N), and the step logs it, for example vergil-tooling: vergil-tooling runs on Python 3.15.2 (<path>). A pre-release such as 3.15.0rc3, or another series, fails the job. The self repo's host sync is checked the same way.

    A path that needs uv and finds none on PATH installs uv from its release tarball at the version and SHA-256 pinned in install-tooling.sh, into $RUNNER_TEMP/uv/bin, and adds that to PATH. uv is never installed with pip. The pinned uv's managed-Python list must offer a released 3.15: uv 0.12.23 resolved --python 3.15 to 3.15.0rc3 (issue #1331), which the interpreter check now catches.

    The tag is read by read-pin.sh, which fails the job with a single ::error:: annotation naming the file or key, and nothing is installed, when: - vergil.toml does not exist (usually because the repository was not checked out first); - vergil.toml is not valid TOML (the annotation includes the parse error); - there is no [dependencies] table, or dependencies is not a table; - [dependencies] has no vergil key; - [dependencies].vergil is not a string, or is empty or blank.

    Apart from the TOML parse error, each annotation says what to add: a pin such as

    [dependencies]
vergil = "v2.1"

  3. Derive the CI versions. Runs derive.sh, which calls vrg-ci-resolve --format json once and writes its answer to the five outputs. The resolution itself is not done here: the resolver reads vergil.toml and the language version window that vergil-containers publishes at the [dependencies].vergil ref, and applies the rules:

    • repository-type = "library" builds the whole window; every other type resolves as an app, which builds exactly one version: the newest, or its single [ci].versions pin;
    • a language whose window has more than one family must pin [ci].versions, since there is no single default: today only C++ (clang-/gcc-). A family prefix alone (TypeScript's node-24) needs no pin;
    • a packaged Python app ([package].builder = "python") builds the newest version that has a published vergil-python runtime; a packaged library keeps the whole window (only its deployed runtime needs a published package);
    • a [ci].versions pin must lie inside the window, and an app's pin must name one version;
    • [ci].primary-version must name a resolved version; without it the primary is the newest resolved version;
    • a repository with no [project].primary-language builds latest on the base image.

Any resolver failure fails the job, and every line of the resolver's message becomes an ::error:: annotation.
