docs.text:
• add reusable ops-epic-sweep reconciliation workflow (#742)
  • feat(workflows): add reusable ops-epic-sweep reconciliation workflow

Reusable workflow (on: workflow_call) that runs vrg-epic-audit --close to reconcile epic/task drift — catching any epic/task that missed its event-driven close. Mints an org-wide app token (no repositories input) since the sweep closes drifted tasks across code repos and rolled-up epics in .github; sets VRG_EPIC_SWEEP=1 to authorize the automated close (vergil-tooling #2104). A scheduled caller per org (task #2105) drives it. Part of epic vergil-project/.github#80.

  • fix(workflows): pass window-days via env to avoid semgrep run-shell-injection

The semgrep run-shell-injection rule flags interpolating a workflow_call input directly in a run: step (caller-controlled). Move inputs.window-days into a WINDOW_DAYS env var and reference "$WINDOW_DAYS" in the shell, per the rule's remediation. Part of epic vergil-project/.github#80.

docs.title: Chores
docs.text: • retire standards-compliance linkage gate (#747) PR-linkage is now guaranteed at PR-body construction in vergil-tooling (epic vergil-project/.github#82), so the standards job and its vrg-pr-issue-linkage action are removed. run-standards, container-suffix, and container-tag are kept as accepted-but-ignored inputs (marked deprecated) so no consumer's reusable-workflow call breaks; removing the inputs is a separate coordinated follow-up. Ref #746

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • fully-qualify the nested cd-docs reusable ref (#751) (#752) cd-docs-refresh is a reusable workflow called cross-repo, but it nested cd-docs.yml via a relative './.github/workflows/cd-docs.yml' — which does not resolve when the outer workflow is invoked from another repo via a tag (GitHub reports 'workflow was not found'), and which vrg-freeze-refs never pins. Make it a fully-qualified '@develop' ref so it resolves cross-repo and the release freeze rewrites it to the release tag. Fixes the org docs repos' daily cd-docs-refresh startup failure.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• key first-release no-op off release tags, not missing main (#758) The version-divergence gate's first-release escape hatch guarded the wrong condition: it keyed off a missing origin/main. But the bootstrap wizard creates and pushes main at init, so main always exists on a brand-new repo, making the hatch unreachable. Every release-bearing repo's first PR into develop then hard-failed the gate with 'version not bumped: head (0.1.0) == main (0.1.0)' — there was no way to satisfy it, since nothing had been released.

Detect the first release from the real signal instead: the absence of a release tag. tag-and-release stamps every release with a vX.Y.Z tag, so no such tag means no release has occurred. This distinguishes the two EQUAL cases exactly — bootstrap (no tag) passes; a genuine missed bump after a prior release (tag exists) still fails — regardless of whether main exists. The fetch and compare steps now run only once a release exists.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• codify the all-hard-gates principle (#765)
  • docs(ci): codify the all-hard-gates principle

Add a foundational-principles doc to the CI Gate Requirements section stating that every check that matters is a hard, asserting gate — there are no report-only or warning gates, because an unheeded warning is meaningless (reviewers optimize for can-I-merge and never revisit warnings). Deprecation warnings are treated as errors (early signal of a future outage), and the sprawling warning-exception list is rejected: if it matters, assert it and fail on it.

Cross-references the CI-evidence publish-safety property (epic vergil-project/.github#140 spec §9.1), which depends on this principle. Wired into the mkdocs nav and the ci-gates section index.

Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#763

  • docs(ci): distinguish gate deployment lifecycle from soft gates

Add a gate-deployment-lifecycle section to the all-hard-gates doc reconciling the all-hard-gates principle with staged rollout. All gates are hard as a permanent configuration — a permanent soft gate does not exist — but deploying a new hard gate is a lifecycle: it first runs in warning mode (reports, does not fail) for a bounded bake-in period to collect reliability data, then is promoted to enforcing (fatal) once proven stable.

Warning mode is a transient deployment state of a hard gate, never a permanent soft gate; the end state of every gate is always enforcing. Uses the CI-evidence gate (epic vergil-project/.github#140) as the concrete example: warning mode first, bake across release cadence, single flag flip to enforcing. This refines rather than contradicts the existing content — the unheeded-warning anti-pattern is the permanent report-only case, not the time-boxed, owned, promotion-committed deployment stage.

Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#763

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• emit ci-evidence- artifacts from gate workflows (#764) Add a shared actions/ci/evidence/emit composite that writes an evidence.json fragment ({gate, tools, metrics, files}) and uploads it, together with any available report files, as a ci-evidence- workflow-run artifact for the release-time harvester (vrg-ci-evidence).

    Wire it into all four required gate workflows via a dedicated needs-gated evidence job so the artifact's presence is itself proof the gate passed, and so each gate emits exactly one artifact despite its matrix/multi-job structure (upload-artifact forbids same-name uploads across jobs):

    • ci-test, ci-audit, ci-quality: one evidence job that runs after the gate's check jobs succeed.
    • ci-security: each scanner (codeql, trivy, semgrep) uploads its SARIF as an evidence partial UNCONDITIONALLY (independent of the code-scanning upload), and a consolidation job merges the partials into the single ci-evidence-security artifact. This lets the harvester read artifacts only, with no code-scanning API dependency (spec section 7).

    Report-file globs (coverage.xml, junit.xml, pip-audit.json, licenses.json) are forward-compatible: they are skipped until the check commands emit them, so test/audit/quality currently produce an evidence.json-only artifact, which is sufficient for completeness.

    Task T8 of epic vergil-project/.github#140.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • pass GH_TOKEN to the docs stage step so evidence links resolve (#772) The 'Stage changelog and release notes' step runs vrg-docs-stage, which links each release page to its CI-evidence bundle via 'gh release view'. Its env block set only MKDOCS_CONFIG, so gh was unauthenticated and the docs job failed. Wire GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} into the same env block; both docs workflows already grant the required contents permission. The nav-patch step (vrg-docs-patch-nav) makes no gh calls and is unchanged. Ref #770

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• harvest, attest, and attach CI evidence (warning mode) (#771) Add the actions/cd/release/ci-evidence composite and wire it as the first publish step of cd-release.yml (evidence-first, spec §9). Ships in WARNING mode (spec §9.2): non-fatal and timeout-bounded so it can never abort a release; promotion to enforcing (Task T11) is a single flip of the evidence-enforce default.

The composite runs vrg-ci-evidence bundle (bounded by the coreutils timeout command, since composite steps cannot use timeout-minutes), attests the bundle digest via actions/attest-build-provenance, and attaches the tarball plus manifest with gh release upload --clobber. Bundle and upload are bash steps that capture the exit code under set +e and, in warning mode, convert any failure or timeout into a ::warning:: and exit 0. The attest step is a uses step that a composite cannot wrap, so the call-site continue-on-error tracks evidence-enforce, keeping warning mode non-aborting even on a rare attest failure.

Add actions: read to the cd-release job permissions so the harvest can list and download the release PR's ci-evidence-* artifacts (spec §5.2); the consuming repo's cd.yml must grant the same scope.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• split cd-release evidence into pre-publish gate + post-release attach (#777) T9 (#769) ran the whole CI-evidence step first, but two things it needs are created later in the same job: the GitHub Release (gh release upload's target, created by tag-and-release) and the SBOM (built by registry-publish). So in warning mode the upload warned and attached nothing, and the bundle omitted the SBOM. Split the single ci-evidence composite in two:

  • ci-evidence-gate (stays first, pre-publish): resolve the release PR, harvest the required gate evidence, and validate completeness. Once enforcing, incomplete evidence fails here before anything is published (spec §9).

  • ci-evidence-attach (new, after tag-and-release): assemble the complete bundle now including the built SBOM, attest it, and upload it to the Release that now exists.

Both composites invoke the existing vrg-ci-evidence bundle CLI and keep the warning-mode contract: set +e captures the exit code so any failure/timeout becomes a ::warning:: and exits 0, and the call-site continue-on-error tracks evidence-enforce so even the uses: attest step cannot abort the release. Promotion to enforcing (T11) stays a pure flip of the evidence-enforce default, which flips both steps' fatality and both continue-on-error guards at once.

docs.title: Refactoring
docs.text:
• share one harvest across evidence gate and attach (#782) Rewire the cd-release CI-evidence gate and attach composites to share a single artifact harvest instead of each running the atomic bundle (which re-downloaded the release PR's artifacts).

The gate now calls vrg-ci-evidence harvest (network download + validate_completeness gate), persisting the downloaded evidence and harvest-state.json into a shared staging dir on the job workspace (${{ github.workspace }}/.ci-evidence-staging). The attach now calls vrg-ci-evidence assemble --staging <same-dir>, which is fully network-free and produces the tarball + standalone manifest offline. Both composites run in the same cd-release job, so the workspace filesystem persists between them and the release's artifacts are downloaded exactly once.

Warning-mode wrappers and the enforce flag are preserved exactly in both steps; the attest and gh release upload steps are unchanged. Part 2 of the double-harvest fix (Part 1 is the vergil-tooling CLI split, #2330).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • explicit CD secrets and semgrep rule-exclusion docs (#788) Document vrg-semgrep-scan's repeatable --exclude-rule flag, the additive DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_RULES fleet baseline, and the temporary fleet-wide github-actions-mutable-action-tag exemption pending vergil-project/.github#194 (with our own @v2.1 refs as a permanent exception). Document that cd-release callers forward explicit least-privilege publishing secrets per ecosystem instead of blanket secrets: inherit; generated cd.yml emits an explicit secrets block or none accordingly.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• route C++ CI to compiler-family images with per-kind cardinality (#793) Extend the reusable ci-*.yml workflows to accept language: cpp and run the C++ pipeline per compiler-family image.

A new actions/ci/matrix composite action resolves the per-version job matrix from the flat versions input: for cpp it splits each clang-/gcc- token and routes it to prod-cpp-clang: / prod-cpp-gcc:, and it emits an 'all' matrix (per-version) plus a 'once' matrix collapsed to the primary version. ci-quality/ci-test/ci-audit gain a matrix prep job and consume all (typecheck, unit) or once (lint, dependencies) so the emitted job/gate names line up exactly with github_config.desired_ci_gates_ruleset for a cpp repo: per-version typecheck/test, run-once lint/audit keyed to the primary clang tag. Non-cpp languages resolve byte-identical images and keep per-version cardinality.

ci-security wires Semgrep p/c and p/cpp for cpp via extra-config (C++ has no single p/ ruleset); CodeQL already forwards the cpp language and cpp is CodeQL-supported. Adds a C++ example to the workflow README.

Ref vergil-project/.github#207

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• gate follows release-model instead of run-release wiring Make ci-version-bump.yml self-guard on the consuming repo's vergil.toml: when release-model is "none" the gate steps do not run and the job passes, so non-releasing repos no longer need to pass run-release: false (the skip escape hatch flagged in #674).

The run-release input is kept for backwards compatibility but is now deprecated: passing false still suppresses the gate and emits a ::warning:: annotation pointing at the calling workflow. Removal is tracked in #688.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• describe dynamic cached-image tooling install CLAUDE.md claimed vergil-tooling CLI tools and validators are pre-installed in the dev container images. The base images contain no vergil-tooling; it is installed dynamically. Rewrite the Environment Setup and Standard-Tooling Integration passages to describe the per-branch cached-image mechanism (vrg-container-run builds :---- with the version pinned in vergil.toml, cache keyed on lockfiles plus vergil.toml) and the CI-side dynamic install via the actions/shared/setup/vergil action. Also fix the stale actions/shared/setup/vergil-tooling path in the action list.

  • replace vrg-docker-run, fix v1.4 pin and pre-installed claim The docs-site and legacy development docs referenced the removed vrg-docker-run command (renamed vrg-container-run), told users to install vergil-tooling@v1.4 (the repo pins v2.1 in vergil.toml), and claimed the dev-base container has every required tool pre-installed. Static linters and docs tools are baked into the base image, but vrg-validate itself arrives via the per-branch cached image that vrg-container-run builds with the vergil.toml-pinned version.

    • Rename the command everywhere (including the CLI-reference link anchor in workflows/index.md), bump the install snippet to v2.1, and rewrite the validation and environment pages to distinguish baked-in tools from the dynamically installed vergil-tooling, matching the corrected CLAUDE.md description from #684.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• skip pip's vendored SBOM in fs/image vuln scans (#798)
  • fix(trivy): skip pip's vendored SBOM in fs/image vuln scans

pip 26.x ships pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json, a CycloneDX SBOM of pip's vendored dependencies. Trivy ingests it and reports those vendored packages (e.g. setuptools 70.3.0, msgpack 1.1.2) as findings even though they are pip internals, not the scan target's attack surface — breaking the docker-publish gate on every pip-bearing image fleet-wide.

Add --skip-files '**/pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json' to the fs and image vuln scans so Trivy no longer parses that SBOM. The sbom generation mode is left untouched (an SBOM should describe everything present).

Verified against the real vergil-containers prod-base image on Trivy 0.71.0 (the action default) and 0.72.0: the skip clears the setuptools and msgpack false positives while every other finding still reports. Lets consumer repos drop their per-image rm workaround (vergil-containers#481).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• wire CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER into ci-audit workflow (#803) Declare the ConanCenter provider token as an optional workflow_call secret in ci-audit.yml and inject it into the dependency-audit step's env: so conan audit can authenticate inside the container. Threaded via the explicit-secret chain (never secrets: inherit, per epics #189/#197).

The token is cpp-only; when the caller leaves it unset the cpp audit path skips the conan gate with a notice rather than failing auth. Documents the caller-side secret passing for cpp repos in the workflows README and ci-audit docs page.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• install declared [container].system-packages on CI test jobs (#808)
  • feat(ci): install declared system-packages on CI test jobs

Add actions/shared/setup/system-packages composite action: reads the declared [container].system-packages via vrg-container-system-packages --install-script and apt-installs them with bounded retry (mirror-flake tolerance) and fail-closed behaviour (a missing candidate exhausts retries and exits non-zero with the speller's package+platform message). The retry/fail-closed loop lives in install.sh so it is unit-testable; action.yml is a thin wrapper. Wired into the unit job of ci-test.yml after Install vergil-tooling — test-runtime only, not lint/typecheck (spec 3.3). Epic vergil-project/.github#272.

  • test(ci): cover system-packages install retry and fail-closed paths

Self-contained, framework-free harness (this repo declares language=shell, which runs no test gate and ships no action-test convention) for install.sh: PATH-stubs vrg-container-system-packages and apt-get to exercise the installable happy path, the fail-closed bogus-package path (non-zero exit with the 'not installable' message), the transient-flake retry-then-success path, and the no-packages skip. Epic vergil-project/.github#272.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• document CI system-packages setup step (#813) Add operator-facing docs for the shared/setup/system-packages composite action and its auto-wiring into the ci-test reusable workflow.

  • New Action Reference page (actions/shared-setup-system-packages.md) with behavior, single-speller apt install, bounded retry, fail-closed on a missing candidate, and test-runtime-only scope; added to the mkdocs nav and the actions index.

  • ci-test workflow reference: note the declared system-packages install on test jobs only (lint/typecheck excluded).
  • configuration.md: cross-reference pointer to the [container].system-packages key's CI effect.

Cross-links to the consuming-repo key docs in vergil-tooling (#2724) rather than restating them. Operator-side companion to vergil-tooling#2724.

Refs vergil-project/.github#272; action #808 (issue #807); issue #812

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• TypeScript support in reusable workflows (#815) Accept language: typescript in the reusable CI workflows.

  • Matrix routing: node- version tokens resolve to prod-ts-node: images (ts-node suffix + numeric tag), mirroring C++ token routing. Extracted the resolver to actions/ci/matrix/resolve.sh with a unit test.

  • Cardinality: TYPECHECK/LINT/AUDIT run once (collapsed to the primary Node version via the matrix once output); only TEST fans out per Node version. The typecheck job now consumes once for TypeScript, matching the run-once gates desired_ci_gates_ruleset keys to ci.versions[0].
  • CodeQL mapping: primary-language typescript maps to javascript-typescript and cpp maps to c-cpp via one table in actions/ci/security/codeql/resolve-language.sh (bare typescript is not a valid CodeQL analysis language). Unit-tested.
  • Semgrep: wire p/typescript for TypeScript repos.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add shared/setup/build-command CI step (fail-closed, no retry) (#820) Add a composite action that runs a repo's declared [container].build-command in CI, read through the vrg-container-build-command speller shipped in vergil-tooling v2.1.189.

Unlike the sibling system-packages action (bounded apt retry), the build command is fail-closed with NO retry: an arbitrary build command that fails is a real failure, not a transient mirror flake. Logic lives in install.sh with a self-contained behavioural harness (tests/install.test.sh) covering execute, fail-closed-no-retry, and skip-when-undeclared.

Wired into ci-test.yml's unit job after system-packages (test-runtime dependency only). Docs and mkdocs nav mirror the system-packages action.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• export NODE_PATH in the build-command step for CI resolution parity (#825) After the declared [container].build-command runs, export NODE_PATH (the npm global root from npm root -g) to $GITHUB_ENV so subsequent CI test steps can resolve a node library baked out-of-workspace by the build-command (npm install -g ) via CommonJS require. This mirrors the NODE_PATH the local dev image injects (vergil-project/vergil-tooling#2781), keeping baked-library resolution identical locally and in CI — the drift epic vergil-project/.github#291 prevents.

    The export is guarded on CI context ($GITHUB_ENV present) and npm being on PATH, so a non-CI or non-node run is a clean no-op; the step stays fail-closed and retry-free. NODE_PATH is honoured by require only (ESM import ignores it).

    Extends the install.test.sh harness with two cases (NODE_PATH appended when a command ran with a stub npm on PATH; nothing appended on the skip path) and documents the behavior and the require-only caveat.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • document build-command step at parity with system-packages (#830) Fill the parity gaps where the sibling [container].system-packages step is documented but build-command is not: the Shared actions list, the ci-test workflow reference, and the repository configuration page. Also add a back-link from the system-packages action page to its build-command sibling. Each addition mirrors the system-packages treatment while capturing the build-command specifics: test-jobs-only, runs after system-packages, fail-closed with no retry, and the NODE_PATH export with its require-only/ESM caveat.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: • promote CI evidence gate to enforcing (#832) Flip the evidence-enforce default from false to true in cd-release.yml (and the two composites' inert enforce defaults, for a self-consistent fail-closed default). Incomplete or failed CI evidence now hard-fails a release before publish — the spec §9 publish invariant. Warning mode remains as a temporary per-repo opt-out (evidence-enforce=false), never a permanent soft gate. Promotion follows a clean ~4-week bake: 54/54 vergil-tooling releases (v2.1.138-191) and 100% bundle attachment across the other cd-release repos within their adoption windows, with complete manifests. Completes T11 of epic vergil-project/.github#140.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • bridge per-matrix report files into test/audit/quality evidence artifacts (#837) In GitHub Actions each job runs on its own runner with its own filesystem. The test/audit/quality exec (matrix) jobs produced their report files, but the separate evidence job did a clean checkout and called evidence/emit against globs that matched an empty tree, stranding every report and shipping empty payloads for those three gates while only security carried real files. Mirror the working ci-security.yml pattern: each matrix leg uploads its version-suffixed reports as a per-version partial artifact, and the evidence job downloads every leg's partials (merge-multiple) before emit, so the bundle carries each interpreter version's reports. quality-ruff.json / quality-mypy.xml are a locked filename contract with vergil-tooling#2811 and stay skipped-empty (non-fatal) until it releases.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • provide GH_TOKEN to cd-docs pre-deploy step (#845) The pre-deploy step runs vrg-roadmap / vrg-activity-log, which shell out to gh to read the org .github epics. In an Actions runner gh exits non-zero without a token, so every CD docs-refresh job failed. The org .github epic home is public, so the repo-scoped default token is sufficient; set GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} on the step. No wrapper or caller changes needed. Ref vergil-project/.github#310.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• capture OpenSSF Scorecard as point-in-time snapshot doc (#841) Add docs/security/openssf-scorecard-snapshots.md capturing OpenSSF Scorecard as dated snapshots rather than accreting findings in the issue tracker. Preserves the 2026-05-19 baseline (5.5/10) and adds a freshly re-run 2026-08-12 snapshot (5.5/10, commit bbaccdd4). Format and location mirror the vergil-claude-plugin capture. Remediation remains tracked separately (epic vergil-project/.github#54, tracking issue vergil-project/vergil-tooling#828).

  • update the all-hard-gates CI-evidence example to enforcing (#843) The CI-evidence completeness gate reached its enforcing end state after a ~4-week bake (evidence-enforce flipped false->true, live as of v2.1.27). The worked example in the all-hard-gates principle doc still described it in present-tense warning mode, which is stale. Rewrite the example as a lifecycle that ran to completion — introduced in warning mode, baked while robustness was validated, then promoted by a single flag flip to enforcing — and state the present end state plainly: an incomplete or failed evidence bundle is now a terminal, publish-blocking failure. Also document that completeness is now measured against report payload, not just envelope presence (ref #2812), and note the two current residuals (empty manifest metrics, empty security tools) as open limitations.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• wire a C++ semgrep ruleset that exists (#851) (#852) p/cpp is not a Semgrep registry ruleset - it 404s, so the semgrep gate failed with exit 7 on every cpp repo. p/c-plus-plus and p/cplusplus 404 as well.

p/c alone is not a fix. extra-config is the entire C++ ruleset here, because vrg-semgrep-scan's _LANGUAGE_RULESETS has no cpp key, and p/c applies rules to .c only - it scans no C++ whatsoever. Dropping to p/c would have turned a hard failure into silent zero coverage.

Measured with an identical probe.c/probe.cpp pair on semgrep 1.173.0, reading paths.scanned: p/c scans only the .c file, while p/security-audit, p/default and p/cwe-top-25 all apply rules to the .cpp file. p/security-audit also fired a real finding on the C probe (insecure-use-string-copy-fn, CWE-676). Full table in the issue.

Surfaced by logical-minds-foundry/mq-protocol-gateway, the fleet's first cpp repo.

  • state plainly that semgrep gives no C++ coverage (#853) (#854) Follow-up to #851/#852, which stopped the p/cpp 404 but documented p/security-audit as restoring C++ rule applicability. That claim is false and the config did not do it.

No community Semgrep pack declares a single cpp rule - measured p/c 0, p/security-audit 0, p/default 0, p/cwe-top-25 0. https://semgrep.dev/c/r/cpp returns 200 with a body of 'rules: []': the C++ namespace exists and is empty, which is also why p/cpp was never published.

The earlier conclusion came from reading semgrep's paths.scanned, where p/security-audit appeared to scan a .cpp probe. That was its 14 generic/regex rules matching any file, not C++ analysis. Direct check with gets(buf) duplicated across t.c/t.cpp/t.cc/t.hpp under --config p/c: 'Scanning 4 files tracked by git with 2 Code rules: Scanning 1 file with 2 c rules', one finding, on t.c only.

Semgrep's GA C/C++ support is Semgrep Code - Pro engine and Pro rules behind SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN - not the unauthenticated community registry this pipeline scans.

docs.title: Chores
docs.text:
• reconcile .gitignore to baseline + add ops.yml (#849) (#850) Rollout for epic #311: bring vergil-actions to a superset of the centralized .gitignore baseline and add a self-policing scheduled ops.yml (staggered per-repo cron).

  • ignore Conan 2 generator output for baseline compliance (#856) Add the Conan 2 generator-output block (CMake presets + conan*.sh scripts) to bring vergil-actions into compliance with the baseline .gitignore. These patterns were added to the baseline in vergil-tooling#2891 but vergil-actions had not caught up, so vrg-github-repo-config audit reported 11 missing patterns. Mirrors the baseline block; conan.lock stays committed for reproducible resolution.

docs.title: Breaking change — ci-security.yml callers must grant actions: read
docs.text:
This release adds actions: read to the permissions: request of the reusable ci-security.yml workflow. GitHub validates that request against the calling job's permissions at workflow startup, so every caller must add actions: read to the permissions: block of the job that calls ci-security.yml before consuming this release. Callers without the grant fail at startup, with no checks registered:

The workflow is requesting 'actions: read', but is only allowed 'actions: none'.

The grant is backward-compatible with v2.1.2 (callers may grant more than a called workflow requests), so consumers can land it before upgrading. The v2.1 rolling tag was rolled back to v2.1.2 when this release first broke consumers, and is re-promoted once all consumers carry the grant. Full incident analysis and rollout plan: #698.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• grant actions: read and add upload-sarif artifact fallback (#694) SARIF upload to code scanning fails on private consumer repos because codeql-action/upload-sarif reads the workflow run via the Actions API, which needs actions: read there; public repos do not, so the gap was invisible on vergil-project repos.

  • Add actions: read at the workflow level and to the codeql, trivy, and semgrep job permissions in ci-security.yml, and to this repo's own caller in ci.yml.

  • Add an upload-sarif input (default true) to ci-security.yml and to the trivy and semgrep actions. When false, scans still run and still fail on findings, but SARIF results are attached as build artifacts (trivy-fs-sarif, semgrep-sarif) instead of being uploaded to code scanning — the documented posture for private repos without GHAS.
  • Gate the codeql job on upload-sarif: CodeQL cannot run on private repos without GHAS regardless of upload destination.
  • Document the permission and the no-GHAS configuration across the workflow, action, and CI-gates docs.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• use python3 from PATH, not /usr/local/bin (#863) (#864) The 'Detect release model' step invoked /usr/local/bin/python3. That path exists in the base/python images - where this workflow's own ci.yml self-test runs (container-suffix: base) - but NOT in prod-cpp-clang:20, where python3 is at /usr/bin/python3. So the version-bump job hard-failed for any cpp repo with 'No such file or directory', before evaluating any version.

Confirmed in the cpp image: /usr/local/bin/python3 is absent; python3 from PATH is /usr/bin/python3 (3.13.5, tomllib present) and reads release-model correctly. Using python3 from PATH resolves to the right interpreter in every image and makes the step image-agnostic - the workflow should not assume a python location.

Surfaced by logical-minds-foundry/mq-protocol-gateway#1 (first cpp repo): PR #12 was green on every job except version/version-bump, purely because of this path.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • evidence gate fails red on a failed/skipped leg (#338) (#878)

docs.title: Chores
docs.text:
• sync .gitignore to the canonical baseline (#869) Append the baseline lines this repo was missing (build-sanitize/, the C++ ASan/UBSan out-of-tree build dir) so .gitignore is a verbatim superset of vergil_tooling.data/gitignore.baseline again. Existing local entries are preserved. Part of epic vergil-project/.github#322.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• stop declaring signing secrets that shadow the package-signing environment (#913) (#914) The first packaged release (vergil-project/packages v1.1.0, CD run 37494464077) failed closed: package-sign saw an empty PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY, although the package-signing environment was applied (deployment on main 16:17:57Z) and holds the secret. cd-release declared PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY/PASSPHRASE under on.workflow_call.secrets (to satisfy actionlint), and a declared-but-unpassed secret shadowed the environment secret with an empty value.

Remove both declarations so the environment is the only source (matching publish-index, which declares none), and ignore actionlint's resulting undeclared-secret finding for exactly those two names in .github/actionlint.yaml. Document the rule.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • upload SARIF without accepted-suppressed results (#921) Code scanning ignores SARIF suppressions, so a finding the SARIF gate accepts (e.g. a justified nosemgrep) still failed GitHub's Semgrep OSS check. The Semgrep and Trivy actions now run vrg-sarif-filter and upload a filtered *.upload.sarif copy, while the unfiltered SARIF remains what the evidence job collects. The ci-security trivy job installs vergil-tooling to provide the filter. CodeQL is unchanged: analyze uploads internally. Docs updated. Requires a vergil-tooling release containing vrg-sarif-filter (vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3114). Ref #920

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • callers must pass secrets: inherit for environment secrets (#918) (#919) A controlled probe (vergil-project/packages#6, run 37507168545) proved that environment secrets reach a job in a cross-repo reusable workflow only when the caller passes secrets: inherit; an explicit map or nothing gives an empty value, and the callee's declaration is irrelevant. Correct the cd-release and publish-index caller docs and examples (inherit plus a scoped nosemgrep), and correct the #913 comments, which attributed the failure to secret shadowing (disproven).

Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#925

docs.text:
• Azure-first apt mirror list, fail-fast apt and job timeouts for package jobs (#933)
  • fix(package): use the Azure apt mirror and fail-fast apt in package setup

Move the package setup OS-prerequisites step into os-prereqs.sh. On x86_64 Ubuntu containers it points the archive and security URIs (deb822 ubuntu.sources and legacy sources.list) at http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/, the mirror GitHub's hosted runners use, before the single apt-get update; arm64 (ports.ubuntu.com) is left untouched. It writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80-vergil-fast-fail (3 retries, 20 s timeouts) for every later apt call in the job, installs all prerequisites including gnupg in one call, and on UBI runs one dnf install with retries=3/timeout=20 and path-form curl/gpg. Adds tests/os-prereqs.test.sh, wired into the smoke workflow, and documents the action. Ref #931

docs.text:
• fail a requested publish whose credential is missing, and drop Ruby (#988) The Publish step now runs publish.sh, which fails with an ::error:: naming the secret when the credential vrg-ecosystem-resolve names is empty, instead of skipping with a notice and letting the release report success. A credential name the action does not provide (vergil-tooling and vergil-actions disagree) also fails loudly. The accepted names are the env vars the publish tools read: CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (cargo publish) and MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE (maven-gpg-plugin).

Remove the Ruby leftovers (rubygems-api-key, GEM_HOST_API_KEY, the RUBYGEMS_API_KEY secret and ruby in the build-and-publish condition); vergil-tooling#3388 removed Ruby support.

Add tests/publish.test.sh, run by the new smoke-registry-publish workflow, covering the credential check and the secret -> input -> env var wiring.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• derive CI versions through vrg-ci-resolve and assert the running toolchain (#990)
  • feat(setup): derive CI versions through vrg-ci-resolve and assert the running toolchain

derive.sh now runs vrg-ci-resolve once and copies its answer to the setup action's outputs, adding container-tags and container-suffixes; the inline Python derivation is gone and resolver errors fail the step as ::error:: annotations. ci/matrix builds every image from the resolver's tags and suffixes with no family routing, and run-once kinds follow the primary version. A new ci/toolchain/assert action checks that each matrix leg runs its resolved Python or Go version, after the leg pins UV_PYTHON. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#962

  • chore(setup): mark the resolver and toolchain-assert scripts executable

Restores the executable bit on derive.test.sh and sets it on the new assert.sh and assert.test.sh, matching the sibling action scripts. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#962

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
• pin Python legs to the image's interpreter with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system (#995)
  • ci(toolchain): pin Python legs to the image's interpreter with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system

Every Python matrix leg (ci-quality lint and typecheck, ci-audit dependencies, ci-test unit) now pins uv through a new ci/toolchain/pin-python action, which exports UV_PYTHON= and UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system. A repo's uv python-preference (e.g. only-managed) can no longer make a leg download a managed Python instead of using the image's; a missing interpreter fails loudly. The pin.test.sh harness also checks that every job with an assert-toolchain step pins through the action and that no workflow sets UV_PYTHON by hand. assert-toolchain now logs the interpreter path it found. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#994

  • ci(toolchain): restore the executable bit on assert.test.sh

An in-place edit dropped the mode to 644 in the previous commit. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#994

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• pull from GHCR mirror with retry; bump to 0.71.0 (#706) The shared Trivy action pulled aquasec/trivy from Docker Hub anonymously with no retry, so transient Hub timeouts and anonymous rate limits turned the security/trivy check red on unrelated diffs (e.g. vergil-claude-plugin PR #475).

  • Default the image to the GHCR mirror ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy, which sidesteps Docker Hub's anonymous pull rate limits entirely. GHCR is the natural registry from GitHub Actions runners and needs no Hub-token secret plumbed through consuming repos.

  • Bump the default tag to 0.71.0 (released 2026-06-01) for freshness.
  • Add a bounded pull-with-backoff step before the scan steps as a registry-agnostic backstop; subsequent docker run steps reuse the local image.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
• pin the docs jobs' uv interpreter source with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system (#1005)
  • ci(docs): pin the docs jobs' uv interpreter source with UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system

The ci-docs and cd-docs jobs ran uv run mkdocs/mike for Python repos without UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE, so a repo with python-preference = only-managed made uv download a managed Python for the docs build, or fail when it also set python-downloads = manual. Both jobs now set UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system in their job env (source only; they resolve no version, so UV_PYTHON stays unset). The cd/docs/deploy action pins its Deploy docs step for direct callers, and setup/vergil pins the vergil-tooling self-install uv sync inline. The pin.test.sh harness gains a uv source guard: every workflow job running a uv project command or ci/toolchain/assert must pin first (pin-python or job env), and every composite action or script must pin on the step or inline, with assert (caller-pinned) and package/setup/detect.sh (needs managed Python) as listed exceptions; fixtures test the guard both ways. smoke-setup-vergil now triggers on any workflow or action change. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1002

  • ci(toolchain): restore the executable bit on pin.test.sh

An in-place sed edit dropped the mode to 644 in the previous commit. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1002

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • make detect.sh ignore the repo's uv settings with uv run --no-config (#1010) detect.sh read vergil.toml with uv run --no-project --python 3.14, which still reads the repo's uv settings ([tool.uv] in pyproject.toml, uv.toml) from the working directory. In a repo that sets python-downloads = "manual" (with python-preference = "only-managed") it failed in the package images, which ship no Python and need uv to download one. It now runs uv run --no-config --no-project, so the repo's uv settings cannot reach it. detect.test.sh gains cases that run detect.sh from inside a fixture repo with those settings in pyproject.toml and in uv.toml, with an empty managed-Python dir, and assert the same install spec. The pin.test.sh source guard no longer exempts detect.sh outright: it is now a config-free file whose every uv command must pass --no-config, with fixtures both ways. Ref vergil-project/vergil-actions#1003

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• test the warning passthrough with a stub resolver; app multi-pin is fatal (#1023) The released resolver (vergil-tooling 2.1.259+) makes an app pinning more than one version a fatal error (T14, vergil-tooling#3372) and prints no warnings (vergil-tooling#3442), so the derive.sh harness case that expected a ::warning:: for that pin failed on every PR. Replace it with a case that drives derive.sh's warning passthrough through a stub vrg-ci-resolve (same five-key JSON shape), add a case asserting the app multi-pin fails with the resolver's ::error::, and update the derive.sh comment and action docs. Ref #1022.

  • derive the release container tag from the resolver (#1024) The release job ran on the caller's container-tag input, which vrg-repo-init freezes into cd.yml at init time, so releases built on a stale version outside the window. A new setup job runs the shared setup action (vrg-ci-resolve) and the release job's image, and its validate-inputs check, now use its primary-container-tag, as CI's single-container jobs do. The container-tag input stays for one release as accepted-but-ignored with a ::warning::, because GitHub rejects an undeclared input to a reusable workflow and every caller still passes it; vergil-project/vergil-tooling#3484 removes it from the callers. Adds the container-tag.test.sh harness and smoke-cd-release workflow, and a cd-release workflow docs page. Ref #1017

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>derive the release image suffix from the resolver (#1030) The release job built its image suffix from the caller's container-suffix, else language, else base, so a C++ caller passing language: cpp got the unpublished prod-cpp image. The setup job now runs the new cd/release/primary-suffix action on the shared setup action's primary-version and container-suffixes, and the release job runs on prod-:, the image CI's primary leg uses (clang-20 -> prod-cpp-clang:20). The caller's container-suffix is kept only as a cross-check that must equal the resolved primary suffix; a mismatch fails setup. container-tag.test.sh gains structure checks for the suffix wiring and fixture cases for C++ (clang-20), TypeScript (node-24), Python with a matching caller suffix, and three mismatched-suffix failures. Ref #1020

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>derive single-container job image suffixes from the resolver (#1034) ci-quality's common job and ci-version-bump's version-bump job built their image suffix from the caller's container-suffix (else base), so a C++ or TypeScript caller passing no suffix ran on prod-base, and a Java or Rust caller on the unpublished prod-base:. Both setup jobs now run the primary-suffix action on the shared setup action's primary-version and container-suffixes, and the jobs run on prod-:, the image CI's primary leg uses (clang-20 -> prod-cpp-clang:20). The caller's container-suffix stays a must-match cross-check. The action now serves CI and CD, so it moves from actions/cd/release/primary-suffix to actions/shared/setup/primary-suffix; cd-release, its harness and the docs follow with unchanged behaviour. The new image.test.sh harness, run from smoke-setup-vergil, checks the wiring of all three single-container jobs, that no workflow job builds its image from inputs.container-suffix or inputs.language, the resolved images for C++, TypeScript, Python and no-language fixtures, and loud failure on mismatched caller suffixes. Ref #1028

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: • build every package cell on the matrix-recorded runtime and check it before signing (#1038) cd-release's package-build and ci-package's build pass each cell's matrix-recorded runtime to vrg-package build --runtime, through matrix.runtime || '' so a non-python cell passes an empty value, never null. package-sign now checks out the repo, installs vergil-tooling, downloads the package-manifest artifact and runs vrg-package check-runtime on the unsigned packages after rpm is installed and before signing, so a mixed-runtime release stops before anything is signed or tagged. Adds the package-runtime.test.sh harness to the cd-release smoke workflow and documents the runtime on the cd-release and ci-package pages. Needs vergil-tooling 2.1.262 (v2.1). Ref #1029

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text: <ul> <li>match uv commands with global options in the uv pin guard (#1055) The uv pin guard in pin-python/tests/pin.test.sh matched only 'uv ', so a global option before the subcommand (uv --quiet run, uv -q sync, uv --directory d run) hid the command from both the UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system check and the detect.sh --no-config check. Both regexes now allow any run of global options (each optionally with one value) before the subcommand, and accept --no-config among the global options or among the bare flags right after the subcommand. uv tool, uv --version, comments and backtick prose stay exempt. Adds 13 fixtures both ways; no existing case changes result.

docs.text: • retry a scan that errors without a report and report it as a scan error (#1080) The fs and image scans now run through scan.sh, which tells a scan with findings apart from one that wrote no report. A no-report scan is retried with backoff and then fails with a 'Trivy scan errored (no report produced)' message instead of being reported as vulnerabilities; it never passes. The action exposes the outcome as a result output (passed, findings, error) and skips the SARIF upload when there is no report. tests/scan.test.sh covers the outcomes with a stubbed docker.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• deploy un-versioned site when versioning-scheme=none (#714) Docs repos with versioning-scheme=none (single-branch org docs sites) were still deployed through mike, producing a versioned site: a 'dev' version with the current content plus an init '0.1'/'latest' version frozen at scaffold. The root redirected to /dev/, but /latest/ (and /0.1/) served stale content, and the /dev/ URL prefix and version selector are meaningless for a repo with one branch and no versions.

Read versioning-scheme from vergil.toml (same [project] read used for primary-language). When it is 'none', skip mike entirely and publish a single plain site to the gh-pages root via 'mkdocs gh-deploy --force' — no version split, no versions.json, no selector. --force replaces the branch, so the prior dev/0.1/latest fragments are cleaned up on the next deploy. Versioned repos are unchanged.

• make container-prefix a universal tunable, starting with cd-release.yml's package jobs (#1139)
  • feat(package): apply container-prefix to cd-release.yml's package-build cells

The ci-package.yml images step moves into a shared composite action, actions/package/image-prefix (action.yml plus apply.sh), which both matrix jobs now run: ci-package.yml's matrix job and cd-release.yml's package-matrix job. cd-release's package-build cells now take the -pkg- images from the workflow's existing container-prefix input; prod (and empty) pass the matrix through byte for byte, any other value fails package-matrix. package-image-prefix.test.sh now checks both workflows' wiring and the action, and runs apply.sh, including an empty matrix for a repo without [package]; package-runtime.test.sh takes cd-release's build output from the images step. Ref #1134

  • feat(ops): add a container-prefix input to ops-upstream-refresh.yml

The upstream-refresh job ran on a fixed prod-base image and the workflow had no inputs. It now declares the optional container-prefix input (prod or dev, default prod) and runs on -base:latest like the other ops workflows, so a caller can move it to the dev images on its own. Callers that pass nothing are unchanged. Ref #1134

  • test(workflows): check that every reusable workflow honours its container-prefix

container-prefix.test.sh scans every workflow_call workflow in .github/workflows: no string names a ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod- image literally, every job container is a - image or a matrix image produced by ci/matrix or package/image-prefix given the workflow's input, every call to a workflow of this repo that declares the input passes it on, and a workflow running any such job declares the input (string, optional, default prod). Fixture workflows check that each rule catches its violation. smoke-setup-vergil.yml runs it. Ref #1134

  • docs(workflows): document container-prefix as a per-workflow tunable

cd-release's binary packages page gains a Container prefix section and its input row now says the prefix also picks the package-build images; ci-package's section points to the shared action; ops-upstream-refresh documents its new input; the workflows overview and README state the rule every reusable workflow follows; and package/image-prefix gets its own action page. Ref #1134

docs.text: • install the newest release of the pinned line for install-source git (#1145) publish-index's build-index job installed vergil-tooling at the floating vX.Y tag. A release dispatches the index rebuild before it moves vX.Y, so the rebuild ran the previous release's tooling. With install-source: git and a line pin, the setup action now lists the line's vX.Y.Z tags with git ls-remote and installs the newest one; a failed lookup or an empty line fails the job rather than falling back to vX.Y. Per the human's decision, the release order and the promote stage are unchanged, and the auto install path keeps the floating tag. Ref #1144.

• name release job "release / release" to match confirm-main gate (#720) vergil-tooling's confirm-main stage (hardened under #1853) matches the CD release job name EXACTLY against "release / release" and fails closed on any other name. This repo runs a reduced inline release job (freeze-refs + tag-and-release; no registry publish, as an actions-only library) whose display name was "cd / release" — a designed convention (see the CD-checks table in the 2026-05-09 workflow-convention spec, where CD checks were informational, not enforced).

The floating v2.1 tooling pin adopted the tightened gate silently between the 2.1.5 release (passed) and 2.1.6 (stalled at confirm-main, leaving a half-applied release and open tracking issue #715).

Rename the job's display label to "release / release" to match the tooling and align with the sibling docs job, which already surfaces as "docs / docs". The inline job's steps are unchanged. Update the spec's CD-checks table entry to keep docs consistent with the code.

• stage each language's test and audit reports for CI evidence (#1218)
  • fix(ci): stage each language's test and audit reports for CI evidence

ci-audit staged only Python's pip-audit.json and licenses.json, so a Rust audit leg uploaded no cargo-deny.json and the release-time evidence gate refused the audit gate as an empty payload. The new ci/evidence/reports action holds the one per-language report contract (python and rust; test and audit), stages a leg's declared reports version-suffixed, and fails a leg whose gate passed but wrote a report missing or empty, or whose language has no contract. ci-test and ci-audit stage through it and take the emit step's tools from it. Ref #1211.

  • keep a released site's default version on a develop deploy (#1219)

  • fix(docs-deploy): keep a released site's default version on a develop deploy

The develop deploy guarded set-default dev with a grep for a [default] marker in mike list, but mike never prints one: it records the default only as the root index.html that set-default writes, so the guard never matched and every develop deploy reset a released site's default to dev. The guard now asks whether a version carries the latest alias (mike list --json) and sets dev as the default only when none does; a failing mike list fails the deploy. The step's logic moves to deploy.sh, and default.test.sh, run by smoke-cd-docs.yml, checks it with the real mike. Ref #1214

docs.text:
• remove early-exit pipes under pipefail and guard against them (#1326)
  • fix(shell): remove early-exit pipes under pipefail and guard against them

Under set -o pipefail, a consumer that exits on its first match (grep -q, grep -m, head) lets the producer die of SIGPIPE, so the pipeline fails although it matched. This failed release PR #1324's container-tag fixtures check.

Every such site (38 lines in 17 files, two in action.yml run steps) now tests the producer's output with no pipe: a here-string for grep, find -print -quit for the semgrep detection, and a yq [...] | .[0] for the one head. scripts/bin/check-early-exit-pipes, run by validate-custom with its own tests, fails on reintroduction.

docs.title: Reusable Workflows
docs.text: v2.0.0 introduced reusable CI workflows that provide canonical job and check names across all managed repositories. Each workflow bundles one or more composite actions with the container, tooling, and permission setup needed to run them. CD workflows handle post-merge delivery (releases, documentation).

docs.title: Why reusable workflows?
docs.text: Composite actions run as steps within a caller-defined job. Reusable workflows run as complete jobs, which means they control the job name that appears in GitHub's checks UI. This guarantees consistent, canonical check names across repositories — a requirement for pattern-based required status checks in rulesets.

docs.title: CI workflows (pre-merge)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose CI Docs ci-docs.yml Build-only MkDocs strict verification (no deploy) CI Security ci-security.yml Security scanning (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) CI Quality ci-quality.yml Common linting, custom validation, language-specific lint and typecheck CI Audit ci-audit.yml Dependency audit CI Test ci-test.yml Unit tests CI Version Bump ci-version-bump.yml Version divergence gate CI Package ci-package.yml Build and install-test .deb/.rpm packages (repos with [package] only)

docs.title: CD workflows (post-merge)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose CD Release cd-release.yml Full release pipeline (tag, build, publish, version bump); repos with [package] also build, sign and attach .deb/.rpm packages (binary packages) CD Docs cd-docs.yml MkDocs documentation deployment Publish package index publish-index.yml Signed apt/dnf package-repository site, deployed to Pages CD Docs Refresh cd-docs-refresh.yml Regenerate the roadmap and activity pages and redeploy the docs site, on a schedule

docs.title: Ops workflows (scheduled and event-driven)
docs.text: Workflow File Purpose Ops GitHub Config ops-github-config.yml Nightly vrg-github-repo-config update as the automation App, branch sweep, and vrg-dependabot-audit open-alert gate Ops Agent Audit ops-agent-audit.yml Daily vrg-agent-audit as the automation App: every merge into develop and main since the audit markers, checked for its actors and merge-review coverage. A security signal, never reported Ops Epic Rollup ops-epic-rollup.yml Close a task's parent epic when its last task closes (called on issues: closed) Ops Epic Sweep ops-epic-sweep.yml Daily org-wide reconciliation: close epics and tasks that missed their event-driven close, drain standing epics into archives, and attach orphan issues to an epic Ops Upstream Refresh ops-upstream-refresh.yml Scheduled vrg-upstream-refresh: run the repository's [upstream-refresh].hook with no secrets, then open one PR that merges itself as the automation App once CI passes, or close an earlier one when nothing changed

docs.title: Dynamic version matrix and evidence gates
docs.text:
The matrixed CI workflows (ci-audit, ci-quality, ci-test) take their version matrix from vrg-ci-resolve at run time, via the shared setup action's outputs. The resolver reads the consumer's vergil.toml and the published language version window: a library builds the whole window, any other repository type builds one version, and a [ci].versions pin must lie inside the window. Each leg asserts that it runs the version it was resolved for (ci/toolchain/assert). A consumer's ci.yml is therefore a thin caller that passes only language: and container-suffix:. The versions: and container-tag: inputs were removed in #899.

Single-container jobs (ci-quality's common and custom, ci-version-bump, and cd-release's release) run on the resolver's primary version: [ci].primary-version if set, else the newest resolved version, on the resolver's image suffix and tag for it (clang-20 runs on prod-cpp-clang:20; see shared/setup/primary-suffix). The caller's container-suffix never picks an image: the matrix legs accept any resolved suffix as a cross-check, and the single-container jobs require the primary version's.

Each matrixed workflow emits a stable, version-agnostic aggregate gate named <kind> / evidence — audit / evidence, quality / evidence, and test / evidence. The evidence job needs every matrix leg and runs with if: always(), asserting each leg's result is success, so a failed or skipped leg makes the aggregate fail red rather than skip green. Branch protection requires these stable evidence gates, not the per-version legs, so the required-check set does not churn when the resolved version set changes (a new language window, or a change to the [ci].versions pin). See Required Checks.

quality / evidence always bundles the common job's transcript (quality-common.log, the full vrg-validate --check common output) alongside any lint/typecheck reports. That transcript gives a language-less repo (container-suffix: base), which has no lint/typecheck reports, a real quality report. Release-time harvest rejects an evidence.json-only payload as incomplete, and cd-release follows each evidence step with an explicit enforcement guard, so an incomplete gate blocks the release in enforcing mode (see All Hard Gates).

quality / evidence also bundles the custom job's transcript (quality-custom.log, the full vrg-validate --check custom output). The custom job runs the repo's custom validator (scripts/bin/validate-custom or vrg-validate-custom) in PR CI, or logs one "no custom validator" line and passes when the repo has none. The evidence job needs it, so a failed or skipped custom stage fails quality / evidence — no extra required check (epic vergil-project/.github#488).

docs.title: Consuming a reusable workflow
docs.text:
Reference workflows using the full path to the workflow file with a rolling minor tag pin:

uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1

Tag pinning

The same tag pinning guidance applies as for composite actions. Pin to @v2.1 for automatic patch releases, or @v2.1.0 for full reproducibility.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Reusable workflows inherit permissions from the calling workflow. Callers must declare the permissions each workflow needs at the job level:

jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    with:
      language: python

A called workflow's own permissions: blocks are requests against the caller: GitHub validates at workflow startup that the calling job's effective permissions cover every requested scope, and rejects the run with startup_failure if they do not. See each workflow's page for the scopes it requests.

docs.title: Container image prefix
docs.text:
All reusable workflows run inside container images from the ghcr.io/vergil-project/ registry. The image name follows the pattern:

ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>

The prefix defaults to prod and selects which image variant to use. Every reusable workflow that runs a job in one of these images accepts a container-prefix input that overrides this default for every image it uses, including the package toolchain images of ci-package and cd-release (<prefix>-pkg-*). Each workflow file reads only its own input, so a caller can switch its CI and its release separately. (publish-index runs on the bare runner and has no such input.) The Docker images are part of the development and deployment environment only — there is no runtime dependency on them from the artifacts these workflows produce.

docs.title: Overriding the prefix
docs.text:
To test against development Docker images, pass container-prefix: dev to the reusable workflow calls in the consumer's ci.yml, cd.yml, or ops.yml. Override a single workflow call to test one phase, or override all calls in a file to run the full CI/CD pipeline against dev images.

Single workflow override:

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

Full CI file override (add container-prefix: dev to every call):

jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-prefix: dev

  test:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-test.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python
      container-prefix: dev

Committing and pushing the overrides is expected when running a full end-to-end integration test of the dev images through CI and CD. Remove the overrides once the dev images have been validated and promoted to prod.

For local validation using development containers, see the vrg-container-run documentation for instructions on specifying the container prefix.

docs.title: Reference freezing
docs.text: The workflow source files reference composite actions via @develop during development. At release time, the publish workflow freezes all @develop references to the release tag (e.g., @v2.1.0), ensuring that a pinned workflow version uses the matching action versions.

docs.title: cd-docs-refresh
docs.text:
Regenerates a docs site's generated pages and republishes the site. It is a thin wrapper over cd-docs.yml with the page generation pre-wired.

It exists for an organization's documentation-site repository, whose roadmap and activity pages change with epic activity in the org rather than with any change to the docs repository. There is no push or release to rebuild on, so the caller runs it on a schedule and on demand.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description pre-deploy-command string no vrg-roadmap > docs/site/docs/roadmap.md && vrg-activity-log > docs/site/docs/activity.md Command that regenerates the generated pages before the deploy mkdocs-config string no docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to the MkDocs configuration file container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the report job's ops/report step and, in the cd-docs.yml run that refresh calls, to the pre-deploy command and the docs staging step, which stop when it is missing or invalid

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description refresh <caller> / refresh / docs Calls cd-docs.yml, whose docs job runs the command, stages the docs and deploys them report <caller> / report Always, after refresh: reports its result as docs-refresh to the org's operations queue through ops/report

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The refresh job calls cd-docs.yml with the three inputs, report: false (the refresh reports its run to the operations queue itself, so cd-docs.yml must not report it a second time) and both App secrets. Its docs job:

  1. Runs in the automation environment, which holds the App secrets, and mints an App token scoped to the repository with only Contents write. It checks out the repository with that token and full history, and installs vergil-tooling.
  2. Runs pre-deploy-command. The default runs vrg-roadmap and vrg-activity-log, which read the org's .github epics with gh; the step sets GH_TOKEN to the workflow's github.token, which is enough because the epic home is public.
  3. Stages the changelog and release notes with shared/docs/stage.
  4. Deploys with cd/docs/deploy: mike for a versioned site, or mkdocs gh-deploy to the gh-pages root for a repository with versioning-scheme = none. The gh-pages push uses the App token, and the commit is made as the App's <app-slug>[bot] user (see The App identity).

cd-docs runs in the cd-docs concurrency group without cancelling, so a refresh queues behind a deploy that is already running.

The nested call is to cd-docs.yml@develop, fully qualified so it resolves when cd-docs-refresh is called from another repository. The release freezes that ref to the release tag (see Reference freezing).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. The deploy pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch with the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
name: CD Docs Refresh

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 1 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  refresh:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-docs-refresh.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets: inherit

A caller in another organization passes the two keys by name, as Secrets shows.

The Run workflow button (workflow_dispatch) is the manual "refresh now".

docs.title: cd-release: binary packages
docs.text:
When the caller's vergil.toml has a [package] section, cd-release.yml also builds, signs and attaches the repo's .deb/.rpm packages:

Job Behavior package-matrix Always runs. vrg-package check-unpublished --version <version> first refuses the release if any package it would publish (same name, full version, arch and format) was already published by an earlier release; a repo without [package] passes. Then vrg-package matrix --github-output --manifest packages-manifest.json resolves the build cells and writes the release manifest, and package/image-prefix applies the caller's container-prefix to each cell's image. For each builder = "python" package it resolves the vergil-python runtime once, and records it as runtime on that package's build cells and in the manifest's runtimes map. With several [[package]] entries, cell ids are package-qualified (<name>--<id>). package-build / <cell> One job per build cell, on the cell's runner inside the cell's package toolchain image (prod-pkg-ubuntu or prod-pkg-rhel, or their dev-pkg- variants with container-prefix: dev), set up with package/setup as in ci-package.yml. It runs vrg-package build --cell <cell> --runtime <runtime> with the cell's recorded runtime, so every cell of a package builds on the same runtime. A cell without one (a non-python builder) passes an empty --runtime, never null. The packages are unsigned. package-sign Declares the package-signing environment. Before signing anything it runs vrg-package check-runtime --manifest packages-manifest.json --artifacts dist/packages, which fails unless every .deb and .rpm of each python package depends on exactly the runtime the manifest records for that package (packages with no recorded runtime are not checked). It then signs every .rpm with the org signing subkey and verifies each signature, then attests the provenance of every package. release Runs only if package-sign succeeded. It attaches the signed packages and packages-manifest.json to the Release, then dispatches package-released to <owner>/packages.

A re-published package version, a failed build cell, a mixed-runtime package set or a failed signing step stops release before anything is published or tagged. The runtime check (vergil-tooling#3478) catches cells that built on different runtimes, as vergil-tooling 2.1.258 did (amd64 on vergil-python3.15, arm64 on vergil-python3.14). The --runtime and check-runtime options need vergil-tooling 2.1.262 or later at the caller's [dependencies].vergil pin; v2.1 resolves to it. The re-publish check is the CD backstop for a release that did not go through vrg-release preflight, which runs the same check: a package version published twice breaks the shared package index for every repo. Any gh error fails the check rather than skipping it. The dispatch is deferred: if minting the App token or the dispatch fails, the release still stands. The index's weekly reconcile picks it up, and vrg-release reports the miss. Repos without [package] see only the extra package-matrix job. The other package jobs are skipped, and they never reference the package-signing environment.

A packaged repo needs:

  • A package-signing environment. Its deployment-branch policy must admit only main. It holds the PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY secret (the ASCII-armored export of the signing subkey) and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE. If the key is missing or empty, package-sign fails.
  • secrets: inherit on the caller. Within vergil-project the caller passes secrets: inherit, as vrg-github-repo-init generates it. It carries the package-signing secrets, which cd-release.yml does not declare, and the org App secrets APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY, which every release needs to push its tags and the index dispatch needs too. vrg-validate's secrets-inherit check allows inherit to cd-release.yml, so the line needs no nosemgrep. GitHub passes inherit only to a reusable workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise, and a packaged repo outside vergil-project cannot sign its packages yet (vergil-project/.github#1592). The App must be installed on <owner>/packages with permission to create repository dispatches (contents: write).
  • The same permissions the release job already needs. The package jobs request only contents: read, id-token: write and attestations: write:
jobs:
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      actions: read
    with:
      language: python
    # `inherit` within vergil-project: it carries the App keys and the
    # package-signing secrets.
    secrets: inherit

docs.title: Container prefix
docs.text:
The package-build cells run on the images vrg-package matrix names, ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod-pkg-<distro>:<version>. The workflow's container-prefix input, which also picks the release job's image, applies to them too, by the same package/image-prefix action ci-package.yml uses: with dev, the package-matrix job rewrites the prod-pkg- start of each cell's image to dev-pkg-, so the release builds its packages on the development package images. Nothing else in the matrix changes, and with prod (the default, which an empty value also means) it is passed on unchanged. Any other value, or a missing or malformed vrg-package matrix output, fails package-matrix, and so the release before anything is built. The job log lists the image each cell will use.

The input is set per workflow file, so a caller can run its package CI (ci-package.yml) and its release on different images. dev is a temporary setting: remove it once the production images serve again.

jobs:
  release:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-prefix: dev  # optional; omit for prod
    secrets: inherit

docs.title: cd-release
docs.text: The release pipeline. On a push to main it checks the CI evidence of the release PR, builds and publishes the release, tags it and creates the GitHub Release. Repos with [package] in vergil.toml also build, sign and attach .deb/.rpm packages (binary packages).

docs.title: Container image
docs.text:
The release job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>:

  • <prefix> is container-prefix (default prod).
  • <suffix> and <tag> are the resolver's image suffix and tag for the primary version ([ci].primary-version, or the newest resolved version), the same image CI's primary leg runs on. The setup job runs the shared setup action, which calls vrg-ci-resolve against the consumer's vergil.toml and the published language version window. The tag is its primary-container-tag; the suffix is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix.

For example clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, node-24 gives prod-ts-node:24, 3.14 gives prod-python:3.14 and a language-less repo's latest gives prod-base:latest.

So a release builds and tests on the image CI resolves today, not on a tag written into the caller's cd.yml when the repo was initialized, or a suffix guessed from language (language: cpp used to name prod-cpp, which is not published). The caller passes no tag, and needs no container-suffix. If it passes one, the value must equal the resolved suffix, or setup fails: the caller's cd.yml and vergil.toml disagree on the language. A resolver error fails setup too, and release does not run.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Default Description language string "" Language ecosystem (go, python, rust, typescript). Omit it for repos with no language. container-suffix string "" Cross-check only. The image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the resolved primary suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes the image. container-tag string "" Deprecated and ignored. The tag comes from the resolver. A non-empty value only adds a ::warning:: to the run. The input is kept for one release so callers that still pass it do not fail: GitHub rejects a reusable-workflow call that passes an input the workflow does not declare. It is deleted once vergil-tooling#3484 removes it from every caller. container-prefix string prod Image name prefix (prod or dev). It picks the release job's image and, for repos with [package], the <prefix>-pkg-* images of the package-build cells (binary packages). registry-publish boolean false Publish build artifacts to the language's package registry. build-command string "" Override the ecosystem's build command. publish-command string "" Override the ecosystem's publish command. attestation-subject-path string "" Glob for build provenance attestation. Empty skips it. sbom-output-file string "" SBOM output path ($VERSION placeholder). Empty skips it. release-artifacts string "" Files to attach to the Release ($VERSION placeholder). evidence-enforce boolean true true fails the release before publish when the CI evidence is incomplete or failed. false only warns, as a temporary per-repo opt-out.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text: Job Behavior setup Always runs. Resolves primary-container-suffix and primary-container-tag for release, fails if the caller's container-suffix disagrees with the resolved suffix, and warns if the caller passed container-tag. package-matrix Always runs. Resolves the package build cells; a repo without [package] reports none. See binary packages. package-build / <cell>, package-sign Packaged repos only. Every cell builds on the runtime package-matrix recorded, and package-sign checks every package against it before signing. See binary packages. release Runs when setup and package-matrix succeeded, and package-sign too for a packaged repo. Validates the inputs, gates on the CI evidence, publishes, tags and releases, then attaches the evidence bundle.

docs.title: Re-running a published release
docs.text:
A re-run of the release job after its tag exists never moves or recreates the tag and never publishes again: the secrets check, the token mint, the package and registry steps, Tag and release and the package index dispatch all run only for a new tag.

The CI evidence bundle is checked instead. The Check the release's CI evidence step reads the existing GitHub Release's assets:

  • When it carries both v<version>-ci-evidence.tar.gz and v<version>-ci-evidence-manifest.json, the evidence steps are skipped and the job succeeds with a notice.
  • When either is missing (an earlier attempt failed after Tag and release, for example at the bundle's provenance attestation), the evidence gate, the attach with its attestation and both enforcement guards run as on a new release, with a warning naming the missing assets. With evidence-enforce: true, the job fails if the bundle cannot be gated or attached. A configured SBOM is taken from the Release's assets, since a re-run builds nothing; if it is not one, the bundle is assembled without it, with a warning.
  • When the Release cannot be read, the job fails, naming the tag.

Only a run on the tagged commit counts as a re-run. When the tag is on another commit (a push to main with no version bump), the job attaches nothing to that older release, since this commit's evidence is not its own, and succeeds with a notice.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  release:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      registry-publish: true
    secrets: inherit

A caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit; a caller in another org passes the secrets by name (see Secrets). The caller's permissions: must include actions: read (the evidence gate downloads the release PR's CI evidence artifacts), contents: write, id-token: write and attestations: write. A packaged repo must pass secrets: inherit; see binary packages.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY) APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the same App CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN Rust registry publish only crates.io token for registry-publish

Both App secrets live in the calling repository's automation environment. Only the release job declares environment: automation and reads them; a packaged release's package-sign job declares package-signing instead (see binary packages).

Every release needs the two App secrets. The release job pushes the v<version> tag with the App's installation token, never its GITHUB_TOKEN, so that the Tag protection ruleset can let only the repository Admin role and the App create a release tag. The token is scoped to the calling repository with Contents write only. A packaged release also uses the App to dispatch the package index.

The workflow declares both App secrets optional, so a caller that does not pass them still runs. Its release job then fails at its first release step, Require the automation App secrets, with an error naming each missing secret, before the evidence gate, the registry publish or any tag.

A calling job cannot declare an environment, so the caller passes the secrets on by one of two routes, as vrg-github-repo-init generates it. Within vergil-project it passes secrets: inherit, which carries the App keys, CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and a packaged repo's signing secrets. vrg-validate's secrets-inherit check allows it only to the App-key workflows:

    secrets: inherit

GitHub passes secrets: inherit only to a reusable workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise, so a caller in another org passes the keys by name, adding CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN for a Rust registry publish:

    # By name, not inherit: GitHub passes `secrets: inherit` only to a
    # reusable workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise.
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

A packaged repo outside vergil-project cannot sign its packages yet (vergil-project/.github#1592).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS).
