Passed to the package-matrix job's Refuse re-publishing a released package version step and to the release job's CI evidence gate, which stop when it is missing or invalid

A release run before the variable is published fails at one of those steps, before anything is published or tagged; re-run it once the variable is published.

docs.title: ci-audit
docs.text: Dependency audit workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Each leg's image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must be one of the resolved suffixes (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or the matrix job fails. It never changes an image. container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Secret Required Description CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER no ConanCenter provider token for conan audit. Only meaningful for cpp repos; other ecosystems ignore it. Pass it explicitly via the caller's secrets: block — never secrets: inherit. It is not required because non-cpp callers never use it, but a cpp caller must pass it: when it is unset, the cpp audit command fails the conan gate, and so the audit.

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python), installs Python's dev dependencies with ci/toolchain/install-python (skipped with a notice on a repository with neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. Callers are thin: they pass only language: and container-suffix:.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description dependencies / <version> <caller> / dependencies / <version> Dependency audit (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) evidence audit / evidence Aggregate gate — needs every dependencies leg, runs if: always(), and asserts each leg succeeded; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Evidence reports
docs.text: Each dependencies leg stages the language's audit reports for the ci-evidence-audit artifact: pip-audit.json and licenses.json for Python, cargo-deny.json for Rust, npm-audit.json and licenses.json for TypeScript. As for Python, licenses.json is the license report: TypeScript's is written by vrg-npm-license-gate. The names come from ci/evidence/reports. A leg whose audit passed but wrote no report fails, unless the repository is not bootstrapped yet and vrg-validate skipped the gate: the leg then prints a notice and stages a skip record, audit-not-bootstrapped-<version>.json, in place of its reports, and the evidence lists no audit tools, since none ran (see Not-bootstrapped repositories). A language with no audit report contract yet (Go, C++) gets a warning and stages nothing, and the release-time evidence gate decides.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  audit:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-audit.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

For cpp repos, forward the ConanCenter provider token through the explicit-secret chain so conan audit can authenticate:

jobs:
  audit:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-audit.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: cpp
      container-suffix: cpp-clang
    secrets:
      CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER: ${{ secrets.CONAN_AUDIT_PROVIDER_TOKEN_CONANCENTER }}

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: The dependencies job runs each language's real audit through vrg-validate --check audit: pip-audit and pip-licenses for Python, cargo-deny for Rust, npm audit and vrg-npm-license-gate for TypeScript. The audit commands live in vergil-tooling, not in this workflow. Each leg then stages its reports through ci/evidence/reports, whose table is the one place this repository records a language's audit report names. Giving a language without a contract yet (Go, C++) audit evidence means adding its entry to that table alongside the vergil-tooling gate command that writes the reports; the workflow itself needs no change.

docs.title: ci-docs
docs.text: Build-only documentation verification workflow. Runs the same staging as the CD docs deploy and then mkdocs build --strict — without mike, a push, or any credentials — so documentation that fails to build is caught at PR time instead of post-merge in the CD docs deploy.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description mkdocs-config string no docs/site/mkdocs.yml Path to the mkdocs configuration file container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the build job's shared/docs/stage step, which stops when it is missing or invalid

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
Job Check name Description build <caller> / docs Stages docs sources and runs a strict mkdocs build

With the standard caller job key docs, the check is docs / docs, which is a required check for repositories that publish docs (see Required Checks).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The build job:

  1. Checks out the repository with full history (fetch-depth: 0) so the changelog and release-notes staging can read tags.
  2. Detects whether the configured mkdocs config exists. When it is absent the remaining steps are skipped and the job passes — repos without docs are unaffected, mirroring how cd-docs is wired in only for repos that publish documentation.
  3. Stages changelog and release-notes pages and patches the mkdocs nav using the shared actions/shared/docs/stage action — the same staging the CD docs deploy performs, so a green CI docs check reliably predicts a green CD docs deploy.
  4. Runs mkdocs build --strict. The build is credential-free (no mike, no --push, no id-token); --strict turns nav and reference warnings into failures.

For Python repositories the build runs as uv run mkdocs; otherwise it runs mkdocs directly, matching the toolchain resolution in actions/cd/docs/deploy.

docs.title: Interpreter source
docs.text:
The build job sets UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system in its job env, so every uv command in the job, including uv run mkdocs, uses the image's Python (/usr/local/bin/python3 in prod-base). A repository may set uv's python-preference (for example only-managed). Without the pin, uv would download a managed Python for the docs build, or fail when the repository also sets python-downloads = "manual". uv's environment variables take precedence over a repository's uv settings (epic vergil-project/.github#407, spec §6.5).

Only the source is pinned. The job resolves no Python version, so UV_PYTHON is not set and uv picks the image's interpreter against the repository's requires-python. If the image cannot satisfy it, the build fails loudly. There is no fallback. Repositories that do not set these uv options build as before. Added in issue #1002.

docs.title: MkDocs 2.0 banner
docs.text: The "Build docs" step sets NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING=1. Without it, mkdocs-material 9.7.x prints a MkDocs 2.0 warning banner on every build. The workflow has to set the variable itself: a caller's env does not reach a reusable workflow, so callers cannot set it. The variable only hides the banner. Consumers still pin mkdocs<2 in their own docs dependencies. Added in v2.1.43 (#947, PR #948).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  docs:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-docs.yml@v2.1

Add the job only in repositories that publish documentation ([publish] docs = true in vergil.toml), the same condition under which cd-docs is wired into cd.yml.

docs.title: ci-package
docs.text: Build and install-test a repo's binary OS packages (.deb/.rpm) from its [package] section.

docs.title: Tiered matrix
docs.text:
ci-package.yml is called only by repos whose vergil.toml has a [package] section. Calling it without one fails the run. Its gate job surfaces as package / evidence under a caller job keyed package.

The matrix job picks a tier and passes it to vrg-package matrix --github-output --tier <tier>:

Event Tier Pull request from release/* of the same repository into main full Any other pull request, a fork's release/* head included reduced Any non-PR event (push, workflow_dispatch, …) full

A fork chooses its own branch names, so only a release/* head in the repository itself gets the full tier automatically.

The reduced tier keeps every build cell but runs only one install-test leg per format, so feature PRs get feedback sooner. For each format it picks from that format's shared (non-native) targets, or from its native ones if it has no shared target. It prefers amd64 (falling back to arm64) and takes the oldest release, compared numerically: the strictest compatibility case (lowest glibc, oldest rpm/dnf/systemd). The selection is done by vergil-tooling's vrg-package matrix (lib/package/matrix.py).

Release PRs always run the full tier, and the release evidence harvest reads the release PR's CI. A caller can override the automatic choice with the optional package-tier input (auto, full or reduced; default auto). Any other value fails the matrix job.

jobs:
  package:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-package.yml@v2.1
    with:
      package-tier: full  # optional; omit for auto

package / evidence runs in both tiers. It fails unless the matrix, build and install-test jobs all succeeded, and it records the tier that ran as metrics.tier in the ci-evidence-package artifact.

This needs a vergil-tooling release whose vrg-package matrix accepts --tier.

docs.title: Build runtime
docs.text: For builder = "python", vrg-package matrix resolves the vergil-python runtime once and records it as runtime on every build cell (vergil-tooling#3478). Each build / <cell> job passes it on as vrg-package build --cell <cell> --runtime <runtime>, as cd-release.yml's package-build does, so PR builds and release builds use the same runtime on every architecture. A cell without a runtime (a non-python builder) passes an empty --runtime, never null, which vrg-package build reads as none recorded. This needs vergil-tooling 2.1.262 or later at the caller's [dependencies].vergil pin; v2.1 resolves to it.

docs.title: Toolchain setup
docs.text:
Each build / <cell> and install-test / <cell> job runs inside the cell's package toolchain image (prod-pkg-ubuntu or prod-pkg-rhel, which the caller's vergil-tooling names, or their dev-pkg- variants with container-prefix: dev) and sets it up with package/setup. That action checks the image against its /etc/vergil/package-toolchain marker and installs vergil-tooling; it installs no toolchain itself, so a cell in a raw image fails at once. The prod-pkg-ubuntu image carries the apt mirror list (on amd64) and a fail-fast apt config (3 undelayed retries, 20-second timeouts, a 60-second dpkg lock wait) that every apt call in the job inherits.

Every package job sets timeout-minutes, in both ci-package.yml (matrix 5, build 30, install-test 15, evidence 5) and cd-release.yml (package-matrix 5, package-build 30, package-sign 15). A normal build takes about 45 seconds, so a stall fails the job in minutes rather than running to GitHub's 6-hour limit.

docs.title: Container prefix
docs.text:
vrg-package matrix names every cell's image ghcr.io/vergil-project/prod-pkg-<distro>:<version>. The optional container-prefix input (prod or dev; default prod, which an empty value also means) picks the image variant: with dev, the matrix job rewrites the prod-pkg- start of each image in its build and test outputs to dev-pkg-, so the build and install-test jobs run on the development package images. Nothing else in the outputs changes, and with prod they are passed on unchanged. Any other value, or a missing or malformed vrg-package matrix output, fails the matrix job. The job log lists the image each cell will use. The rewrite is the package/image-prefix action, which cd-release.yml runs on its package cells as well (binary packages). Each workflow reads its own input, so a caller can move its package CI to the dev- images without moving its release, or the other way round.

jobs:
  package:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-package.yml@v2.1
    with:
      container-prefix: dev  # optional; omit for prod

docs.title: ci-quality
docs.text: Code quality, linting and custom validation workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Every image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the primary version's resolved suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes an image.

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The lint and typecheck matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python), installs Python's dev dependencies with ci/toolchain/install-python (skipped with a notice on a repository with neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. The single-container common and custom jobs run on the resolver's image for the primary version (see Common checks and Custom validation). Callers are thin: they pass only language:, and optionally container-suffix: as a cross-check.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description common <caller> / common Runs common linters based on file presence (single-container job on the primary version — informational, gated through quality / evidence) custom <caller> / custom Runs the repo's custom validator with vrg-validate --check custom, or logs that there is none (single-container job on the primary version — informational, gated through quality / evidence) lint / <version> <caller> / lint / <version> Language-specific linting (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) typecheck / <version> <caller> / typecheck / <version> Language-specific type checking (matrix-expanded — informational, not a required check) build / <version> <caller> / build / <version> The release build, vrg-validate --check build, once on the primary version, only for a language whose BUILD check vergil-tooling turns on (see Release build — informational, gated through quality / evidence) evidence quality / evidence Aggregate gate — needs the common, custom, lint, typecheck and build jobs, runs if: always(), and asserts each of the first four succeeded and that build matches the BUILD flag; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Common checks
docs.text:
The common job runs inside a single container on the primary version — ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>, the image the primary lint and typecheck legs run on. The setup job resolves both parts with the shared setup action: <tag> is its primary-container-tag, and <suffix> is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix. For example clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, 3.14 gives prod-python:3.14 and a language-less repo's latest gives prod-base:latest. If the caller passes a container-suffix that differs from <suffix>, setup fails and common does not run.

The job conditionally executes each linter based on whether matching files exist in the repository:

Tool Condition markdownlint *.md files found shellcheck *.sh files or scripts/bin/ directory found yamllint *.yml or *.yaml files found hadolint Dockerfile* files found actionlint .github/workflows/ directory found

docs.title: Custom validation
docs.text:
The custom job runs the repository's custom validator (scripts/bin/validate-custom or vrg-validate-custom) in PR CI with vrg-validate --check custom, which runs the language install stage and then the custom stage. A repository with no custom validator gets one "no custom validator" line and a passing job; a validator that is present but not an executable regular file fails the job. Like common, it runs once, on the same image. For Python it pins uv to the primary version's interpreter (with ci/toolchain/pin-python) and installs the dev dependency group first (with ci/toolchain/install-python, which skips it on a repository not bootstrapped yet), so the validator sees the repo's dev dependencies; ci/toolchain/assert then checks the running toolchain is the primary version.

The job's transcript is uploaded as the ci-evidence-quality-reports-custom partial and bundled into ci-evidence-quality as quality-custom.log. The evidence job needs custom, so a failed or skipped custom stage fails quality / evidence — there is no separate required check (epic vergil-project/.github#488).

docs.title: Release build
docs.text:
The build job runs vrg-validate --check build, the language's build command, the same one the release job runs, so a build that would fail at release fails on the PR instead (epic vergil-project/.github#1174). It runs once, on the primary version's image, with the same checkout, setup, Python pin and assert-toolchain steps as a typecheck leg.

The job runs only when the matrix job's build-enabled output is true. That output is vrg-ci-resolve's build-enabled, passed on by the setup action: vergil-tooling decides which languages have a BUILD check, and no language list lives in this workflow, so turning BUILD on for a language needs no change here. A vergil-tooling release older than the flag gives false.

A skipped build job is a valid result, so the evidence job does not require it to succeed. It checks the result against the flag with ci/evidence/assert: skipped with BUILD off and successful with BUILD on pass, and anything else, a skipped build with BUILD on included, fails quality / evidence. The job uploads no report. There is no separate required check and no ruleset change.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  quality:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: Each of the five check jobs runs a vrg-validate check: common runs vrg-validate --check common, custom runs vrg-validate --check custom, each lint and typecheck leg runs vrg-validate --check lint or vrg-validate --check typecheck for the language, and build runs vrg-validate --check build. The lint, typecheck and build commands live in vergil-tooling, not in this workflow, so a language's checks change there.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
quality / evidence always carries the common and custom transcripts (quality-common.log and quality-custom.log), for every language. Each lint and typecheck leg stages its language's reports through ci/evidence/reports, whose lint and typecheck contracts name them, with the leg's version suffix:

Language Leg Report Tools python lint quality-ruff.json ruff python typecheck quality-mypy.xml mypy rust lint quality-clippy.json rustfmt, clippy rust typecheck quality-cargo-check.json cargo typescript lint quality-eslint.json prettier, eslint typescript typecheck quality-tsc.txt tsc

The reports are required. A leg that passes but leaves its report missing or empty fails its staging step. A leg that fails is not failed again for a missing report. Before it emits, the evidence job checks that every report of the language is there from at least one leg, and fails naming any that is not. The emitted artifact takes every quality-* file the jobs uploaded, and its tools are vrg-validate-common, vrg-validate-custom, then the language's lint and typecheck tools.

On a repository not bootstrapped yet (none of the language's manifests and no sources), vrg-validate skips the lint and typecheck gates, loudly. Each leg's staging step then prints a notice and stages a skip record, quality-<leg>-not-bootstrapped-<version>.json, in place of its report, and the evidence job accepts the skip records instead of the reports and lists none of a skipped leg's tools, keeping only vrg-validate-common and vrg-validate-custom when both legs were skipped. The step checks the skip strictly, and a leg that wrote no report without one fails as before: see Not-bootstrapped repositories.

A fleet language with no lint or typecheck contract yet (go, cpp) gets a warning on its legs and in the evidence job, stages no report and lists no lint or typecheck tools. A repository with no fleet primary language (a shell or Claude plugin repository, or one that passes no language) gets a notice instead. Either way the evidence carries the common and custom transcripts and their tools only.

docs.title: ci-security
docs.text: Security scanning workflow: CodeQL, Trivy and Semgrep, plus an evidence job that bundles their SARIF results for the release harvester.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Language for the security scanners (e.g., python, go, rust) run-security boolean no true Run the scanner jobs (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep) run-codeql boolean no true Run CodeQL analysis (disable for languages CodeQL does not support, such as shell) container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev) for the semgrep job's <prefix>-base:latest container run-standards boolean no false Deprecated — no longer has any effect. The standards job it controlled was removed; the input is still accepted so consumers that pass it do not error container-suffix string no — Deprecated — fed the removed standards job and no longer has any effect. Still accepted so consumers that pass it do not error

New callers should not pass run-standards or container-suffix.

docs.title: Required permissions
docs.text:
permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

GitHub validates the workflow's permissions: request against the calling job's effective permissions at startup, so a caller whose security: job carries an explicit permissions: block (the standard posture) must grant both there. The job block fully replaces any workflow-level block in the caller, so a workflow-level grant alone is not sufficient. A caller missing a grant fails with startup_failure and no registered checks.

The workflow no longer requests actions: read, which v2.1.3 added for SARIF uploads from private repositories (epic vergil-project/.github#1476 removed it). A caller that still grants it keeps working and can drop the grant.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
GitHub names each check <caller job> / <job>. With the caller job keyed security (the standard posture, as in the usage examples below):

Job Check name Condition codeql security / codeql run-security and run-codeql are both true trivy security / trivy run-security is true semgrep security / semgrep run-security is true evidence security / evidence trivy and semgrep succeeded, and codeql succeeded (run-codeql true) or was skipped (run-codeql false)

The evidence job downloads each scanner's SARIF partial and emits the consolidated ci-evidence-security artifact. Its evidence.json names the scanners whose SARIF it holds in tools: trivy and semgrep always, and codeql when the codeql job ran and passed. If any scanner fails, it does not run, so no security evidence is emitted. It is not a required check; see Required Checks for which of these checks branch protection requires.

Each scanner also uploads its SARIF to code scanning, and GitHub adds its own SARIF analysis checks (CodeQL, Trivy, Semgrep OSS); see Security Scanning.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    with:
      language: python

To skip CodeQL for languages it does not support:

jobs:
  security:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-security.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    with:
      language: shell
      run-codeql: false

docs.title: Implementation notes
docs.text:
• The semgrep job runs inside the ghcr.io/vergil-project/<container-prefix>-base:latest container (prod-base by default). Semgrep never executes the target code, so it needs no language runtime.
  • The codeql and trivy jobs run directly on ubuntu-24.04, with no container. CodeQL autobuild for compiled languages needs the language toolchains that the runner provides.
  • Each scanner job uploads its unfiltered SARIF as an evidence partial, beside the copy sent to code scanning. For Trivy and Semgrep, the copy sent to code scanning omits accepted-suppressed results (via vrg-sarif-filter); the evidence copy keeps them so they remain auditable.
  • The Semgrep action auto-detects repository content and enables additional rulesets: p/dockerfile when Dockerfiles are present, p/github-actions when workflow files exist under .github/workflows/. No configuration is needed from consuming repos. vrg-semgrep-scan resolves the language ruleset from the language input, p/c for cpp (which covers .c files only) and p/typescript for typescript.

docs.title: ci-test
docs.text: Unit test workflow.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. Each leg's image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must be one of the resolved suffixes (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or the matrix job fails. It never changes an image. container-prefix string no prod Image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Version matrix
docs.text: The matrix comes from vrg-ci-resolve at run time: the workflow's matrix job runs the shared setup action, which calls the resolver, and passes its versions, image tags and image suffixes to ci/matrix. Each leg pins uv to its version and to the image's interpreter (Python, with ci/toolchain/pin-python), installs Python's dev dependencies with ci/toolchain/install-python (skipped with a notice on a repository with neither pyproject.toml nor uv.lock) and then asserts the running toolchain with ci/toolchain/assert. Callers are thin: they pass only language: and container-suffix:.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Condition unit / <version> <caller> / unit / <version> Matrix-expanded per version — informational, not a required check evidence test / evidence Aggregate gate — needs every unit leg, runs if: always(), and asserts each leg succeeded; a failed/skipped leg makes it fail red rather than skip. This stable, version-agnostic gate is the required check (see Required Checks)

docs.title: Evidence reports
docs.text: Each unit leg stages the language's test reports for the ci-evidence-test artifact: coverage.xml and junit.xml, for Python, Rust and TypeScript alike. The names come from ci/evidence/reports. A leg whose tests passed but wrote no report fails, unless the repository is not bootstrapped yet and vrg-validate skipped the gate: the leg then prints a notice and stages a skip record, test-not-bootstrapped-<version>.json, in place of its reports, and the evidence lists no test tools, since none ran (see Not-bootstrapped repositories). A language with no test report contract yet (Go, C++) gets a warning and stages nothing, and the release-time evidence gate decides.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  test:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-test.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python
      container-suffix: python

docs.title: System packages
docs.text:
Each unit job installs the system packages the repository declares under [container].system-packages in its vergil.toml, via the shared/setup/system-packages action. This runs on test jobs only — lint and typecheck jobs do not exercise the code and are deliberately excluded, so the packages are installed exactly where the tests need them and nowhere else.

The install is a no-op when a repository declares no system packages. When it does declare them, the step installs with a bounded retry (to absorb transient apt mirror flakes) and fails closed if a declared package has no install candidate — the offending package and platform are named in the log and the test job fails rather than running against a missing dependency. See the action reference for the full behavior, and the container-config reference on the vergil-tooling side for the [container].system-packages key itself.

docs.title: Build command
docs.text:
After the system-packages install, each unit job runs the command the repository declares under [container].build-command in its vergil.toml, via the shared/setup/build-command action. Like the system-packages install, this runs on test jobs only — lint and typecheck jobs do not exercise the code and are deliberately excluded — and it runs after the packages are installed, before the tests.

The step is a no-op when a repository declares no build command. When it does declare one, the step fails closed with no retry: an arbitrary build command that fails is a real failure, not a transient one, so — in deliberate contrast to the system-packages install's bounded retry — a non-zero exit fails the test job immediately rather than being retried and masking a genuine break.

After the command runs, the action exports NODE_PATH (the npm global root, from npm root -g) so subsequent test steps can resolve a node library the build baked out-of-workspace (e.g. npm install -g <lib>).

require-only caveat. NODE_PATH is honoured by CommonJS require resolution only; ESM import ignores it. A baked library consumed via import will not resolve through NODE_PATH — a documented Node limitation, not an action bug.

See the action reference for the full behavior, and the container-config reference on the vergil-tooling side for the [container].build-command key itself.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: Each unit leg runs the language's real test suite through vrg-validate --check test. The test commands live in vergil-tooling, not in this workflow. The leg then stages its reports through ci/evidence/reports (see Evidence reports), whose table is the one place this repository records a language's test report names. Giving a language without a contract yet (Go, C++) test evidence means adding its entry to that table alongside the vergil-tooling gate command that writes the reports; the workflow itself needs no change.

docs.title: ci-version-bump
docs.text:
Version divergence gate workflow.

The gate follows the consuming repo's configuration: the job reads release-model from vergil.toml and, when it is "none", passes without running the gate. Non-releasing repos need no caller wiring to stay green.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description language string yes — Primary language of the repository run-release boolean no true Deprecated — the gate follows release-model in vergil.toml. Passing false still suppresses the gate but emits a deprecation warning. Tracked for removal in #688 container-suffix string no "" Cross-check only. The image suffix comes from the resolver. A non-empty value must equal the primary version's resolved suffix (e.g. python, cpp-clang, base), or setup fails. It never changes the image.

docs.title: Image
docs.text: The version-bump job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-<suffix>:<tag>, the resolver's image for the primary version, as in ci-quality's common job: <tag> is the shared setup action's primary-container-tag, and <suffix> is the primary version's entry in its container-suffixes, picked by shared/setup/primary-suffix (clang-20 gives prod-cpp-clang:20, a language-less repo gives prod-base:latest).

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
Job Check name Condition setup <caller> / setup Always runs; resolves the image suffix and tag for version-bump, and fails if the caller's container-suffix disagrees with the resolved suffix version-bump <caller> / version-bump Always runs; the gate steps run only when release-model is not none

With the standard caller job key version (as in the usage example below), the required check is version / version-bump, for repositories whose release-model is not none.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
jobs:
  version:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ci-version-bump.yml@v2.1
    with:
      language: python

Repos that don't release (e.g., infrastructure or documentation repos) declare it in vergil.toml instead of passing run-release: false:

[project]
release-model = "none"

The version-bump job then passes without running the gate, and the tooling-derived required-check set omits it entirely.

docs.title: ops-agent-audit
docs.text:
The daily audit of agent merges (epic vergil-project/.github#1384). Every managed repository's ops.yml calls this workflow after its config job, as a job named agent-audit. It runs vrg-agent-audit --repo <calling repo> as the org automation App.

The audit checks every merge into develop and main since the repository's two markers, the branches vergil/agent-audit/develop and vergil/agent-audit/main, each holding the last merge commit it audited on its branch. It then moves each marker to where its audit reached. For each merge it checks:

  • that the merge or auto-merge actor is one it expects: the human, the user agent, or the automation App on PRs the App authored;
  • on a PR an agent opened or acted on, that a merge-review record or an approved exemption covers the merged head's change;
  • that nobody but the human merged into main.

It is a security-signal job. It files no issue, posts nothing and has no reporting job, since a security signal never goes to a public ops issue (epic vergil-project/.github#1494, spec §2.3). Its findings are its exit status and its run log, which hoshin reads by the job name agent-audit.

The audit never creates a marker. A repository gets both when vrg-github-repo-init creates or adopts it; a scheduled run that finds one missing reports a missing-marker finding and fails.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (<org>-automation) APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's automation GitHub App

Both live in the calling repository's automation environment, which the job declares (see The automation environment).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). The human and agent logins come from it. The audit fails when it is missing, or names no human or more than one

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description agent-audit <caller> / agent-audit From develop only: runs vrg-agent-audit --repo <calling repo> as the automation App

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The agent-audit job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest:

  1. Fails unless the run's ref is refs/heads/develop, before any token is minted: the token can move the audit markers, so it is only ever minted for a run of develop's code.
  2. Mints an App token scoped to the calling repository only.
  3. Checks out develop with its full history (fetch-depth: 0). The audit needs a full-history clone whose origin is the audited repository, and refuses a shallow one.
  4. Installs vergil-tooling.
  5. Runs vrg-agent-audit --repo "$REPO" with the App token as GH_TOKEN. The audit fetches what it reads, each merged PR's head from refs/pull/<n>/head and the markers, through the checkout's read-only GITHUB_TOKEN. Only its API calls, the marker moves among them, use the App token.

The exit codes are a contract:

Exit Meaning Job result 0 Every merge since the markers is clean Pass 1 At least one finding, a missing marker, or a read failure Fail 2 A usage error Fail

Each finding is one line of the log. A read failure is never treated as a pass.

docs.title: Token permissions
docs.text: Requested App permission Why contents: write Move the vergil/agent-audit/* marker refs (the "Agent audit markers" ruleset lets only the admin role and the automation App do so), and list the PRs of a commit pull-requests: read Read each merged PR, its reviews and its timeline issues: read Read the PR's timeline, and the task issue's comments that hold its merge-review record metadata: read Always included, stated so the token's whole permission set is explicit

docs.title: Concurrency and timeout
docs.text: The job runs in the per-repository concurrency group ${{ github.repository }}/agent-audit, with cancel-in-progress: false: two runs would audit from the same marker and race to move it. It is capped at 60 minutes, the life of the App token it moves the markers with.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout and the audit's own fetches. Every API call uses the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The job in a repository's ops.yml, after its github-config job. A caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit, which carries the App keys from its automation environment:

jobs:
  github-config:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-github-config.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    secrets: inherit

  agent-audit:
    needs: github-config
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-agent-audit.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets: inherit

GitHub's secrets: inherit passes secrets only within one organization. A caller in another org passes the two keys by name instead:

    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: ops-epic-rollup
docs.text:
Event-driven epic rollup. When an issue closes, it runs vrg-epic-rollup, which closes the issue's parent epic once every task in that epic is closed.

The rollup is a no-op unless the closed issue is a managed task whose parent is a finite epic (an epic-labelled issue that is not a standing ad-hoc epic), so the caller can run it on every issue close. Epics usually live in a different repository (the org's .github), which is why the workflow uses a GitHub App token rather than GITHUB_TOKEN.

ops-epic-sweep is the scheduled safety net for any close this workflow misses.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev) epic-repo string no .github Repository in the caller's org that holds the epics. The App token is scoped to it so the rollup can close the parent epic there

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's GitHub App APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's GitHub App

The App must be installed on the calling repository and on epic-repo, with issues: write.

Both live in the calling repository's automation environment. The epic-rollup and report jobs declare environment: automation and read them.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the vrg-epic-rollup step and to the report job's ops/report step, which stop when it is missing or invalid

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description epic-rollup <caller> / epic-rollup Runs vrg-epic-rollup for the closed issue report <caller> / report Always, after epic-rollup: reports its result as epic-rollup to the org's operations queue through ops/report

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The epic-rollup job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest:

  1. Mints an App token scoped to the calling repository and epic-repo, requesting only issues: write.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs vrg-whoami --mode with the App token and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, and fails unless it prints automation: vergil-tooling verifies that the token was minted by the App the variable names before any write.
  4. Runs vrg-epic-rollup --task "<owner>/<repo>#<issue number>" with the App token as GH_TOKEN.

The issue number comes from github.event.issue.number, so the caller must be triggered by an issues event.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Issue writes use the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
A caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit:

name: Epic Rollup

on:
  issues:
    types: [closed]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  epic-rollup:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-epic-rollup.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets: inherit

GitHub's secrets: inherit passes secrets only within one organization. A caller in another org passes the two keys by name instead:

    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: This repository's caller: epic-rollup
docs.text: .github/workflows/epic-rollup.yml in this repository is the vergil-project caller above: it runs on issues: closed and passes the App secrets to ops-epic-rollup.yml@v2.1. It is not a reusable workflow. Each managed repository carries the same thin caller, and all the logic (token, checkout, install, run) stays in ops-epic-rollup.

docs.title: ops-epic-sweep
docs.text:
Scheduled epic and task reconciliation. It runs vrg-epic-audit --close, which makes three passes over the whole org:

  • Drift close. Closes work that missed its event-driven close, for example when the ops-epic-rollup run failed, a secret was broken or two closes raced: epics whose tasks are all closed, and task issues whose PR has merged. It also reopens an epic that was closed while a child was still open.
  • Archive drain. Moves the closed children of every standing epic (ad-hoc, intake and planning) into per-quarter archive epics.
  • Orphan pass. Enforces "every issue belongs to an epic": it links body-only Parent: lines as native sub-issues, removes the retired triage, idea and research labels, and attaches every orphan to its home's intake epic.

So the sweep changes labels and sub-issue links, not only issue state. Each pass acts only on provable drift, so a run with nothing new to fix changes nothing.

The org's epic home calls it once a day; one run covers the whole org. The same caller's workflow_dispatch trigger is how the one-time migration for "every issue belongs to an epic" is run.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev) window-days string no "30" How many days back to look for merged PRs whose task issue is still open. Epic drift (all tasks closed) is not limited by the window

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's GitHub App APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's GitHub App

Both live in the calling repository's automation environment. The epic-sweep and report jobs declare environment: automation and read them.

The token is minted for every repository the App is installed on in the org, because the sweep closes, relabels, links and moves issues in the code repositories, and closes, drains and attaches under epics in .github. The token requests only issues: write (closing, reopening, commenting on, relabelling, creating and linking issues, and creating labels), pull-requests: read (the merged-PR search) and contents: read (each repository's vergil.toml). vrg-epic-audit --close makes no security-advisory call; the human or the user agent syncs advisory states with vrg-security-record sync.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the vrg-epic-audit --close step and to the report job's ops/report step, which stop when it is missing or invalid

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description epic-sweep <caller> / epic-sweep Runs vrg-epic-audit --close across the org report <caller> / report Always, after epic-sweep: reports its result as epic-sweep to the org's operations queue through ops/report

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The epic-sweep job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest:

  1. Mints an App token for the caller's org, with no repository restriction, scoped to issues: write, pull-requests: read and contents: read.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs vrg-whoami --mode with the App token and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, and fails unless it prints automation: vergil-tooling verifies that the token was minted by the App the variable names before any write.
  4. Runs vrg-epic-audit --close --window-days "$WINDOW_DAYS" with the App token as GH_TOKEN and VRG_EPIC_SWEEP=1.

vrg-epic-audit --close runs its passes in this order:

  1. Closes drifted tasks and rolled-up epics, and reopens any epic closed with an open child.
  2. Drains the ad-hoc epics, then the intake and planning epics, into per-quarter archives, and closes past archives.
  3. Runs the orphan pass: links body-only Parent: lines natively, strips the retired labels, then attaches orphans to intake.

The log prints a count line for each step, for example Retired kind labels stripped: 41 issue(s). and Orphans attached to intake: 50.

docs.title: When a run fails because a queue is full
docs.text:
An intake or planning epic holds at most 95 open children. When an epic is at that cap, the orphan pass stops before it adds anything past it. The step prints every issue it did not link and exits 1, so the run fails. A failed run can therefore mean the queue needs attention (run intake review, or work the planning queue), not only a broken token or an outage. The next run attaches the rest once the queue has room.

vrg-epic-audit --close is otherwise a human-only action: it refuses unless the identity resolves to human. VRG_EPIC_SWEEP=1 marks this scheduled run as the trusted automation that may close. An interactive agent session never sets it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Issue writes use the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
A caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit:

name: Epic Sweep

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  epic-sweep:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-epic-sweep.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets: inherit

GitHub's secrets: inherit passes secrets only within one organization. A caller in another org passes the two keys by name instead:

    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: ops-github-config
docs.text:
Nightly per-repository ops checks. Every managed repository's ops.yml calls this workflow on a schedule, and it runs four independent jobs:

  • branch-sweep deletes the calling repository's branches whose pull-request work is finished.
  • github-config keeps the calling repository in sync with its expected configuration with vrg-github-repo-config update, as the org automation App, and runs only from develop.
  • trusted-authors-check checks the org's trusted-authors Actions variables with vrg-trusted-authors check, as the org automation App, and uploads the values it read as the trusted-authors-values artifact. It runs only in the org's own .github repository (<org>/.github) and is skipped in every other calling repository.
  • dependabot-audit fails when the calling repository has any open Dependabot alert, at any severity.

The jobs do not depend on each other, so one failing does not stop the others. Each one mints its own GitHub App token from the org's automation App (see APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY). Every token is scoped to the calling repository only, except trusted-authors-check's, which reads every repository of the org and holds read-only permissions only.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Secret Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID yes Client ID of the org's automation GitHub App (<org>-automation) APP_PRIVATE_KEY yes Private key of the org's automation GitHub App

Both live in the calling repository's automation environment. Every job declares environment: automation and reads them: branch-sweep, github-config, trusted-authors-check, dependabot-audit and report-branch-sweep.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description VRG_AUTOMATION_APP yes Org-level Actions variable holding the automation App's slug (<org>-automation), visible to the calling repository (see step 10 of the App setup). The github-config and trusted-authors-check jobs fail when it is empty VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS yes Org-level Actions variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the branch-sweep job's ops/github-config/branch-sweep step, the github-config job's update step, the dependabot-audit job's audit step and the report-branch-sweep job's ops/report step, which stop when it is missing or invalid. The trusted-authors-check step needs none (see trusted-authors-check)

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text:
Job Check name Description branch-sweep <caller> / branch-sweep Deletes finished branches via ops/github-config/branch-sweep github-config <caller> / github-config From develop only: runs vrg-github-repo-config update --repo <calling repo> as the automation App trusted-authors-check <caller> / trusted-authors-check In <org>/.github only (skipped elsewhere): runs vrg-trusted-authors check --org <calling repo's owner> as the automation App and uploads the trusted-authors-values artifact dependabot-audit <caller> / dependabot-audit Runs vrg-dependabot-audit --repo <calling repo> report-branch-sweep <caller> / report-branch-sweep Always, after branch-sweep: reports its result as branch-sweep to the org's operations queue through ops/report

github-config, trusted-authors-check and dependabot-audit get no reporting job: their failures are security signals, which never go to a public ops issue (epic vergil-project/.github#1494, spec §2.3).

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Every job runs in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<prefix>-base:latest and follows the same pattern:

  1. Mints an App token with actions/create-github-app-token. Each job passes explicit permission-* inputs, so its token carries only the permissions that job needs. No job but trusted-authors-check passes an owner or repositories input, so each other token is scoped to the calling repository alone.
  2. Checks out the repository and installs vergil-tooling.
  3. Runs its command with the App token as GH_TOKEN.

branch-sweep and dependabot-audit check the token before they use it: a step between the install and the command runs vrg-whoami --mode with the App token and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, and fails unless it prints automation. vergil-tooling then verifies that the token was minted by the App the variable names, and an empty variable fails the step too. github-config and trusted-authors-check set VRG_AUTOMATION_APP on their command's step instead, whose command makes the same check (below). actions/ops/report/tests/app-identity.test.sh guards the order.

github-config is the exception: its first step, before any token is minted, fails the job unless the ref is refs/heads/develop and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP is set, and its checkout pins ref: develop (see github-config).

docs.title: Token permissions per job
docs.text:
Job Requested App permissions Why branch-sweep contents: write, pull-requests: read Delete a branch ref, and read pull requests to decide which branches are finished github-config administration: write, contents: write, pull-requests: write, workflows: write, actions: read, metadata: read update reads and converges repository settings, branch protection, rulesets (GitHub returns a ruleset's bypass_actors only to a caller that can edit it), Actions permissions and whether vulnerability alerts are enabled (Administration). It pushes the sync branch, and GitHub returns a repository's merge settings only to a token with Contents read and write (see Get a repository) (Contents). It opens the sync PR, closes an earlier one and turns on auto-merge (Pull requests), and a sync PR can change files under .github/workflows/ (Workflows). It reads the automation environment and its deployment branch policies, which GitHub serves only to a token with Actions read (Actions). It makes no Issues call. Minted only after the job has checked that it runs from develop and that VRG_AUTOMATION_APP is set trusted-authors-check organization-actions-variables: read, actions-variables: read, metadata: read (organization and repository Variables: Read), for the org's whole installation (owner: ${{ github.repository_owner }}) Read the org variables and every repository's variables. actions/create-github-app-token declares no input for either Variables permission, but it turns every permission-* input into a token permission; .github/actionlint.yaml ignores exactly these two inputs dependabot-audit vulnerability-alerts: read only (Dependabot alerts: Read) List the repository's open Dependabot alerts

The org's automation App holds more than any one job requests, Administration write included (see App permissions). Without the permission-* inputs a minted token would carry all of it, so every job asks only for its own set (see Token scoping).

GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do this work. This workflow requests only contents: read for it, and a called workflow can never hold more than its caller's ops.yml grants (the standard ops.yml grants contents: read and issues: write). Neither can delete a branch or read Dependabot alerts.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: Each job runs in its own per-repository concurrency group, ${{ github.repository }}/<job> (for example vergil-project/vergil-tooling/github-config), with cancel-in-progress: false. A new run of a job waits for a running one of the same job in the same repository and neither is cancelled, so a scheduled run and a manual dispatch never overlap. The jobs stay independent of each other.

docs.title: Git credentials
docs.text:
The github-config job runs gh auth setup-git with the App token as GH_TOKEN before the tool runs. git then gets its HTTPS credentials from gh, so any git clone or git push vergil-tooling makes authenticates as the App with this job's scoped token, not with the checkout's GITHUB_TOKEN.

It then sets git's global user.name to <app-slug>[bot], from the token step's app-slug output, and user.email to <id>+<app-slug>[bot]@users.noreply.github.com, with <id> the bot user's ID from gh api /users/<app-slug>[bot]. This follows the pattern in actions/create-github-app-token's README, so sync commits show as the automation App.

docs.title: branch-sweep
docs.text: The scheduled safety net behind the delete-on-merge repository setting and the delete-on-close rule. It lives in this workflow so that every repository whose ops.yml already calls it is swept with no consumer change. See ops/github-config/branch-sweep for what is deleted, the job summary and the failure handling.

docs.title: github-config
docs.text:
The automatic fleet sync (epic vergil-project/.github#1064). The job runs vrg-github-repo-config update --repo "${{ github.repository }}" as the org automation App. It converges the repository's GitHub settings and rulesets, then checks the managed files committed on develop, in a fresh clone. When any has drifted from its released master copy, it opens one sync PR on an automation/repo-config-sync/<run-id> branch with auto-merge on, and the PR merges itself once its required checks pass. What update cannot fix is left for a human and named in the PR body and the log. For the exit codes and what each step does, see vergil-tooling's vrg-github-repo-config update reference.

Automation identity. The update step sets VRG_AUTOMATION_APP from the org-level Actions variable of the same name, next to the App token in GH_TOKEN. vergil-tooling then resolves the automation identity mode, and checks that GH_TOKEN was minted by that App before it does any automation work. The identity is used only for this mechanized work, never for anything an AI agent does. The variable says the process holds the App's token, so it is set only on that step, never on the job: a vergil-tooling command that sees it without the token, such as the setup action's vrg-whoami check, fails. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs actions/ops/github-config/tests/automation-env.test.sh, which holds every workflow to this. A step that sets VRG_AUTOMATION_APP must carry the App's identity in exactly one of two forms:

  • The token form: GH_TOKEN from an earlier token step of its job (${{ steps.<id>.outputs.token }}), as this job's update step does.
  • The credential form: no GH_TOKEN, and VRG_AUTOMATION_CLIENT_ID and VRG_AUTOMATION_PRIVATE_KEY both from ${{ secrets.<name> }}. This is for a tool that mints its own repo-scoped token, as vrg-upstream-refresh publish does in ops-upstream-refresh.

Any other shape fails the check, and so does a step that has both forms at once.

Develop only. This job holds the workflow's only Administration write token, so no other branch's code may ever run with it. Its first step, before any token is minted, fails the job unless the run's ref is refs/heads/develop, and it checks out develop explicitly. The same step fails the job when VRG_AUTOMATION_APP is empty. Every fleet repository's default branch is develop, so scheduled runs pass the check. A workflow_dispatch from any other branch fails.

Time limit. The job sets timeout-minutes: 60. The automation App's installation token has a fixed one-hour life, and update's wait for its sync PR to merge ends within it, so a run that takes longer could not use its token anyway. Without the cap GitHub's default of 360 minutes would apply, and a run hung outside the tool's own deadline would hold the job's concurrency group for up to six hours. A run that comes close to the limit is a cue to look at the job's performance.

docs.title: trusted-authors-check
docs.text:
The daily check of the trusted-authors Actions copies (epic vergil-project/.github#1467). The org variables VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP are derived from the human's host configuration and published by the human with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). The job runs vrg-trusted-authors check --org "${{ github.repository_owner }}" --values-out trusted-authors-values.json, which flags a missing or invalid org variable, one not visible to every repository, and any repository-level variable of either name, since that would override the org copy in its repository's jobs.

Automation identity. The check step sets VRG_AUTOMATION_APP next to the App token in GH_TOKEN, as github-config's update step does, so vergil-tooling verifies that the token was minted by the automation App. check refuses the agent identity modes. With --org it reads no trusted-authors configuration, so this step, unlike the workflow's other vrg-* steps (see Variables), needs no VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS. The smoke-setup-vergil workflow runs actions/ops/github-config/tests/trusted-authors-check.test.sh, which holds the job to where it runs, its identity, its token's scope and permissions, and the upload.

The exit codes:

Exit Meaning Job result 0 The variables are clean Pass 1 At least one finding, printed as a FINDING: line Fail 2 The check could not run, for example a failed read or an empty VRG_AUTOMATION_APP Fail

The values artifact. On success and on failure (if: always()), the job uploads the --values-out file as the artifact trusted-authors-values: {"<org>": {"<name>": "<value>"}}, the values the check read, logins and slugs only. hoshin start compares it with the values the host configuration implies, so drift between the source and the published copy is caught. When the check could not run it writes no file, and the upload step fails too.

Where it runs. The check covers the whole org, so one run a night is enough. The job runs only in the org's own .github repository: its condition is if: github.repository == format('{0}/.github', github.repository_owner), which names that repository from the calling repository's owner, so it holds for any org. In every other repository whose ops.yml calls this workflow, the job is skipped. That one run's artifact is the org's single latest configuration-audit result, and a finding turns only the .github repository's nightly run red.

docs.title: dependabot-audit
docs.text:
The fleet runs Dependabot report-only (epic vergil-project/.github#420): alerts are on, Dependabot never opens a pull request, and this job turns any open alert into a red nightly run. It runs vrg-dependabot-audit --repo "${{ github.repository }}". Dismissing an alert on GitHub is the only way to clear it.

The exit codes are a contract:

Exit Meaning Job result 0 No open alerts Pass 1 At least one open alert, at any severity Fail 2 The alerts could not be read: alerts disabled, the token lacks Dependabot alerts: Read, no App installation, or an unknown repository Fail

"Could not check" (exit 2) is never treated as a pass. A common cause is an App permission change that has not yet been accepted on the org's installation: until it is, minted tokens do not carry the new permission. See Changing a permission later.

The log carries counts by severity and a link to the Security tab only, so a world-readable log never names a vulnerable package.

For the command's full reference, see vergil-tooling's Dependabot Alert Audit.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Scope Level Reason contents read Checkout. Every other operation uses the App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The standard ops.yml, as generated by vergil-tooling's vrg-github-repo-init (which staggers the cron minute per repository) for a repository in vergil-project:

name: Ops

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '45 1 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  github-config:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-github-config.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    # `inherit` within vergil-project: it carries the App keys from the
    # `automation` environment and any signing or registry secrets the
    # callee declares. Allowed only for the App-key workflows (vrg-validate's
    # secrets-inherit check).
    secrets: inherit

GitHub passes secrets: inherit only to a reusable workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise, so for a repository in any other org vrg-github-repo-init passes the two keys by name instead:

    # By name, not inherit: GitHub passes `secrets: inherit` only to a
    # reusable workflow in the caller's own organization or enterprise.
    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

docs.title: ops-upstream-refresh
docs.text:
Scheduled upstream refresh. It runs vrg-upstream-refresh, which runs the calling repository's [upstream-refresh].hook from vergil.toml on a fresh clone of develop, and turns the result into at most one pull request that merges itself:

  • No change. The run reports "in sync" and exits 0. If an earlier run's refresh PR is still open, it is closed and its branch deleted.
  • A change. The change is checked against the repository's path fence, committed as the automation App's bot user, and pushed to a new branch, automation/upstream-refresh/<run-id>. The PR, titled chore(upstream): refresh upstream inputs, lists the changed files and the hook's notes, and has auto-merge on. The run waits until the PR has merged, then exits 0. An earlier run's open refresh PR is closed first.

No human merges a refresh PR: the job merges it, as the org automation App, once the PR's CI passes. A run is green only when the PR merged or there was nothing to change. This carries out the policy decided in vergil-project/.github#470 (epic vergil-project/.github#1168).

An upstream refresh is separate from a dependency update: vrg-upstream-refresh never runs the [dependency-update] hook, and vrg-update-deps never runs the [upstream-refresh] hook. For the hook contract, the path fence and the [upstream-refresh].paths allowlist, see vergil-tooling's upstream-refresh reference. A repository with no paths refuses every patch, so every run with a change fails until it declares them.

Each consumer calls it from its own ops.yml on its own schedule.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Required Default Description container-prefix string no prod Container image name prefix (prod or dev)

docs.title: Secrets and variables
docs.text:
Name Kind Required Description APP_CLIENT_ID secret yes Client ID of the org's automation App APP_PRIVATE_KEY secret yes Private key of the org's automation App VRG_AUTOMATION_APP Actions variable yes Org-level variable holding the automation App's slug (<org>-automation), visible to the calling repository (see step 10 of the App setup). Both jobs fail when it is empty VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS Actions variable yes Org-level variable holding the trusted-authors configuration, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). Passed to the vrg-upstream-refresh prepare and vrg-upstream-refresh publish steps and to the report job's ops/report step, which stop when it is missing or invalid

Keep both secrets in the calling repository's automation environment and pass them by name or with secrets: inherit. The workflow declares them optional, because prepare holds no keys and declares no environment: GitHub checks a required secret for every job of a called workflow, and one that exists only in an environment does not count for a job that declares none, so declaring them required makes GitHub refuse the whole call before prepare starts. Only publish and report declare environment: automation and read them, and each fails first, naming each missing secret, when either is empty. Nothing falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN.

The secrets reach only the publish job's last step and the report job. vrg-upstream-refresh publish mints its own installation tokens from them, limited to the calling repository with contents: write (push the PR branch, delete an earlier run's), pull-requests: write (open, merge and close refresh PRs), workflows: write (the wait's branch update, below) and metadata: read. See Token scoping.

docs.title: Jobs and check names
docs.text: Job Check name Description prepare <caller> / prepare Runs the hook through vrg-upstream-refresh prepare, with no secrets, and uploads the patch publish <caller> / publish Runs vrg-upstream-refresh publish on that patch: fence, PR, and the wait until it merges report <caller> / report Always, after both: reports their combined result as upstream-refresh to the org's operations queue through ops/report, so a failed prepare that skips publish reports a failure

docs.title: The key boundary
docs.text:
The App's private key never shares a runner with the work: the hook and anything it installs or loads. Steps in one job share a runner's filesystem, so code in an earlier step could rewrite the tool, its packages, or a git hook or config that a later step holding the key then runs. So the workflow runs as two jobs, each on a fresh runner:

  • prepare runs the hook with no secrets and a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN, and hands on data only: a patch and its notes, as an artifact. vrg-upstream-refresh prepare refuses to run if the App's credentials are in its environment.
  • publish runs only the trusted platform: the runner, the released container image and released vergil-tooling. It treats the artifact as data: it never runs it, never runs the hook, and never runs git in a tree prepare touched. It applies the patch in its own fresh clone of develop, on the exact commit prepare ran against, and reads the path fence's rules from that clone's develop tip, never from the artifact.

A third job, report, reports the run to the org's operations queue. It never runs the hook and downloads no artifact; it gets the App's credentials only as the ops/report action's inputs, from which the action mints an issues-only token on report's own runner, and in the env of the shell-only step before it, Require the automation App keys, which fails when either is empty.

actions/ops/upstream-refresh/tests/key-boundary.test.sh, run by the smoke-setup-vergil workflow, holds the workflow to this layout: the secrets only on publish's last step, as the inputs of report's ops-report step and in the env of report's require step, a check of both before each use, no secret and a read-only token on prepare, the guard first in prepare and publish, no if: but report's if: always(), and both time limits.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
Both jobs run in ghcr.io/vergil-project/<container-prefix>-base:latest (prod-base by default). The workflow is in the concurrency group <owner>/<repo>/upstream-refresh: a new run waits for a running one, neither is cancelled, and one run's prepare and publish never interleave with another run's.

prepare (permissions: contents: read, timeout-minutes: 30):

  1. Guard. Fails the job unless the run's ref is refs/heads/develop and VRG_AUTOMATION_APP is set. It is a failing step, not a job-level if:, so a run from another ref shows up red instead of being skipped.
  2. Checks out develop, with persist-credentials: false, only to install the tooling.
  3. Installs vergil-tooling at the caller's [dependencies].vergil ref.
  4. Runs vrg-upstream-refresh prepare, with the read-only GITHUB_TOKEN as GH_TOKEN and VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS in its env. It clones develop, runs the hook there, and writes the hook's tracked changes as a binary patch, the develop commit it ran on, the changed paths and the hook's notes.
  5. Uploads that output as the upstream-refresh-prepare artifact.

publish (needs: prepare, permissions: contents: read, timeout-minutes: 140):

  1. Guard, the same as prepare's, in depth: no App token is minted from any other ref.
  2. Checks out develop and installs vergil-tooling, as in prepare, on this job's own runner.
  3. Downloads the upstream-refresh-prepare artifact.
  4. Runs vrg-upstream-refresh publish on it, with VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, VRG_AUTOMATION_CLIENT_ID, VRG_AUTOMATION_PRIVATE_KEY and VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS set on this step only. The step first fails, naming each missing secret, when either credential is empty, then runs the tool in its place. The tool removes the credentials from its environment at startup, so no git or gh it starts sees them. It checks every minted token against VRG_AUTOMATION_APP, applies and fences the patch, and opens the PR and waits until it merges.

When prepare finds nothing to change, publish still runs: it closes an earlier run's open refresh PR and reports "in sync".

The token and the wait. The tool renews its token once it is older than 30 minutes, revokes each token it replaces, and revokes the last one when it exits, on SIGINT and SIGTERM included. Every git and gh call takes the current token, so a wait longer than one token's hour keeps working: a vergil-containers refresh, whose CI takes 32 to 40 minutes, renews at least once. If develop has moved since prepare, the wait updates the PR's branch from develop and CI decides; that merge needs Workflows write whenever develop has changed a workflow file. The path fence refuses any patch that touches .github/**, so no patch can use it. The wait's deadline is 120 minutes from the tool's own start. publish's timeout-minutes: 140 is that deadline, plus 15 minutes for the steps before the tool, plus a 5-minute margin, so the tool always ends, revokes its token and logs how the wait ended before GitHub kills the job. Only a hard kill skips the last revocation (see Token scoping).

Exit codes of vrg-upstream-refresh publish, which decide the job's result:

Exit Meaning 0 Merged, or nothing to change 2 The PR was opened but did not merge: the log names the PR and the reason (a failed check, a conflict, a closed PR, the branch-update cap or the deadline) 1 Any other failure, with the reason: the hook, a clone, the path fence, the base check, a refused identity, a failed mint or revocation 130 or 143 Interrupted by SIGINT or SIGTERM, such as a cancel, after revoking its token

A run with a non-zero exit shows as a red scheduled run, and the publish log alone says what happened: the PR it closed, the PR it opened or "in sync", each token renewal and revocation, and how the wait ended.

vrg-upstream-refresh refuses the agent identity modes (user and audit), because it opens and merges PRs. Under GitHub Actions, publish refuses to run unless it was given the App's credentials and resolves to the automation identity.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Job Scope Level Reason prepare contents read The checkout, and the clone of develop the hook runs in. Prepare writes nothing to GitHub publish contents read The checkout. Every write uses the token the tool mints, not GITHUB_TOKEN

A called workflow cannot exceed its caller's grant. The caller's contents: read covers both jobs. The artifact passes between them within the run, which needs no GITHUB_TOKEN permission.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
A caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit:

name: Ops

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 1 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  upstream-refresh:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/ops-upstream-refresh.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
    secrets: inherit

GitHub's secrets: inherit passes secrets only within one organization. A caller in another org passes the two keys by name instead:

    secrets:
      APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_CLIENT_ID }}
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

Schedule it on the default branch, develop: both jobs fail from any other ref.

docs.title: publish-index
docs.text: publish-index.yml is called from an <org>/packages repository. Its build-index job runs vrg-package index --config packages.toml --keys keys --out _site, which verifies, retains, indexes and signs the product releases. Its deploy job then publishes the site with the Actions-based Pages deploy. Last, it checks that Pages serves the index this run built (below). The workflow takes no inputs. Runs are serialized by the publish-index concurrency group. Unlike the other reusable workflows, it runs directly on ubuntu-24.04 rather than in a vergil container image.

docs.title: Attestation verification
docs.text: Before indexing, vrg-package index verifies every downloaded .deb and .rpm with gh attestation verify, pinned to the signer workflow vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/cd-release.yml and the source ref refs/heads/main. An asset whose build provenance was not attested by cd-release.yml running on a product's main branch fails the index build. Each .rpm's org signature is checked as well.

docs.title: Post-deploy live check
docs.text: GitHub Pages can report a deployment success while it goes on serving the previous deployment (vergil-project/packages#46). So build-index records the sha256 of every signed InRelease and repomd.xml it built. After the deploy, deploy fetches each of those files from the deployment's page_url, with a cache-busting query string, until all of them match. If they still do not match after about five minutes, the job fails with an ::error:: that names the run and shows what was served. Re-run the workflow; if the fault repeats, raise it with GitHub Support. See publish/index/live-check.

docs.title: Caller requirements
docs.text:
• Pages source set to "GitHub Actions". The deploy job publishes with actions/deploy-pages, so the caller repository's Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source must be GitHub Actions, not "Deploy from a branch".
  • An index-signing environment (below).
  • secrets: inherit and the job permissions shown in the example.
  • The org Actions variable VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS, published with vrg-trusted-authors publish (see VRG_TRUSTED_AUTHORS). The workflow passes it to the build-index job's Build, verify and sign the index step and to the report job's ops/report step, which stop when it is missing or invalid.

The workflow also declares APP_CLIENT_ID and APP_PRIVATE_KEY, the org automation App's credentials, as optional secrets. Its last job, report, runs always, after build-index and deploy, and reports their combined result as publish-index to the org's operations queue (epic vergil-project/.github#1494) through ops/report, which mints its token from them. A caller passing secrets: inherit already passes them. The report job declares environment: automation and reads them; build-index and deploy declare other environments (below).

docs.title: Token identity
docs.text:
Unlike the other unattended jobs (epic vergil-project/.github#1494, spec §5.4), build-index and deploy do not use the App token:

  • deploy publishes with actions/deploy-pages, which uses the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (pages: write) and the run's OIDC token (id-token: write). The job runs in the github-pages environment its deployment is made to, and a job declares only one environment, so it cannot read the App's keys, which live only in the automation environment. This is a recorded identity exception.
  • build-index uses its read-only GITHUB_TOKEN to download releases and verify their attestations. It writes nothing with a token, and it runs in the index-signing environment, so it cannot read the App's keys either.

actions/ops/report/tests/app-identity.test.sh holds both to this.

docs.title: Signing environment and caller example
docs.text:
The signing key comes from the caller repository's index-signing environment, which must admit only develop and hold PACKAGE_SIGNING_KEY and PACKAGE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE. The <org>/packages caller in vergil-project passes secrets: inherit, which carries them, and the App keys, to the reusable workflow (see cd-release: binary packages). Signed packages outside vergil-project are tracked by vergil-project/.github#1592. The caller must also grant the scopes the jobs request:

jobs:
  publish-index:
    uses: vergil-project/vergil-actions/.github/workflows/publish-index.yml@v2.1
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    secrets: inherit
